title: Archive then republish resets first_published_at, rewriting the journal date and order
content: archive_document() deletes the live row, and the next go-live inserts a fresh row with `first_published_at default now()` (`20260925120000_content_versions_and_publishing.sql:77,147-150`). The public journal shows `first_published_at` as the post's date and sorts newest first (`src/lib/journal.ts:84-85`). The column is named 'first', but it is only 'first since the last archive'. Hiding a post with `visible = false` keeps the date, and archiving does not.
quote: delete from public.published_documents where collection = p_collection and doc_id = p_doc_id;
failure_scenario: A post first published 2026-01-05 is archived on 2026-09-30 to fix a paragraph. The owner then publishes the corrected version. The journal now shows it dated 2026-09-30 and sorted first, above posts actually written after it, and its original date is lost. The audit trail holds only 'content.archive' and 'content.publish' with no date to restore from.
fix: Keep the first publication date across an archive. For example, store it in an `archived_at` or `first_published_at` memo that content_go_live reuses (`coalesce` from the prior value), or archive by flagging the row and excluding archived rows in the anon policy instead of deleting it. If a new date on republish is the intent, rename the column and label it in the admin so it is not misread.

title: The advisory locks behind the last-owner guard and the version sequence have no concurrency test
content: The last-owner guarantee rests on `pg_advisory_xact_lock` in a deferred constraint trigger, and its comment (lines 52-56) makes a specific claim about READ COMMITTED snapshots. Version-conflict safety rests on the twin lock in `content_versions_next_seq`. The only tests are sequential: `staff-admin.test.ts:123` demotes one owner, and `publish.test.ts:212-227` re-inserts an old seq. `Promise.all` appears in tests/integration only in checkout.test.ts. Deleting either lock line leaves the whole suite green.
failure_scenario: A later refactor drops the lock line (it looks like dead weight, because the constraint trigger already 'checks'). Two owners are demoted at nearly the same moment, for example two staff-admin set_role calls. Each deferred check runs before the other has committed, sees the other still an owner, and passes. Both commit, leaving zero active owners. Nobody can invite, step up or change roles, and only out-of-band SQL can recover. Likewise, two editors saving seq N+1 of one document at once would both insert without the next_seq lock and fork the history.
fix: Add an integration test with two pg connections. Open two transactions, demote owner A in one and owner B in the other, commit both together, and assert exactly one fails with 23514 and one active owner remains. Add a second test that fires two `content_versions` inserts with the same seq via Promise.all and expects exactly one 23505.

title: S01.2 fix: a failed scheduled publish silently loses its schedule, and nothing in the product shows it
content: publish_due() now isolates each due row in a subtransaction. The handler clears `publish_at` and writes a `content.publish_due_failed` audit row, and the code comment says this is so 'the owner can see it'. No admin screen reads audit_events: grep of `src/` for `audit_events` and `publish_due_failed` returns nothing, and COVERAGE C23 records that no screen shows the trail. The owner home shows only a count of scheduled documents (`AdminHome.tsx:144-152`). Neither `schedule_version` nor the browser `scheduleDocument` (`admin-publish.ts:109-118`, Zod plus media check only) tests the post-slug unique index, so the collision is only found at due time, in the cron job. `when others` also swallows transient errors (deadlock_detected, lock_not_available) and permanently drops the schedule for them, with no retry.
failure_scenario: An editor schedules post B (slug 'my-essay') for tomorrow 09:00 while live post A already uses slug 'my-essay'. schedule_version succeeds and the UI shows «مجدول». At 09:00 content_go_live raises 23505, the handler nulls publish_at and inserts an audit row, and post B never goes live. The scheduled badge just disappears. No screen, email or notice tells anyone, so the post stays unpublished until someone notices. A deadlock between the cron run and a manual publish of the same document has the same silent effect.
fix: Check the slug collision inside schedule_version for posts and raise unique_violation with the constraint name, so the UI shows the existing slug message at schedule time. Make the failure visible: show the latest `content.publish_due_failed` rows on the owner home, or keep a `schedule_error` on the version and show it in CollectionList. Consider retrying once for transient sqlstates (40P01, 55P03) instead of dropping the schedule.

title: S01.1 fix stops at posts: items hidden with «إخفاء» in rooms and scenes stay publicly readable, with their library images
content: The S01.1 fix makes anon RLS honour the D20 'visible' flag for posts only. The admin has a second hide control, the per-item `hidden: true` flag on hideable lists (`src/admin/collections/scenes.ts:20`, `rooms.ts:59,68,98,126,157-159`; UI label «إخفاء» in `FieldInput.tsx:717`). It is enforced only at build time by `dropHidden` (`src/lib/content.ts:146,248`). Every collection except posts is fully readable by anon, and `media_published_ids()` (same file, line 79: `where p.collection <> 'posts' or p.data -> 'visible' = 'true'::jsonb`) walks every UUID string in those documents without looking at `hidden`. So a hidden scene photo or room gallery photo keeps its `media` row readable by anon (`grant select (id, derivatives)`), and its WebP sits in the public `media-public` bucket. AUDIT-1 G4.2 already concluded for the child-featuring films that 'a hidden flag in the content is not enough' (`scripts/prepare-media.mjs:159`). The same reasoning applies to library images hidden through the admin, and nothing in the admin warns that hiding is not privacy.
failure_scenario: The owner uploads a photo of a person (say, a child pending guardian consent) to the library. She adds it to the scenes gallery, ticks «إخفاء», and publishes; the page no longer shows it. Anyone with the publishable key (it ships in the static export) runs `GET /rest/v1/published_documents?collection=eq.scenes&select=data`. The response includes the hidden item with its image UUID. `GET /rest/v1/media?id=eq.<uuid>&select=id,derivatives` also answers, because media_published_ids() counts the UUID. The derivative is then fetched from the public bucket. The photo she believed was withdrawn is retrievable.
fix: Enforce hiding in the database. Strip `hidden: true` items from lists in the copy written to published_documents (a small recursive jsonb helper called from content_go_live). The draft in content_versions keeps them, and the anon policy, media_published_ids() and media_is_published() then see only visible items. Check the admin readers of published_documents (SettingsView.tsx:55, CollectionForm.tsx:100) first. Alternative: expose a stripped view to anon and drop anon's direct select on the table. Either way, add a test in audit-fixes.test.ts like the S01.1 one for a hidden scenes item.

title: media_usage lists every published document twice: as live and as draft
content: The second branch of media_usage counts the latest version of every document as a draft. It does not exclude a latest version that is already the live one. When a document was published and not edited since (latest seq = published seq), it returns a 'live' row from the first branch and a 'draft' row from this branch. UNION does not merge them, because the state column differs. media_where_used passes both rows through. MediaLibrary.tsx:595-599 keys rows by collection-doc_id-state, so both render. docs/media-rights.md:79-80 promises one link per document with its state. The delete guard is unaffected, because either row blocks the delete. The defect is the misleading list. The integration test tests/integration/media-security.test.ts:325-327 uses toContainEqual, so it passes while the duplicate exists. AUDIT-1 did not report this.
quote: select v.collection, v.doc_id, case when v.publish_at is not null then 'scheduled' else 'draft' end
failure_scenario: The owner publishes a room or post that uses image X and does not edit it afterwards, so the latest version equals the live version. In the library, selecting X calls media_where_used(X). It returns (posts, <id>, 'live') and (posts, <id>, 'draft'). The panel «مستخدمة في» shows the same document twice, once with «منشورة» and once with «مسودة». The owner concludes an unpublished draft exists that does not. Every unedited published document shows twice.
fix: Add a forward migration with `create or replace function public.media_usage(uuid)` (same signature, grants kept). In the version branch, skip a non-scheduled latest version that is already live: `and not (v.publish_at is null and exists (select 1 from public.published_documents p where p.collection = v.collection and p.doc_id = v.doc_id and p.seq = v.seq))`. Change the integration test to assert the exact row set, so [liveDoc,'draft'] must be absent.

title: Media metadata edits and bulk folder moves leave no audit event; only create and delete are audited
content: media_complete writes 'media.create' and media_delete writes 'media.delete' to audit_events. Editors can also rewrite name, folder, alt_ar, caption and rights directly through the Data API under the column grant here. media_rename_folder moves every image in a folder in one call. Neither path writes an audit_events row, and no trigger is attached to public.media. The catalog tables get an update audit trigger (products_audit, coupons_audit and others via catalog_audit, migration 20260927160000:232-243). audit_events is the owner's only trail (owner-read, append-only). The `rights` column is the record of who owns an image and what permits publishing it, so silent edits to it matter.
quote: grant update (name, folder, alt_ar, caption, rights) on public.media to authenticated;
failure_scenario: An editor changes `rights` on a published image from the photographer's licence note to another text, or renames the folder that holds fifty images. The owner opens the audit list and finds nothing for either change. Nobody can tell who changed the rights statement, or when.
fix: Add a forward migration with an after-update trigger on public.media that writes 'media.update' to audit_events (actor auth.uid(), entity_id id, summary listing which of name, folder, alt_ar, caption and rights changed, no values for rights or caption). Skip rows where nothing changed, so media_touch stays quiet. Let the same trigger cover media_rename_folder.

title: The exactly-once claim invariant is tested only sequentially; operations denial of media_where_used and media_rename_folder is untested
content: The header (lines 13-15) makes the exactly-once ticket claim the core guarantee. The tests in tests/integration/media-security.test.ts:133-139 and 141-149 call media_claim twice one after the other. The second call sees claimed_at set and gets 55000 even if `for update` is removed from media_claim or media_complete. No test runs two claims in parallel (no Promise.all against media_claim, or two sessions with a held lock), so the race guard is unprotected. Also, media_where_used (role check at line 153) and media_rename_folder (RLS only) are granted to every authenticated user. No test calls either as an 'operations' or inactive staff member. The 'operations sees nothing' test at line 259 covers only direct table reads.
quote: select * into t from public.media_upload_tickets where id = p_ticket for update;
failure_scenario: A refactor drops `for update` from media_claim. Two concurrent media-complete requests for one ticket both read claimed_at null and both proceed to write the public derivatives. The failing request's cleanupAll then deletes the winner's `m/<id>/*.webp` objects, which is exactly what the header says can never happen. The suite stays green. Likewise, removing the role check in media_where_used lets an operations member list document ids and states, with no failing test.
fix: Add an integration test that fires two `media_claim` calls for one ticket with Promise.all on separate connections and asserts exactly one succeeds and the other gets 55000. Add tests where an operations user gets 42501 from media_where_used, and where media_rename_folder returns 0 and leaves the rows unchanged.

title: Notices held back by the quota gate stay 'due' for the outbox kick, so empty per-minute runs hide the owner-home mail-waiting warning
content: outbox_claim holds rows back with a local quota gate. The gate here is `o.priority < 2 or v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - p_reserve`, plus the daily and monthly caps. The effective version is audit_fixes.sql:373-375, where S04.1 changed it to `o.priority = 0 or ...`. A held row stays status 'pending' with next_at <= now(). `finance.outbox_due_since()` (20260927150000_outbox_due_since.sql:19-27) knows nothing about the quota or reserve gate. It returns non-null, so `outbox_kick` POSTs to the `outbox` function every minute. `runOutbox` (supabase/functions/_shared/outbox.ts:148-188) claims nothing, then still calls `job_run_record` with status 'ok' and claimed 0. `AdminHome.emailWaiting` (src/components/admin/AdminHome.tsx:92-98) warns only when no run finished in the last 10 minutes, and that empty run finishes every minute, so it never warns. The I35 header (outbox_due_since.sql:1-10) says one stuck row must not record a run every minute and that mail waiting must be signalled. This reintroduces the first for quota holds and defeats the second. ISSUES I35 says quota-delayed mail is handled by S04.2, but S04.2 only covers a Resend 429 (next_at moved to midnight). It does not cover the local gate in outbox_claim.
quote:
and (o.priority < 2 or v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - p_reserve)
      and v_sent_today < p_daily_quota
      and v_sent_month < p_monthly_quota
failure_scenario: 81 outbox sends are already recorded for the UTC day. At 10:00 a visitor's contact notice (priority 1) is queued. outbox_claim refuses it, because 81 is not below 100 - 20 = 80 (audit_fixes.sql:373). Until 00:00 UTC, pg_cron kicks the Edge Function every minute. That is about 840 invocations and 840 empty job_runs 'ok' rows. Each run makes the owner-home job line look healthy with a fresh finished_at, and emailWaiting() returns false. The visitor's message sits unsent for up to 14 hours and the owner is told nothing. Once the monthly cap (3000) is reached, the same happens for the rest of the month, roughly 1,440 empty runs a day.
fix: In a new forward migration, make `finance.outbox_due_since()` apply the same gates as outbox_claim: the priority/reserve gate, the daily cap and the monthly cap. Alternatively, when the gate refuses a row, park it (set next_at to the next UTC midnight or month start), as the QUOTA path does. Then let the owner home warn on quota-held mail instead of counting an empty run as a heartbeat.

title: Contact intake cap (200/day, one notice per recipient) exceeds the notice drain cap (80/day), so a Turnstile-passing flood backlogs the queue FIFO and delays real messages for days
content: contact_submit admits up to 200 messages a day (`contact:all`) and queues one priority-1 outbox row per active owner or operations member (lines 207-212). Priority-1 rows are drained only while v_sent_today < DAILY_QUOTA - RESERVE = 100 - 20 = 80. That gate is in this file's outbox_claim at line 291 and in audit_fixes.sql:373 after S04.1. Priority-0 receipts share the same budget. Claims are strictly FIFO (`order by o.priority, o.next_at, o.id`). Intake therefore exceeds drain by at least 120 notices a day with one recipient, and by 320 a day with two. The backlog grows without bound while the flood continues, and a real visitor's notice queues behind it. docs/operations.md:80-89 accepts the flood only as a form lockout and states 'nothing is lost — messages already stored still reach the owner's mailbox'. That reasoning ignores the queue backlog, and the owner-home warning is also silenced (see the previous comment).
quote: or not finance.rate_limit_take('contact:all', repeat('0', 64), 200, interval '1 day')
failure_scenario: An attacker who solves Turnstile 200 times a day, across 40 or more IPs at 5 per hour each and distinct emails at 3 per hour each, sustains the flood. With one active owner, the queue grows by 120 pending notices a day. On day 3 a genuine visitor writes to Anas. Their notice waits behind about 240 spam notices at 80 a day, so it arrives about 3 days late, and the delay keeps growing while the attack lasts. Anas's mailbox also receives 80 spam notices a day, and the owner home shows no warning. The docs claim the opposite.
fix: Make the intake cap consistent with the drain cap. Either add a per-day notice count to the contact throttle, so intake x recipients <= DAILY_QUOTA - RESERVE (for example about 40 messages a day with two recipients), or serve contact notices per sender fairly instead of FIFO. Correct the 'nothing is delayed' wording in docs/operations.md:80-89. This has to be a new migration, because this one is applied history.

title: A scheduled post that fails to publish (slug already live) silently loses its schedule; nothing the owner can open shows why
content: AUDIT-1 S01.2 fixed publish_due so one failing document no longer stops the others. The fix drops the schedule and writes a 'content.publish_due_failed' audit row, and its comment says this is "so the owner can see it". No screen reads audit_events. grep of src/ and supabase/functions/ finds no reader, and PLANS/COVERAGE.md C23 records that no admin screen shows the audit trail. schedule_version (same file, line 188) never checks post-slug uniqueness, and the browser's validateVersion in src/lib/admin-publish.ts checks only the Zod schema and media ids. So the one condition that makes publish_due fail (the published_documents_post_slug unique index) is accepted at schedule time and then fails silently at due time. A publish-now gets the clear message «معرّف المقال مستخدم في مقال منشور آخر؛ غيّره ثم انشر.», but the schedule path gets nothing.
failure_scenario: Post A is live with slug 'launch'. The owner drafts post B with slug 'launch' and schedules it for 09:00. schedule_version succeeds and the UI shows «مجدول في ...». At 09:00 publish_due calls content_go_live, which raises 23505. The handler sets publish_at = null and writes the audit row. B never appears, the list shows B as an ordinary draft with no schedule, and the «المحتوى المجدول» count on the owner home drops by one. The only trace is an audit_events row that only the Supabase Studio SQL editor can display.
fix: Refuse at schedule time: in schedule_version, for collection 'posts', raise unique_violation if another published post already uses the same slug. The UI already maps 23505 to the slug message. Also surface the failure, for example by counting content.publish_due_failed rows from the last 7 days on the owner home.
note: orchestrator: kept; DB-core-2 (same defect) was refuted on AUDIT-1 intent

title: Four every-minute pg_cron jobs and no purge of cron.job_run_details
content: The repo schedules four every-minute jobs: content-publish-due (20260925120000:299), site-build-trigger (this line), email-outbox (line 253) and checkout-expire (20260927160000:1093). pg_cron logs every run into cron.job_run_details and never purges it. That is about 5,760 rows a day, roughly 2.1 million a year, each carrying the command text and status. The repo purges finance.job_runs (job-runs-purge, S17.1) and contacts, but grep finds no job_run_details cleanup anywhere in migrations, docs or scripts.
failure_scenario: After a year of uptime cron.job_run_details holds about 2 million rows of pure noise, on the order of 0.5 GB. On a small hosted plan (the free tier is 500 MB) that eats the database quota. It also slows every look at the cron history, and the small runid index grows with it.
fix: Add one daily job in a new migration: select cron.schedule('cron-run-details-purge', '17 3 * * *', $$delete from cron.job_run_details where end_time < now() - interval '7 days'$$);

title: Sign-in email declares RTL only on <html>, and the code paragraph flips to the left edge
content:
dir="rtl" is set only on the element, and the three

elements carry no direction. Gmail web and the Gmail app discard the attributes of and , so there the Arabic paragraphs get an LTR base direction: they are left-aligned and the trailing ':' and '.' land on the wrong end of the sentence. Independently of the client, the code paragraph sets direction: ltr, so its text-align: start resolves to the left. Even where is honoured, the code sits at the left edge under right-aligned Arabic lines. Digits are Latin and the {{ .Token }} isolate is correct.
failure_scenario: Anas requests a sign-in code and opens the email in Gmail. The sentence «رمز الدخول إلى لوحة أنس:» is left-aligned with the colon at the wrong end, and «صالح لعشر دقائق. إن لم تطلبه، تجاهل هذه الرسالة.» renders the same way. In clients that do honour html dir, the code is left-aligned while the text above and below is right-aligned.
fix:
Wrap the body content in
and give the code

style="direction:ltr; text-align:right; unicode-bidi:isolate" (keep the Latin digits as they are).

title: outbox_due_since counts quota-blocked rows as due, so cron calls the function every minute, records 'ok', and hides the stall from the owner home
content: finance.outbox_due_since() (the predicate behind outbox_kick, the every-minute email-outbox cron in 20260927090000:253) treats any pending row with next_at <= now() as due. outbox_claim applies extra gates that the predicate ignores. Since AUDIT-1 S04.1 those gates are: priority > 0 rows need v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - p_reserve, and every row needs v_sent_today < quota and v_sent_month < monthly quota. Contact notices are priority 1 (20260926120000:207). Once 80 sends are recorded for the UTC day, those rows stay due but are never claimable. Each minute the kick posts to the outbox function, runOutbox claims nothing, and job_run_record writes an 'ok' run with claimed = 0. AdminHome.emailWaiting then sees a run that finished under 10 minutes ago and stays quiet, and outbox_attention lists only exhausted, uncertain and suppressed rows, not pending ones.
quote: where o.status = 'pending' and o.next_at <= now() and o.attempts < o.max_attempts),
failure_scenario: A contact-form flood queues notices. After 80 sends in a UTC day, 5 more priority-1 notices sit pending. From then until 00:00 UTC, pg_cron makes about 1,000 pointless Edge Function calls and job_runs inserts. The owner home says «سليم» for إرسال البريد because a run finished a minute ago, so the owner is not told that the notices are delayed up to 24 hours (up to a month if the monthly cap is hit).
fix: Make finance.outbox_due_since() apply the same gate as outbox_claim (compute v_sent_today and v_sent_month there and drop priority and quota-blocked rows). Alternatively, when runOutbox claims 0 while due rows exist, record 'skipped' with a QUOTA_WAIT reason and let the owner home warn on it.

title: A missing pages_deploy_hook makes publishing look successful while the site is never rebuilt, and the owner home cannot tell
content: When Vault has no 'pages_deploy_hook', site_build_trigger returns false every minute and writes no finance.job_runs row. The local stack needs this no-op, but a hosted project that forgot or mistyped the Vault name behaves identically. The owner home then shows «بناء الموقع: لم يعمل بعد», the same text as on a fresh install with nothing published. The email path does not share this blind spot. There a missing Vault value leaves due rows, and emailWaiting warns «تأكد من الجدولة». The admin tells editors a change "shows within minutes" (ARCHITECTURE Publishing D32).
quote: select decrypted_secret into v_hook from vault.decrypted_secrets where name = 'pages_deploy_hook';
failure_scenario: On the hosted project the owner sets functions_url and jobs_secret but the hook is missing or misnamed. He publishes a post and sees the success message. Every cron run returns false silently, finance.site_builds.requested_at stays newer than triggered_at forever, and the public site never changes. Nothing in the UI, the job list or the audit trail flags it.
fix: When a request is owed (requested_at is not null and triggered_at is null or older than requested_at) and the hook is missing, insert one finance.job_runs row ('site_build', 'skipped', {"reason":"NO_HOOK"}), only if the latest site_build run is not already that. The owner home already labels 'skipped' as «متجاوز».

title: Approval pins the DB's published seq, but buyers read the static page built earlier, so acceptance can bind to text they were not shown
content: commerce_policies_approve records the seqs currently in published_documents into commerce_settings.policy_revisions. The policy text a buyer reads, however, is the static /policies/[slug] page, rendered at build time (src/app/(public)/policies/[slug]/page.tsx; the page shows no seq). The cart takes its consent value from checkout_quote, i.e. the live DB value: CheckoutForm.tsx sends `policyRevisions: quote.policyRevisions`. checkout_create only compares that echoed value with the same DB row, so POLICY_CHANGED cannot detect a page that is older than the approval. Nothing in the approval (or the checkout) checks that a build containing the approved seqs has been deployed. The build is asynchronous (site_build_trigger coalesces to 2 minutes, then the Pages build runs) and, by design (src/lib/store.ts header), a build that fails leaves the last good deployment live indefinitely. The X1.1 guarantee ("what a buyer reads and accepts is what the owner approved") therefore does not hold after any policy change. X2.4 (recorded) covers a different gap: which seq the owner reviewed at click time. Checkout is still off and E08 is open, so this is a design gap to close before P08, not a live exposure.
quote: select seq into v_store from public.published_documents where collection = 'policies' and doc_id = 'store';
failure_scenario: Editor publishes store policy seq 4 (a changed refund window). The trigger resets the approval. Owner approves seconds later, and policy_revisions becomes {store:4,...}. The Pages build for seq 4 has not finished, or it failed on an unrelated malformed catalog row and the last good deploy stays live. A buyer opens /cart, ticks consent and reads /policies/store, which still shows seq 3. The quote returns {store:4}, checkout_create sees an exact match, and the order snapshot records that the buyer accepted revision 4, which they never saw. The refund window they accepted is not the one on their screen.
fix: Bind consent to the displayed text. Have the build embed the seq of every policy it rendered, in the policy pages and the checkout page. Make CheckoutForm send those build-time seqs as policyRevisions instead of quote.policyRevisions. checkout_create already refuses a mismatch with POLICY_CHANGED, which then means 'reload, the page is stale'. Optionally show 'نسخة N' on each policy page.
note: orchestrator: latent until P08 opens checkout; P08 prerequisite

title: Stale-version conflict raises 40001, which AUDIT-1 records as unanswered by PostgREST, and the 409 path is only tested with mocks or a direct pg connection
content: AUDIT-1's own fix X2.3 (20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:160-166) switched publish_version/schedule_version from a stale-tab error to unique_violation because, as its comment states, "PostgREST does not answer a 40001 at all: the call hangs". commerce_settings_save here, and commerce_policies_approve (20260927170000_policy_approval.sql:37-40, same `using errcode = 'serialization_failure'`), still raise 40001. The `admin` Edge Function reaches both through the same path: serviceRpc() calls serviceClient().rpc(), which is supabase-js to PostgREST (supabase/functions/_shared/db.ts), and admin.ts:370 and :389 then expect error.code === '40001'. No test exercises that mapping over PostgREST. tests/unit/admin-function.test.ts:315 and :383 throw a fabricated error with code 40001. tests/integration/commerce-settings.test.ts:144-168 and policy-approval.test.ts:135-151 call the SQL over a direct pg connection. So either the AUDIT-1 comment is wrong, or the owner's two stale-version conflicts never produce the documented 409 «تغيّرت الإعدادات من جلسة أخرى. أعد تحميل الصفحة.». I could not run the stack here (read-only), so I am reporting the contradiction and the missing real-path test, not a measured hang. The write itself is still refused either way, because the raise aborts the transaction.
quote: raise exception 'Commerce settings changed in another session.'
failure_scenario: Owner has /admin/settings open in two tabs. Tab A saves the seller name (version 3 to 4). Tab B, still holding version 3, completes the TOTP step-up and submits. commerce_settings_save raises 40001. If PostgREST behaves as the audit_fixes comment says, the Edge Function's rpc() call never returns an error, so the admin function times out or answers 500. The form shows no reload message, and the owner cannot tell whether the save happened.
fix: Pick one and prove it with a test through the real Data API (not pg and not mocks). If 40001 is answered, correct the audit_fixes comment. If it is not, raise a code PostgREST maps to a 4xx, as publish_version does with unique_violation (23505, mapped to 409), in both commerce_settings_save and commerce_policies_approve, and map that code in admin.ts:370 and :389.
note: orchestrator: hasql-transaction retries 40001 without bound; X2.3 siblings missed

title: Retention purge hard-codes its child tables and, like contacts_purge, leaves no run record, so P08's payment tables would stop it silently
content: buyer_retention_purge deletes from exactly three child tables (order_items, inventory_reservations, coupon_redemptions) and then `delete from finance.orders`. Any table with a non-cascading FK to finance.orders makes the whole function fail with 23503 every night, and nothing shows it. The customers step, the audit row (written only when something was deleted) and the return value are all skipped, and nothing in the app or in finance.job_runs records the failure. The job is a bare cron.schedule (line 53). finance.contacts_purge (20260927140000_privacy_requests.sql:229) is the same: no job_runs row and no audit row at all. Neither job is in AdminHome's KNOWN_JOBS. PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:37 already plans payment_attempts with an order FK for P08, and an abandoned gateway visit leaves an initiated attempt on an order that later expires. This is the exact status the purge targets. The 90-day period is a promise the privacy text must state (privacy-data-map.md), and a silent failure breaks it without any signal.
quote: delete from finance.orders where id = any (v_orders);
failure_scenario: P08 adds finance.payment_attempts(order_id uuid references finance.orders). A buyer opens the payment page, abandons it, and the hold expires, so the order is 'expired' and has an 'initiated' attempt. 90 days later buyer_retention_purge reaches the `delete from finance.orders` statement for that order and raises foreign_key_violation. The transaction rolls back, so no order and no customer is deleted, and no audit row is written. It repeats every night. The owner home shows nothing, and buyer names, emails, phones and addresses stay past the promised 90 days.
fix: Have both purge jobs write a finance.job_runs row (ok or failed, with counts), for example by adding a job_run_record call inside an exception block, and list them in AdminHome KNOWN_JOBS. Add a test that fails if any FK into finance.orders is not covered by the purge (query pg_constraint against the function's table list), or give the P08 tables ON DELETE CASCADE and record that requirement in the P08 brief.

title: Stock-only variant saves from the admin still request a site rebuild, contrary to the stated design and the test
content: The header comment (lines 94-96) says a stock change does not request a rebuild, and tests/integration/checkout.test.ts:941 asserts it. The trigger is a statement-level `after ... update of <columns>` trigger. In Postgres, `update of` fires when a listed column appears in the UPDATE's SET list, whether or not its value changed. It also fires when the statement matches 0 rows. The only writer of variants is the admin form. `TableForm.save()` sends `config.toRow(values)`, and variants.ts `toRow` always includes sku, title, fulfillment, price_halalas, enabled and sort_order alongside stock. So every variant save calls `catalog_request_build()`, whether the owner edited only stock, edited nothing, or lost a version conflict. The passing test issues `update ... set stock = 9` alone, which the admin never does.
quote: after insert or delete or update of product_id, sku, title, fulfillment, price_halalas, enabled, sort_order
failure_scenario: The owner corrects a signed edition's stock from 10 to 9 in the admin variant form. The client runs `update product_variants set sku=..., title=..., price_halalas=..., enabled=..., stock=9, ...`. The `update of price_halalas` trigger fires. `site_build_request()` sets requested_at, and within 2 minutes `site_build_trigger()` POSTs the Cloudflare Pages deploy hook and starts a full static rebuild. Nothing public changed. Repeated stock edits, or saves that end in a stale-version conflict with 0 rows, each burn a Pages build, and the build quota is finite. The integration test stays green because it never updates the way the admin does.
fix: In a forward migration, drop the update statement trigger. Keep the insert/delete statement trigger. Add a row-level `after update on public.product_variants for each row when ((old.product_id, old.sku, old.title, old.fulfillment, old.price_halalas, old.enabled, old.sort_order) is distinct from (new.product_id, new.sku, new.title, new.fulfillment, new.price_halalas, new.enabled, new.sort_order)) execute function public.catalog_request_build()`. Change the test to update every admin-sent column with an unchanged price and a new stock, and expect no build request.

title: A coupon can make the order total 0, and checkout_create creates a pending order nothing can pay
content: `coupons.percent_bp` allows 10000 (100%). The admin coupon form allows max 10000 bp. A fixed coupon has no upper bound relative to the cart, only `least(amount, eligible)`. `orders.total_halalas` is only checked as `= subtotal - discount + shipping`, so 0 passes. A digital-only cart has no shipping. A physical cart to a city with `fee_halalas = 0` (allowed by the 0..1000000 check) has none either. `checkout_price` returns ok:true with total 0, and `checkout_create` inserts a `pending_payment` order with total 0, a 20-minute stock hold and an active coupon redemption. The payment design (DATA-AND-SECURITY 'Checkout transaction' steps 4-7) creates an invoice for the expected full amount and has no zero-total or free-order path, and P08 will inherit this state. No refusal code exists for it, and the Edge REFUSALS map has no entry.
failure_scenario: The owner creates a coupon FREE100 (percent, 10000 bp), or a fixed coupon of 100000 SAR. A buyer with a digital-only cart applies it. The quote shows total 0, checkout_create returns 201 with an order and accessToken, and the email and session are then blocked by ACTIVE_HOLD for 20 minutes. Stock, if any, is held. The order can never be paid or completed and expires unpaid. Once P08 exists, the invoice step gets amount 0. Until then the buyer is told the order is pending payment.
fix: Decide the rule in checkout_price. Either refuse `v_total < 1` with a new error code (for example TOTAL_TOO_LOW, added to REFUSALS in supabase/functions/_shared/checkout.ts with an Arabic message), or record a deliberate free-order state that P08 completes without a gateway. Add `check (total_halalas >= 1)` on finance.orders if refused. Add an integration test with a 100% coupon.

title: The SQL cart-validation and money-bound branches have no database-level test
content: tests/integration/checkout.test.ts covers the coupon math, holds, idempotency, throttle, concurrency and expiry. The refusal branches in `finance.checkout_price` that guard malformed or oversized input appear only in tests/unit/checkout.test.ts, which feeds fake rpc replies through the Edge mapping and never executes this SQL. Untested here are CART_TOO_LARGE (line 593, the guard that keeps `subtotal_halalas::integer` from overflowing), TOO_MANY_LINES (512), INVALID_LINE (519-526), INVALID_QUANTITY (532), DUPLICATE_LINE (536) and INVALID_DEDICATION (556). Also untested is the expired-token branch of `checkout_cancel` (line 1038). Nothing in the repo runs those branches against Postgres.
failure_scenario: A later edit to checkout_price (for example, moving the cart-size check after the coupon step) removes or mis-orders the 500,000 SAR guard. A 50-line cart of 10,000,000-halala items then reaches `(v_price ->> 'subtotal')::integer` in checkout_create and raises 22003 numeric_value_out_of_range. The Edge Function turns that into a generic 500 instead of CART_TOO_LARGE 422. An expired-token cancel could likewise start succeeding after a refactor. The whole suite still passes, because the unit tests only check the status-code mapping.
fix: Add integration tests that call checkout_quote and checkout_create with: 51 lines; a duplicate variant; quantity 0, 21 and '5' (string); a 201-character dedication; and a cart over 50,000,000 halalas. Assert the exact codes. Add a cancel test that sets access_token_expires_at to the past and expects NOT_FOUND.

title: X1.1 fix leaves a window where buyers accept a policy revision whose text they were never shown
content: policies_reset_approval clears the approval when an approved policy gets a new seq. That closes checkout only until the owner re-approves. The forced workflow is publish, then approve within seconds. The buyer reads the policy on a static page, `/policies/<slug>`, which shows only the text and no revision number. That page is rebuilt from `published_documents` only after `site_build_request` and the two-minute `site_build_trigger`, then a Pages build. The consent revisions come live from `commerce_settings` through `checkout_quote` and `checkout_create`. Nothing compares the two. `commerce_policies_approve` and `checkout_create` do not check whether a deployment containing the new text is live, and CheckoutForm only links to the static pages. AUDIT-1 stated the goal as "what a buyer reads and accepts is what the owner approved". The fix meets it only after the rebuild completes. If the Pages build fails, the last good deployment stays live, so the mismatch has no end. Checkout is off until P08, so this is latent today.
failure_scenario: 12:00:00 an editor publishes the store policy as seq 4, so the trigger clears the approval and checkout closes. 12:00:20 the owner approves, so policy_revisions becomes {store:4, delivery:.., refund:..} and checkout opens. The static `/policies/store` page still renders seq 3 until the rebuild deploys, several minutes later or never if the build fails. At 12:02 a buyer opens the linked page, reads seq 3, and ticks consent. The quote carries {store:4}, checkout_create sees equal revisions, and the order snapshot records acceptance of revision 4, text the buyer never saw.
fix: Tie approval to what is actually deployed. Embed the published policy seqs into the built `/checkout` page at build time. Have CheckoutForm disable consent and checkout, showing a «السياسات قيد التحديث» message, whenever `quote.policyRevisions` differs from the built seqs. Alternatively, record the deployed policy seqs in `finance.site_builds` from a post-deploy hook and make `commerce_policies_approve` and `checkout_create` refuse until they match the published seqs. Document the residual in docs/operations.md.

title: RECIPIENT_INACTIVE rows are counted and offered for replay in the admin, yet can never be cleared or replayed
content: The S03.5 sweep marks a notice for an inactive recipient `exhausted` with last_error RECIPIENT_INACTIVE. `outbox_attention` returns every exhausted row (line 516). AdminHome.tsx `replayableCount` counts every exhausted or uncertain row as "needs attention". EmailView.tsx shows the «إعادة الإرسال» button for every exhausted row. `outbox_replay` always refuses these rows with 22023, because the recipient is inactive (lines 545-553). Rows are removed only by the contacts retention purge, about 90 days after the contact's sent notice, or by `privacy_erase_staff`. AdminHome.tsx:64-67 states the design rule that the count must be something the owner can bring back to zero, and this fix breaks it.
failure_scenario: The owner demotes operations member Sara to editor while 3 contact notices addressed to her are pending, for example held by the daily reserve. The next outbox_claim exhausts the 3 rows with RECIPIENT_INACTIVE. The owner home shows «مشكلات تحتاج انتباهًا: 3» and البريد lists them under «تحتاج تدخل». Each «إعادة الإرسال» click fails with «المستلم لم يعد عضوًا نشطًا…». The number stays at 3 until the contacts purge runs, about 90 days later, so a real email problem is drowned out.
fix: Do not surface these rows as actionable. Simplest: in `outbox_attention`, exclude `o.last_error = 'RECIPIENT_INACTIVE'`. Alternatively delete the swept rows, as privacy_erase_staff does for unsent notices, or make the UI treat that last_error as «انتهت» (ended) in `replayableCount` and in EmailView's REPLAYABLE_STATUSES check.

title: A QUOTA give-back keeps first_attempt_at, so a long quota wait turns the next ambiguous send into a manual replay
content: The S04.2 branch gives the attempt back and re-queues the row as pending, but leaves `first_attempt_at` set by the refused request. The 23-hour idempotency window is measured from that column: the claim's uncertain rule at line 371, and `replay_needs_confirmation` at line 514. A 429 quota refusal is a definite non-send, so the provider never started a window for this key. After a wait of a day or more, and especially the monthly quota, which is probed once a day, `first_attempt_at` is already older than 23 hours on the first real attempt.
failure_scenario: Resend's monthly quota is exhausted, and a notice is claimed on day 1 with first_attempt_at = day 1 10:00. It answers 429 QUOTA and goes back to pending with attempts 0. This repeats daily for 20 days. After the reset, attempt 1 times out, or the dispatcher throws DISPATCH_FAILED, and the outcome is 'uncertain'. The row is now 'uncertain' with first_attempt_at 20 days old. The claim requires first_attempt_at > now() - 23h, so it is never retried, and outbox_due_since ignores it. The owner must open البريد and confirm a duplicate risk that does not exist, since no attempt was ever accepted.
fix: In the QUOTA branch, when `o.attempts = 1` (no earlier attempt could have reached the provider), also set `first_attempt_at = null` so the window starts at the first real attempt. Keep it when attempts > 1. Extend the QUOTA tests in outbox.test.ts with a multi-day wait followed by an 'uncertain' outcome.

title: A JSON `null` body crashes staff-admin with an unhandled TypeError instead of BAD_JSON
content: The body is parsed with a bare `JSON.parse(text)` and then dereferenced at `switch (body.action)` (line 69). Only the parse sits inside the try/catch. `admin.ts:148` guards the same case explicitly (`typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)`), but staff-admin does not. `JSON.parse('null')` returns null, so `body.action` throws a TypeError outside any try. Deno.serve then answers a plain-text 500 that does not follow the `{ok:false,error:{code,message}}` contract from `_shared/http.ts`. Only an active owner with a fresh TOTP can reach this, so the blast radius is small.
failure_scenario: An owner-authenticated client (or a script holding an owner token) POSTs the body `null`. Auth passes, `JSON.parse('null')` gives `null`, and `body.action` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. The reply is Deno's default 500 with no JSON body. `TeamView.callStaffAdmin` cannot read an `error` object from it and shows the generic 'تعذّر الاتصال بالخادم.', where BAD_JSON was intended.
fix: Reuse the shape guard from admin.ts. After `body = JSON.parse(text)`, throw when `typeof body !== 'object' || body === null || Array.isArray(body)` so the existing catch answers 400 BAD_JSON.

title: Settings status reports analytics as configured when fetchAnalytics treats it as NOT_CONFIGURED
content: `settingsStatus().analytics` is true when `ANALYTICS_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` are set. `fetchAnalytics` (analytics.ts:216-227) also needs `SITE_URL` to parse as a URL with a non-empty host, and otherwise returns `{status:'unavailable', reason:'NOT_CONFIGURED'}`. The owner's Settings screen (SettingsView.tsx:174) prints «الإحصاءات: مضبوط» while the stats page shows the feature as not configured. The status action exists to answer whether a feature is configured, and here it gives a wrong yes.
failure_scenario: The hosted project sets ANALYTICS_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID, but SITE_URL is typed without a scheme (`anas.studio`) or is missing. `new URL('anas.studio')` throws, so `siteHost` is '' and the Settings line reads «الموقع: غير مضبوط». The next line still reads «الإحصاءات: مضبوط», while /admin/stats shows analytics unavailable (NOT_CONFIGURED). The owner is told the setup is complete when it is not.
fix: Compute `analytics` with the same gate as fetchAnalytics: `optionalEnv('ANALYTICS_TOKEN') !== undefined && optionalEnv('CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID') !== undefined && siteHost !== ''`.

title: A transient Storage read error is reported as MISSING_PART and triggers cleanup of parts that were uploaded
content: `MediaStore.read` returns null for any `download` error, not only a missing object. `mediaComplete` treats null as 'a part was never uploaded': it runs `cleanupPrivate()` and answers 422 MISSING_PART «لم يُرفع كل جزء من الصورة.». The ticket was already claimed (once only), so the browser cannot retry the completion. A Storage 5xx during the read therefore deletes a complete upload and blames the user's upload, when the fault is server-side. The wrong-cause message, and the 422 instead of a retryable 5xx, is the defect.
failure_scenario: An editor uploads an original plus four derivatives, and all five parts are present. `media-complete` claims the ticket, then `download(stagedOriginal)` fails with a Storage 503 or a network reset. `read` returns null, so the handler calls `cleanupPrivate()` and returns 422 MISSING_PART. The parts are deleted, the ticket is spent, and the UI tells the user the upload was incomplete. The user must re-upload up to 31 MiB and cannot tell that it was a server error.
fix: Return null only when the Storage error is a not-found (check `error.statusCode`/`status` 404 or the 'not found' message). Otherwise throw, so the existing catch answers 500 FAILED «تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.».

title: Top-paths query takes 100 leading groups before the asset filter, so real pages fall out of the list
content: `TOP_PATHS_QUERY` asks Cloudflare for the 100 highest-count `clientRequestPath` groups. The JS filter (`isRealPage`) then drops `/_next`, `/admin`, `/api` and static extensions. The 100-group cap therefore applies to assets and pages together. The constant's own comment says this: 'Top paths are taken after filtering, from this many leading groups'. The status filter added for S07.1 removes 404s and 304s but not assets. On the export that ships today the static asset URLs greatly outnumber the pages. `out/` has 197 .webp, 13 .mp4, 7 .woff2, 54 `_next` files and 212 RSC .txt payloads, against 22 public HTML pages. Shared chunks, fonts and layout images are requested about once per cold visit. Each page's own images and chunk tie or beat that page's HTML count. The 100 slots fill with assets, so only a handful of real pages survive to `parseTopPaths`. The unit test 'parseTopPaths drops assets ... then takes the top 10' feeds pre-windowed fixtures, so it cannot catch this.
failure_scenario: In the 7-day window, 60 or more shared asset URLs (chunks, the 7 fonts, layout images) each have count near the number of cold visits. Each popular page also has 10 to 20 own image and RSC URLs with counts at or above the page's HTML count. The top 100 groups by `count_DESC` are almost all assets. `parseTopPaths` filters them out and returns only 3 to 5 pages. The owner's 'أكثر الصفحات طلبًا' list omits pages that really ranked 5th to 10th, or shows fewer than 10 rows.
fix: Filter pages server-side so the window holds only pages, for example `edgeResponseContentTypeName: "html"` in the query filter (confirm the field name in the schema at gate E11). Otherwise raise `limit` to the node's maxPageSize (10000) so the JS filter sees every path. Add a test where more than 100 asset groups outrank the pages.

title: ACTIVE_HOLD refusal tells the buyer to complete or cancel an order the page cannot reach, and gives no wait
content: `checkout_create` refuses with ACTIVE_HOLD when an unexpired pending order exists for the same normalized email or the same checkout session (SQL lines 889-897). The buyer's only handle on that order is `{orderNumber, accessToken}` in per-tab sessionStorage. The AUDIT-1 S14.9 fix persisted the idempotency key and fingerprint, but also in sessionStorage (cart.ts, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY and PENDING_ORDER_KEY). It covers a reload in the same tab only. CheckoutForm.tsx:323-331 shows this server message only when `readPendingOrder()` is null. So the message reaches exactly the buyers who cannot act on it. It also omits that the hold frees itself in 20 minutes, which is the only way out.
quote: ACTIVE_HOLD: { status: 409, message: 'لديك طلب قيد الانتظار؛ أكمله أو ألغه أولًا.' },
failure_scenario: A buyer submits checkout in an in-app browser (Instagram or WhatsApp). The order is created and the token is stored in that tab's sessionStorage. The buyer then opens the store link in Safari or Chrome, or reopens the site in a new tab. There is no pending order, idempotency key or checkout session in the new tab. They submit the same email and get 409 ACTIVE_HOLD, shown as 'أكمله أو ألغه أولًا'. The page has no way to complete or cancel that order, and the buyer is blocked for up to 20 minutes with no hint of when it ends.
fix: Change the copy to state the wait, for example 'لديك طلب قيد الانتظار بهذا البريد؛ يُفرَج عنه تلقائيًا خلال 20 دقيقة، أو أكمله من الصفحة التي بدأته منها.' Better, have `checkout_create` return the hold's remaining time or expiry with ACTIVE_HOLD, so the client shows it. Keep the same-tab shortcut in CheckoutForm.

title: Operator-side Turnstile failures are reported to visitors as 'you are not human' with no log, so a wrong secret looks like every visitor failing the challenge
content: verifyTurnstile discards the siteverify `error-codes` array. Any `success !== true` becomes INVALID_TOKEN, and TEST_SECRET_IN_PRODUCTION (line 56) is a non-UNREACHABLE code too. contact.ts (lines 136-139) and checkout.ts (324-326) map every code except UNREACHABLE to HTTP 400 'TURNSTILE' with the message 'تعذّر التحقق من أنك إنسان.'. Server-side causes (`invalid-input-secret`, `missing-input-secret`, `internal-error`, a test secret on a hosted site) are then indistinguishable from a bad visitor token. The visitor is told the failure is theirs, the widget resets, and every retry fails the same way. The function logs nothing, so the operator has no signal (SettingsView shows only 'configured' and 'test secret').
quote: if (typeof verified !== 'object' || verified === null || verified.success !== true) {
failure_scenario: At the first hosted deploy TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is pasted with a typo, or the secret belongs to a different widget. Cloudflare answers {success:false,'error-codes':['invalid-input-secret']}. Every contact and checkout attempt returns 400 with 'تعذّر التحقق من أنك إنسان.'. Real customers conclude they are being flagged as bots, and the checkout and contact form are dead while function logs show nothing. Cloudflare's transient `internal-error` gives the same visitor-blaming reply instead of a 503 retry.
fix: Read result['error-codes']. Map invalid-input-secret, missing-input-secret, internal-error and TEST_SECRET_IN_PRODUCTION to a server-side code that callers answer 503 TURNSTILE_UNAVAILABLE. console.warn the codes only (no token, no IP). Keep invalid-input-response and timeout-or-duplicate as INVALID_TOKEN.

title: S04.5 fix strips line breaks only; a visitor can still close the FSI/PDI isolate and override direction for the rest of the notice
content: `isolated()` exists so that 'mixed-direction text cannot reorder the line around it', but the visitor controls the characters inside it. A name (or message line) that contains U+2069 (PDI) closes the isolate early, and a following U+202E (RLO) or U+2067 then applies to the template's own text and to the following lines wherever the mail client renders plain text in a single HTML block (line breaks are not paragraph separators for the bidi algorithm). The fix for S04.5 handles \r, \n, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, but leaves the other bidi controls (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069) in name and message. The same applies to every message line at line 251. There is no test for it (tests/unit/email.test.ts only checks that FSI/PDI wrap ordinary lines).
failure_scenario: A visitor submits name '⁩‮x'. The notice line becomes 'الاسم: <FSI><PDI><RLO>x<PDI>'. The RLO is never terminated, so in a client that renders the body as one HTML block the البريد, الوقت and message lines below display reversed or reordered, including the address the owner is about to reply to. It is cosmetic and self-inflicted, but it defeats the stated purpose of the isolation.
fix: Strip U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 (and U+200E/U+200F if desired) from name and every message line before wrapping in isolated(); add a unit test with a PDI+RLO name.

title: Quota-held contact notices are recorded as an 'ok' run, so the owner home shows no warning; a contact flood then delays real notices by days
content: After S04.1, once 80 outbox sends are used in a UTC day (or 100, or 3,000 in the month) every priority-1 contact notice waits. Those rows stay 'due' (pending, next_at <= now()), so outbox_kick() calls the function every minute. Each call claims nothing, and line 182 maps `claimed === 0` to status 'ok', so job_run_record writes a fresh 'ok' run each minute. AdminHome.emailWaiting() warns only when a row has been due for over 10 minutes AND no run finished in the last 10 minutes. The run written a minute ago defeats that rule, so the owner home reports the email job as healthy while notices are held. outbox_attention() lists only exhausted/uncertain/suppressed/bad-delivery rows, not pending ones. The scheduler-liveness signal cannot see held-back mail. On top of that, outbox_claim orders by priority, next_at, id (strict FIFO), and contact_submit queues one notice per active owner/operations member while allowing 200 messages/day (contact:all). The reserve caps notice sends at 80/day. docs/operations.md accepts the flood risk because 'nothing is lost - messages already stored still reach the owner's mailbox' and reasons only about a one-day form lockout. With the reserve, the backlog is not one day long. It is measured in days, and D31 makes the notice email the only inbox (public.contacts has no reader).
failure_scenario: Owner + one operations member are active (2 recipients). An attacker who passes Turnstile submits 200 messages in a UTC day (about 40 IPs at 5/hour, or one IP plus rotating emails). This queues 400 notice rows, 80 are sent that day, 320 stay pending. The next day another 200 arrive and the drain is 80 again, so the queue only grows. A real visitor's message stored on day 2 has its notice behind 300+ spam rows and is emailed days later, or never while the flood lasts. Meanwhile each minute's run is recorded 'ok' with claimed 0, AdminHome shows 'ok (time)' for إرسال البريد, and outbox_attention is empty. Nothing tells the owner a real message is waiting. The same silent state occurs when the 3,000/month cap is reached.
fix: Report held-back work: when claimed === 0 and outbox_due_since() is non-null (or the claim returned nothing because of the daily/reserve/monthly caps), record status 'partial' with reason 'QUOTA_HELD' and have emailWaiting/JOB_STALE_TEXT treat it as trouble. Reduce the flood's effect: lower contact:all so cap x recipients <= DAILY_QUOTA - RESERVE, or collapse notices into a digest once the day's notice budget is spent. Correct the accepted-risk paragraph in docs/operations.md.
note: orchestrator: flood is an accepted risk; the ok-while-held status is the real defect

title: Email grammar accepts RFC-invalid addresses; when the provider refuses the Reply-To, the notice is permanently exhausted and the visitor was still told it arrived
content: EMAIL_SHAPE, and the identical DB CHECK on public.contacts.email, allow leading, trailing and consecutive dots in the local part, empty and leading/trailing-hyphen domain labels, and labels longer than 63 characters (verified in node: a..b@gmail.com, john.@gmail.com, .john@gmail.com, me@gmail..com, me@-a.com, me@.a.com and a 100-character label all match). The stored address becomes `reply_to` in the Resend request (email.ts sendWithResend). email.ts classifies every 4xx other than 409/429, including 400/422 validation_error, as 'permanent', so outbox_result exhausts the row on the first attempt. The contact was stored (contact_submit) and the visitor got the 201 'received', but the only copy of the message is public.contacts, which has no reader (D31: no admin inbox), and outbox_replay re-sends the same payload and fails again. Local e2e uses Mailpit, which does not apply the provider's address validation, so no test reaches this. The 'me@gmail..com' typo passes the form's own regex (ContactForm EMAIL) as well. I could not fetch Resend's docs from this sandbox. That Resend validates reply_to format is from its documented validation_error behaviour, and the classification comment in email.ts itself treats 400/422 as permanent.
failure_scenario: A visitor types 'ahmad..ali@gmail.com' or 'me@gmail..com' and sends a genuine enquiry. Zod, the DB CHECK and contact_submit all accept it, the notice row is queued, and the form says 'وصلت رسالتك'. The dispatcher sends to Resend with reply_to 'me@gmail..com', Resend answers 4xx validation_error, the row becomes exhausted with last_error HTTP_422 or HTTP_400, and an email.exhausted audit row is written. The owner never receives the message body, a replay fails identically, and the only trace is a row on البريد with no content.
fix: Tighten the grammar in contact.ts and the DB CHECK (new migration): local part without a leading/trailing/consecutive dot, domain as dot-separated labels of 1-63 alphanumerics with inner hyphens only. Also make the dispatcher resilient: for a contact_notice that gets a validation_error, retry once without reply_to (the address is already printed in the body line 'البريد:') instead of exhausting.

title: Checkout form still renders when approval was reset (empty policyRevisions) or the seller is unset; the buyer only learns after typing everything
content: AUDIT-1 X1.1 added the trigger policies_reset_approval (20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:119-158). Any change to an approved policy sets commerce_settings.policy_revisions to '{}' and leaves checkout_enabled true. checkout_quote (20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:769) returns checkoutEnabled: checkout_enabled and policyRevisions: {}. The client gates only on quote.checkoutEnabled. checkout_create refuses this state with POLICIES_NOT_CONFIGURED (SQL:859-861), and SELLER_NOT_CONFIGURED (SQL:856-858) behaves the same way. The client was not updated for the new reachable state, so the fix leaves the buyer with a broken form.
failure_scenario: P08 enables checkout. The owner republishes the delivery policy, and X1.1 resets the approval. A buyer opens /checkout. The quote says checkoutEnabled: true, policyRevisions: {}. The form renders. consentPolicies is empty, so the mandatory checkbox reads «قرأت  وأوافق عليها» with no policy links. The buyer fills every field and solves Turnstile, which spends the token. Pressing «تأكيد الطلب» returns 503 POLICIES_NOT_CONFIGURED. The page shows «الشراء غير متاح حاليًا، ويفتح قريبًا.» under the form, after all the effort.
fix: Treat an empty policyRevisions like a closed store in the client: `if (!quote.checkoutEnabled || Object.keys(quote.policyRevisions).length === 0) return <closed note>`. Better, have checkout_quote return checkoutEnabled = checkout_enabled AND seller configured AND policy_revisions <> '{}', so it mirrors checkout_create's gates 2a to 2c.

title: A failed quote refresh disables staleness detection, so the button stays enabled on an outdated summary and burns create attempts
content: S14.8 blocks submit while `stale || !quote.ok`. But `stale` is defined with `!quoteFailed`, so as soon as a refresh fails (with a quote already on screen) staleness is switched off. The summary keeps the old shipping, discount and total, and the button stays enabled. The submit sends the new city or coupon with the old quoteHash, and the server answers QUOTE_CHANGED (409). checkout_create takes the per-IP (10/h) and per-email (5/h) throttles and a Turnstile verification before it reaches the price check (SQL:879-917), so each such attempt is spent. The QUOTE_CHANGED branch (lines 294-300) then does not clear quoteFailed or update quoteKey, so the failure banner also stays on top of a fresh quote.
quote: const stale = quote !== null && !quoteFailed && quoteKey !== currentKey
failure_scenario: A buyer with a physical cart picks Riyadh (quote OK). They switch to Jeddah and the debounced quote request drops (mobile network blip), so quoteFailed=true. The summary still shows Riyadh shipping and the button is enabled. The buyer presses «تأكيد الطلب», which sends cityKey=jeddah with the Riyadh quoteHash, and the server answers 409 QUOTE_CHANGED. One of the buyer's 5 hourly create attempts is gone, and the «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» banner remains over the freshly returned quote.
fix: Compute stale as `quote !== null && quoteKey !== currentKey` (independent of quoteFailed) so submit stays blocked until a quote for the current inputs arrives. In the QUOTE_CHANGED branch also call setQuoteKey(currentKey) and setQuoteFailed(false).

title: With a quote already on screen, a failed refresh shows «أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات» but offers no retry action
content: S14.3 fixed the case where the form was replaced. The full-page retry button now exists only in the `quoteFailed && quote === null` view (lines 421-430). When a quote is already on screen, the failure is only an alert banner. The quote effect depends on [ready, cart, city, coupon], and applyCoupon with an unchanged code sets an equal state, so nothing re-runs. The buyer's only way out is a reload, which loses everything typed. That is the exact complaint S14.3 recorded. The gap is worst after POLICY_CHANGED: refreshQuote() fails (line 190), consent is reset, and the old policyRevisions stay in `quote`. Every re-confirm then sends the old revisions and is refused with POLICY_CHANGED again.
failure_scenario: A digital-cart buyer applies a coupon and the quote request fails. They see «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار؛ أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات.» with no control that retries. Waiting does nothing, because no effect re-fires. The only recovery is a reload that wipes the email and name fields.
fix: Render an «أعد المحاولة» ActionButton (calling refreshQuote) inside this banner, as the quote===null view already does.

title: A confirm press that was answered with a Turnstile failure is still 'pending', so a later Turnstile recovery submits the order without a new press
content: awaitingToken is set on a press made before the token exists (line 233). It is cleared only when submit() later passes validation and reaches line 237. If Turnstile fires error-callback while waiting, useTurnstile sets failed=true and token=''. `waiting` becomes false, so the button is re-enabled with the normal label, and the note «تعذّر تحميل التحقق؛ حدّث الصفحة.» appears. awaitingToken stays true. src/lib/turnstile.ts:64-67 clears `failed` and sets a token on a later successful callback, so recovery is an anticipated path. The effect below then fires requestSubmit() on its own.
failure_scenario: The buyer presses «تأكيد الطلب» before the check finishes. Turnstile errors, and the page says to refresh. The buyer instead edits the address. Turnstile auto-retries and returns a token. The effect calls requestSubmit(), and the order (a 20-minute hold) is created from the current form state. No press followed the error message.
fix: Clear awaitingToken when turnstileFailed becomes true, for example `useEffect(() => { if (turnstileFailed) setAwaitingToken(false) }, [turnstileFailed])`, or also call setAwaitingToken(false) in the `turnstileFailed` branch at line 229.

title: City list failures and an empty city list are silent: the buyer of a physical cart gets a dead select and only «اختر مدينة التوصيل»
content: fetchCities returns [] on a non-OK response (quote.ts:280) and the catch here also maps errors to []. It is called once on mount, with no retry and no state that distinguishes 'failed' from 'none served'. shipping_rates only exposes rows that are enabled and priced to anon, and D09 says an unpriced city is not served, so an empty list is a legitimate state too. In either case the physical branch renders a select containing only «اختر المدينة». The summary and the field error both say «اختر مدينة التوصيل.», which the buyer cannot satisfy.
failure_scenario: The REST call to /rest/v1/shipping_rates times out, or the owner has enabled no city yet. A buyer with a physical cart sees the city select with a single placeholder option. Pressing confirm shows «اختر مدينة التوصيل.» forever. Nothing says delivery is unavailable or that the list failed to load, and there is no retry.
fix: Keep a `citiesState` of 'loading' | 'failed' | 'loaded'. For 'failed' show an alert with a retry. For a loaded empty list show «لا نوصل إلى أي مدينة حاليًا» and disable submit.

title: Coupon input has no length cap; a code over 64 characters makes every quote fail and, after a reload, leaves checkout as a dead end
content: The checkout function bounds couponCode at 64 characters (_shared/checkout.ts:46, and :66 for create). A longer value is refused at the schema step with 422 INVALID, so fetchQuote throws (quote.ts:229-231) and only the generic «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار؛ أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات.» appears. That message blames the connection. The name (120) and address (500) inputs in this form carry maxLength, but the coupon input does not. applyCoupon persists the value to sessionStorage, and the mount effect restores it (lines 117-121). On the next reload of /checkout the first quote fails with quote===null, so the page is replaced by the «أعد المحاولة» view (lines 421-430). That view has no coupon field and no link to /cart, and its retry re-sends the same bad code.
failure_scenario: A buyer pastes a 70-character string into «كود الخصم» and presses «تطبيق». The quote fails with a misleading network message. They reload the page. Checkout now shows only «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» and «أعد المحاولة», and retrying never succeeds, because the saved coupon is re-sent every time. The only escape is finding the header cart link and clearing the coupon there.
fix: Add maxLength={64} to the coupon input in CheckoutForm (and CartView). In the quote-failed view render the coupon field or a link to /cart. When the function answers 422 for a quote, drop the stored coupon.

title: The order summary the buyer confirms never shows the signed-book dedication, although the server echoes it and it is tab-scoped by design
content: QuoteLine.dedication is parsed (quote.ts:126) but nothing renders it. The summary line shows only title, variant and quantity. The dedication lives only in sessionStorage and goes with the tab (cart.ts:6-8, G1.3), and SQL order_summary does not return it either. The confirmation screen is therefore the only step where a buyer could catch a missing or wrong personal message, and it says nothing about it. A dedication is lost silently whenever the checkout tab has different sessionStorage from the cart tab (ctrl/middle-click into a new tab, a later visit with the localStorage cart intact). That state looks identical to 'no dedication wanted'.
failure_scenario: A buyer types «إلى أمي مع الحب» for a signed copy on /cart, then opens «إتمام الشراء» in a new tab. sessionStorage is empty there, so the quote is priced without a dedication. The summary shows the book, ×1 and the price, with nothing about the dedication, and the buyer confirms. The book is prepared and shipped unsigned.
fix: Under each summary line render `line.dedication` (the server-echoed, trimmed text) when present, and a short «بدون إهداء» line for signed lines that lack one. Show them in the pending-order view too if the order summary later returns them.

title: writeCart persists a whole-cart snapshot from React state, so a stale /cart tab silently deletes items added in another tab
content: CartView computes every edit from the cart it loaded at mount, e.g. update(setQuantity(cart, ...)). CartProvider.update passes it straight to writeCart, which overwrites the localStorage key. Nothing re-reads storage before the write. CartProvider reads once on mount and has no `storage` listener. CartLink was given one (S14.11), which shows the design expects cross-tab changes.
failure_scenario: Tab A shows /cart with [book X]. In tab B the buyer adds product Y, so storage is [X, Y]. Back in tab A the header count reads 2 but the page lists only X. The buyer presses «+» on X, which writes [X×2] and drops Y. No message is shown, and Y is gone from every tab.
fix: Make edits read-modify-write: have `update` accept an updater function applied to readCart().cart just before writing. Also refresh CartProvider state on the window `storage` event, as CartLink does.

title: A stored pending order can only be cleared by a successful cancel; a NOT_FOUND reply leaves the tab stuck on a hold view that no longer describes anything
content: On reload, the pending order comes from sessionStorage (line 108) and replaces the whole checkout with the hold view. Its only exit is cancelOrder, which clears storage only on ok with status cancelled or expired (line 357). checkout_cancel answers NOT_FOUND once access_token_expires_at (created as now()+7 days, SQL:957) has passed (SQL:1036-1041). That leaves the else branch, which just shows «لم نجد هذا الطلب.». The static copy «حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة» never checks holdExpiresAt, which orderSchema parses and then drops. Mobile tabs and restored sessions routinely outlive 7 days.
failure_scenario: A buyer creates an order on their phone, gets distracted, and the tab survives eight days. They open it. The page claims a 20-minute hold and offers «إلغاء الطلب». Cancel answers 404 «لم نجد هذا الطلب.» and pending is never cleared, so the buyer cannot reach the checkout form in this tab again.
fix: On code NOT_FOUND in cancelOrder, treat the order as ended: clearPendingOrder(), clearIdempotency(), setClosed('expired'). Store holdExpiresAt with the pending order and show the closed state directly when it is in the past.

title: ACTIVE_HOLD from a hold whose token this tab does not have still tells the buyer to complete or cancel it, which the page cannot do
content: S14.9's complaint was 'blocked by their own hold and told to do something the page cannot do'. The fix keeps the key and a digest across a reload, but that only recovers if the buyer retypes a request that normalizes to the same fingerprint. Otherwise readPendingOrder() is null (the reply was lost, or the order was made in another tab or on another device). The code falls to line 332 and shows the server text «لديك طلب قيد الانتظار؛ أكمله أو ألغه أولًا.». checkout_create matches holds by email hash OR checkout session (SQL:889-895). No page offers to complete or cancel without the token in this tab's sessionStorage. The `mine` branch is effectively unreachable, because a stored pending order already replaces the form on mount.
failure_scenario: A buyer places an order on their phone and then tries again from a laptop with the same email. The laptop shows «أكمله أو ألغه أولًا», but there is nothing to complete or cancel there. They are locked out until the hold expires, up to 20 minutes, with no indication of how long.
fix: When ACTIVE_HOLD arrives and there is no local pending order, show a specific message: a hold under this email exists and can be retried after it lapses (20 minutes), or cancelled from the tab that created it. Drop the unreachable `mine` branch.

title: Cart quote failure tells the buyer to retry but offers no retry, and nothing retries
content: When the quote request fails (network blip, HTTP 5xx, the quote throttle returning 429), CartView sets quoteFailed and shows «أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات». The effect at lines 103-127 depends only on ready, storedCart, city and coupon, so it never runs again on its own. There is no button and no timer. AUDIT-1 S14.3 fixed the same defect in CheckoutForm by adding an «أعد المحاولة» ActionButton wired to refreshQuote (CheckoutForm.tsx ~421-427). The cart page, which is the first page of the flow, did not get it.
quote:
{quoteFailed &&

تعذّر تحديث الأسعار؛ أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات.

}
failure_scenario: The buyer opens /cart with two lines and the first quote returns 500 or 429. quote stays null, so every line title and price renders «…», there are no totals and no checkout link. The alert says to retry after a moment, but no control exists and no timer fires. The buyer can recover only by reloading, or by changing a quantity, coupon or city to change the effect deps.
fix: Add an «أعد المحاولة» ActionButton beside the alert that re-runs the quote. Use a retry counter in the effect deps, or reuse the refreshQuote pattern from CheckoutForm. Alternatively retry once automatically after a few seconds.

title: Coupon field has no length bound; an over-long code makes every quote fail with a misleading message and survives reload
content: The checkout function's quote schema is `couponCode: z.string().max(64)` (supabase/functions/_shared/checkout.ts:46) and the database code pattern is `^[A-Z0-9]{3,32}$`. The input has no maxLength. «تطبيق» stores the trimmed, upper-cased text in sessionStorage (COUPON_KEY), which is restored on mount. A 65+ character value gets HTTP 422 INVALID. fetchQuote throws on !reply.ok, so CartView shows the generic price-update failure instead of «كود الخصم غير صالح». The CheckoutForm coupon input has the same gap.
failure_scenario: The buyer pastes a 70-character string (a URL or a sentence) into «كود الخصم» and taps «تطبيق». Every quote now gets 422. The cart turns into the failed state (lines show «…», no totals, no checkout link) with a message that suggests a network problem. Reloading does not help because the coupon is restored from sessionStorage. Nothing points at the coupon field.
fix: Add maxLength={32} to the coupon inputs in the cart and in CheckoutForm, matching the DB pattern. Optionally map a 422 INVALID reply on quote to the COUPON_INVALID message when a coupon was sent.

title: «إزالة غير المتاح» deletes lines that are only over-quantity or have a bad dedication, not just unavailable ones
content: invalidVariants (line 133) collects every error that carries a variantId. That includes OUT_OF_STOCK with available > 0, INVALID_DEDICATION and DEDICATION_NOT_ALLOWED, which the buyer can fix by lowering the quantity or clearing the text (the line's own message says «المتاح: n»). The button is labelled «إزالة غير المتاح» (remove unavailable) and removeLines drops the whole line, along with its typed dedication.
failure_scenario: The cart has 5 copies of a signed edition with stock 3. The line error reads «الكمية المطلوبة غير متوفرة؛ المتاح: 3.» and the «إزالة غير المتاح» button appears. A buyer who taps it expecting only sold-out items to go loses the whole line, including the 3 copies that were available and the typed dedication, and has to re-add it from the product page.
fix: Limit the bulk removal to UNAVAILABLE lines, and to OUT_OF_STOCK with available === 0. For partly available lines offer «اجعلها n» (set the quantity to available) or leave the fix to the quantity control.

title: Dedication inputs on different lines share one accessible name
content: AUDIT-1 X3.11 gave the quantity, ± and «حذف» controls per-line names built from `name`. The dedication input inside the same line card is still labelled by the bare text «نص الإهداء», so every signed line exposes the same name. A screen-reader user moving through the form controls cannot tell which product a field belongs to.
failure_scenario: The cart holds two signed books. Tabbing through the controls, a screen-reader user hears «نص الإهداء» twice with no product name and cannot tell which book each field is for. This is the same problem X3.11 fixed for the other controls.
fix: Add `aria-label={`نص الإهداء: ${name}`}` to the input, or a visually-hidden `: {name}` inside the label as AddToCart does.

title: Cart is read once on mount and then written back whole, so another tab's additions are overwritten
content: CartProvider reads localStorage once. update() then writes the full `next` cart built from that in-memory snapshot. CartLink listens to 'storage' and CART_EVENT, but CartProvider never re-syncs from other tabs. Any edit on /cart (quantity, «حذف», dedication) or /checkout overwrites the shared `anasaq:cart:v1` with the stale snapshot.
failure_scenario: Tab A shows /cart with one line. In tab B the buyer opens a product and adds a second item, which writes localStorage. Back in tab A the second item is not shown. The buyer taps «حذف» on the first line, and A writes a cart without the second item. The item added in B is silently lost, and the «السلة (n)» link in B drops to match.
fix: In CartProvider, listen to 'storage' (and CART_EVENT) and call setState(readCart()). Or re-read readCart() inside update() and apply the mutation to the fresh cart.

title: S06.8 fix leaves the partial-cap case: an add clamped by addLine still says «أُضيف إلى السلة»
content: AUDIT-1 S06.8 was «confirms an add that addLine refused or capped». The fix compares cartCount before and after and only reports a refusal when nothing changed. addLine also caps a merged line at 20 (`Math.min(MAX_QUANTITY, l.quantity + quantity)`), so a partial add changes the count and passes this check. The note then claims success and gives only the whole-cart count.
failure_scenario: The cart holds 18 of a variant plus 4 items in other lines. The buyer sets the quantity to 5 and taps «أضف إلى السلة». The cart goes from 18 to 20, only 2 of the 5 are added, and the note says «أُضيف إلى السلة. في السلة الآن 24.». The buyer believes 5 were added and does not learn that the per-product maximum of 20 clipped the add.
fix: Compare the added amount with the requested one: `const added = cartCount(next) - cartCount(cart)`. If `added < quantity`, say that only `added` were added because the maximum is 20 per product. Keep the current message for added === 0.
