MotionLayer's scan runs at the old offset, so the first-screen reveals are skipped as 'above the fold'. It affects the main way of moving between rooms.
fix: Add `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` to the `<html>` element in src/app/(public)/layout.tsx (and the admin layout if it loads globals.css). In-page anchors and SectionNav links keep their smooth scroll.

title: menu-weave has no `to` clip-path, so the menu opens empty and its bands pop in instead of wiping
content: Same root cause as the motion.css keyframes. `.menu[open] .menuLink` runs `menu-weave` with `backwards` fill and `calc(var(--i) * 45ms)` delay. The keyframe has only `from { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 100%) }` and the end state is `none`, so Chromium treats it as discrete (verified: stays fully clipped until 50% of the eased time, then `none`).
failure_scenario: On a phone the visitor taps «القائمة». The dialog opens showing only the top bar on the aubergine backdrop. Each of the 60px+ bands stays invisible for roughly 280ms (`--dur-base` 560ms halved) plus `i * 45ms`, then appears at once, so the last band (i up to 6-7) shows at about 600ms. It reads as lag, not as the woven wipe DESIGN.md describes.
fix: Add `to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0) }` to menu-weave.

title: tile-in, viewer-in, photo-next and photo-prev are from-only clip-path animations (discrete flip at 50%)
content: tile-in (line 61), viewer-in (150), photo-next (200) and photo-prev (205) each declare only `from { clip-path: ... }`. The end state is `clip-path: none`, which does not interpolate with `inset()`, so each snaps at 50% of its eased duration (verified in Chromium 153). The lightbox 'opens with a wipe' and a photo 'step' from DESIGN.md:142 are therefore a delayed appearance.
failure_scenario: Open /scenes: each tile is clipped away for about 350ms plus `min(i,10) * 45ms` and then pops in. Open a photo: the dialog shows only the aub-900 backdrop for about 140ms, then the whole viewer appears. Press the next arrow: the new photo is invisible for about 140ms, then appears, so each step blinks instead of wiping.
fix: Add an explicit `to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0) }` to all four keyframes (same fix as motion.css).

title: ::selection colours equal the aubergine band colours, so selected text is invisible on aub bands
content: `::selection` paints `--aub` background with `--sand-50` text globally. On `data-tone="aub"` the band is `--bg: var(--aub)` with `--fg: var(--sand-50)`, i.e. exactly the same pair, so selection changes nothing. There are 25 `tone="aub"` bands, and the footer (`<footer data-tone="aub">`) is on every public page. On night and deep bands the difference is about 1.2:1. No other `::selection` rule exists for the site (the only one is in the book reader).
failure_scenario: A visitor selects the footer poem or the home statement band to copy or read it aloud. Nothing is highlighted, so they cannot tell what was selected or whether the drag worked.
fix: Make the selection tone-aware, e.g. `::selection { background: var(--fg); color: var(--bg); }`, which inverts on every band, or give dark tones an explicit saffron selection.

title: .motion-scrub > * also animates Figure's corner caption
content: Figure.tsx:38 puts the `motion-scrub` class on the frame, and the frame contains both the `<picture>` and the absolutely placed `<figcaption class=corner>`. `.motion-scrub > *` therefore applies the scroll-linked `scale(1.16) -> scale(1.06)` and `translateY` to the caption as well as the image. The doc comment describes the class as 'an image frame that zooms out slowly'. The combination is real: PassedRoomView.tsx:112 (product brand captions «ارم», «مرادي») and BookView.tsx:153 (photo captions) both use `scrub` with `captionPlacement="corner"`.
failure_scenario: On /passed in a browser with scroll timelines, the brand label on each product tile grows to 1.16x (15px text becomes about 17px) when the tile enters and shrinks to 1.06x as it scrolls, while its bottom and inline-start edges are pushed against the frame's overflow:hidden. The label looks like it breathes as the page scrolls.
fix: Scope the rule to the image: `.motion-scrub > picture { ... }` (Figure and the journal/home figures all wrap the image in `<picture>`), or render the corner caption outside the scrubbed frame.

title: Section links' focus ring is clipped top and bottom by the scroller
content: `.scroller` sets `overflow-x:auto`, which computes `overflow-y` to `auto` (checked in Chromium). `.list` has `padding-block:0` and `.link` is exactly 54px tall, so the scroller is 54px high. `.link` has no data-tone and no focus rule, so it gets the global `:focus-visible` ring (3px outline, 3px offset), which lies 3px to 6px outside the link box and is clipped by the scroller at the top and bottom. Only the two side bars remain. Elsewhere the code moves rings inside for exactly this reason (`[data-tone]:is(a,button)`, `.play`, `.captionLink a`).
failure_scenario: A keyboard user tabs through «أقسام الكتاب» on /book. Each link shows only two vertical saffron bars, no top or bottom edge, on a 54px strip, which is a weak indicator against the aubergine bar.
fix: Draw the ring inside: `.link:focus-visible { outline-offset: -6px }`, or give `.list` block padding of at least 6px.

title: The film's own focus ring is fully clipped, so the focus VideoTile moves to it has no visible indicator
content: VideoTile.tsx:70 moves focus to the `<video>` when playback starts. `.video` fills `.tile`, which has `overflow:hidden`, and gets the global `:focus-visible` ring drawn 3px outside its box (there is no `.video:focus-visible` rule and no data-tone), so the whole ring is clipped. `.play` was given an inside ring for the same reason, but the video was not.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user presses Enter on «تشغيل». The button unmounts and focus lands on the `<video>`, but nothing shows where focus is until the next Tab reaches a native control. Space or K works on an element the user cannot see is focused.
fix: Add `.video:focus-visible { outline-offset: -6px; }` (tone colour comes from the band; `--focus` is inherited).

title: An AbortError from the visitor's own pause is reported as a playback failure
content: `start()` sets state 'playing' (native controls appear) and then calls `play()`. With `preload="none"` the promise stays pending until data arrives. If the visitor presses pause in that window, the browser rejects the promise with AbortError ('interrupted by a call to pause()'). The catch handler sets 'failed' regardless of the reason. The film itself is fine. This is separate from AUDIT-1 S13.5, whose fix (always-mounted status region) holds.
failure_scenario: On a slow mobile connection the visitor taps «تشغيل» on the 5.8 MB raha-reel film, sees the controls, and taps pause before the first bytes arrive. `state` becomes 'failed': the controls are removed, the play button returns and «تعذّر تشغيل المقطع. حاول مرة أخرى.» is announced, though nothing failed.
fix: Ignore the abort: `.catch((error) => { if (error?.name !== 'AbortError') setState('failed') })`.

title: .lattice paints its solid --line colour into unfilled cells; two 3-item lattices leave an aubergine hole at tablet widths
content: `.lattice` uses `background: var(--line)` for its 1px seams, and that background also fills any empty grid cell. Other lattices append a weave filler (JournalList.tsx:82, ShelfRoomView.tsx:189, PassedRoomView.tsx:54; scenes.module.css:44 says 'A row that does not fill shows the weave, as B's lattices end'). BookView.tsx:182 (`.objects`, 3 items, `--tile:240px`) and ShelfRoomView.tsx:74 (`.doors`, 3 items, `--tile:280px`) have no filler. At a 768px viewport the content width is about 689px, so auto-fit gives 2 columns for both and the third item sits alone in row 2.
failure_scenario: On an iPad-portrait viewport (768 to about 805px on /book, 625 to about 935px on /shelf) the last row is one card plus a solid aubergine rectangle the size of a card, instead of the woven cell used everywhere else.
fix: Add a `weave` filler cell (aria-hidden li with the existing weaveCell style) to those two lists, or make `.lattice > :last-child:nth-child(...)` fillers a shared class in layout.module.css that paints weave.svg instead of solid ink.

title: The current-room and current-section triangles vanish in forced-colors mode
content: The only visual cue for `aria-current` is a triangle drawn with `background: currentColor` (site.module.css `.here` line 68, `.menuHere` line 172) or `background: var(--coral)` (section-nav.module.css:67). In forced-colors mode Chromium replaces `background-color` with the system Canvas colour. Checked with forcedColors emulation: a `background:currentColor` triangle on a sand page computes to rgb(255,255,255), the same as the page, so it is invisible. action.module.css and signature.module.css already have forced-colors handling for their decorative shapes, but these state cues do not.
failure_scenario: A sighted Windows High Contrast user opens the header on /book. No link shows which room they are in, and SectionNav shows no current section, because the triangle has become Canvas on Canvas.
fix: Add `@media (forced-colors: active) { .here, .menuHere { forced-color-adjust: none; background: CanvasText; } }` in site.module.css and the same for `.here` in section-nav.module.css.

title: The pressed filter is shown only by a background swap, which forced-colors mode erases
content: `.filter[aria-pressed='true']` differs from the unpressed state only by `background` and `color`. Checked with forcedColors emulation in Chromium: a pressed button computes to background rgb(255,255,255) and an unpressed one to transparent white on a white page, both with black text, so they look the same. scenes.module.css:20 has the identical rule. Both filters are visible only when scripting is enabled.
failure_scenario: A Windows High Contrast user on /journal or /scenes clicks a category. The list changes, but no filter button shows which one is active, so they cannot tell the current filter or how to get back to «الكل».
fix: Add to both files: `@media (forced-colors: active) { .filter[aria-pressed='true'] { background: Highlight; color: HighlightText; forced-color-adjust: none; } }`, or add a border or underline on the pressed state.

title: go() during a running turn lands on the wrong spread: holding End (key repeat) ends on the blank/endpaper spread
content: go() drives page-flip's flip(page). Flip.flipToPage() mutates the collection's currentSpreadIndex to next-1 (or next+1) before the animation starts, and the index is only corrected when the animation callback runs. A second go() while a turn is in flight computes 'next vs current' against the mutated index, so page-flip first finishes the first turn (finishAnimation runs its callback) and then starts one more turn in the same direction. onKeyDown does not ignore event.repeat, and docs/book-preview.md promises 'Home and End go to the cover and the closing leaf'. Home is bounded by the cover, so it is safe. End targets a middle spread, so it overshoots by one spread. The same happens if a second part is picked in «انتقل إلى» within the 900ms turn.
failure_scenario: Landscape, preview plan of 12 leaves, book on the cover. The visitor holds End for a little over 0.5s. Keydown 1 calls go(8). The mutated spread index is 3 and a 900ms backward turn starts. The auto-repeat keydown then calls go(8) again. flipToPage sees current=3 and next=2, so it flips again. finishAnimation completes turn 1 and lands on spread 2, then start() begins another backward turn. The book stops on page-flip spread [1,2], which is reading leaves 10 and 9: the back endpaper and a blank. The label reads «نهاية الصفحات المتاحة» but the closing leaf with «النسخ ←» is not on screen. Reduced-motion users are unaffected because they take the fade path.
fix: In go() (and turn()), return early while a turn is running: expose getState() in page-flip.d.ts and use `if (flip.getState() !== 'read') return`, or check `block.dataset.turning !== undefined`. Also ignore `event.repeat` for Home and End in onKeyDown.

title: Resizing or rotating into portrait on the last spread strands the reader on an empty endpaper and arms a stale skip that hijacks the next turn
content: page-flip's update() ends in pages.show(), which fires a 'flip' event with no turn in progress. The ResizeObserver calls flip.update() on every size change. When the book changes from landscape to portrait while on the last inner spread, the event carries leaf 10, the back endpaper (the left leaf of the last spread is always an empty leaf). The handler sees portrait and an empty leaf, so it stores skipRef and returns without setIndex or any turn. skipRef is only consumed on the next changeState 'read', which does not come for a resize.
failure_scenario: A phone in landscape (width over 800px) is turned to the last spread [9,10] (a blank, then the endpaper). The visitor rotates to portrait. The book now shows the bare endpaper alone. `from` equals `at` (both 10), so the handler walks the target backwards to leaf 8 and sets skipRef=8. Nothing turns the page. The visitor taps «التالية». The turn reaches the back cover (leaf 11). On the resulting 'read' state, skip !== null, so a requestAnimationFrame runs go(8). The book jumps back to the closing leaf right after arriving at the back cover, while the visitor asked to go forward.
fix: In the flip handler, when flip.getState() === 'read' (an update or orientation change, not a turn), call requestAnimationFrame(() => go(target)) directly instead of storing skipRef. Alternatively clear skipRef on every 'flip' event that does not come from a turn.

title: A failed getDocument() never destroys its loading task, so every failed load or «إعادة المحاولة» leaves a live pdf.js worker (S15.6 fixed only the measureFrame path)
content: getDocument() without a shared worker creates its own PDFWorker (node_modules/pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.mjs:15484-15487). When the load fails (missing or corrupt file, or the network dropping: DocException at :16653, or the setup chain at :15565), the code only rejects the capability with `.catch(task._capability.reject)`. Nothing destroys the worker; that only happens in PDFDocumentLoadingTask.destroy() (:15597). openPreview() destroys doc.loadingTask only when measureFrame() throws, and tests/unit/pdf-open.test.ts covers only that path.
quote: const doc = await pdfjs.getDocument({ url, enableXfa: false, disableFontFace: true, verbosity: pdfjs.VerbosityLevel.ERRORS }).promise
failure_scenario: The visitor is on a flaky connection. The preview request fails, the reader shows «تعذّر فتح الصفحات.», and the visitor presses «إعادة المحاولة» four times. Each attempt calls getDocument() again and rejects. Five pdf.js Worker threads stay alive for the whole SPA session and are never terminated. tests/e2e/reader.spec.ts:264 exercises exactly this retry sequence but does not assert worker cleanup.
fix: Keep the task: `const task = pdfjs.getDocument({...}); let doc; try { doc = await task.promise } catch (error) { void task.destroy(); throw error }`, then continue with the existing measureFrame try/catch. Add a unit case where getDocument's promise rejects and assert destroy was called.

title: Arrow/Home/End handling ignores modifier keys and steals Alt+← / Cmd+← (browser Back) while the book has focus
content: onKeyDown maps event.key without looking at altKey, ctrlKey or metaKey and calls preventDefault. The book host is focused automatically as soon as the book opens (host.focus() in the build effect), so the handler is live for a visitor who has not touched the book.
failure_scenario: The visitor opens the book (focus moves to the book), reads a page, then presses Alt+ArrowLeft (Windows or Linux) or Cmd+ArrowLeft (macOS) to go back. The keydown is cancelled and the page turns instead, so history navigation is blocked until they click elsewhere. Ctrl/Cmd+Home and Ctrl/Cmd+End are swallowed the same way and cannot scroll to the page top or bottom.
fix: Add `if (event.altKey || event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey) return` before the lookup.

title: «انتقل إلى» is controlled by state that only updates after the 900ms turn, so the select snaps back and cannot be stepped with the arrow keys
content: The select's value is part.index, derived from the index state. That state only changes on page-flip's 'flip' event at the end of the animation. onChange calls go() but sets no state, so React restores the DOM select to the old value right after the event handler. In a closed select, Chrome and Firefox on Windows and Linux fire change on every arrow keypress.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user focuses «انتقل إلى» on the cover and presses ArrowDown. The change event fires go(2) (الإهداء) and React immediately resets the select to «الغلاف». Pressing ArrowDown again within the turn selects «الإهداء» again instead of «المقدمة», so the third option is unreachable without waiting about a second between presses. A screen reader hears the chosen option revert, then change once the turn ends.
fix: Hold the picked value in local state set in onChange (the select shows it at once), and clear it when the 'flip' event updates index. Or use an uncontrolled select with a key that changes with part.index.

title: The closing leaf's flex centring is dead: page-flip writes inline display:block on every shown leaf
content: HTMLPage.simpleDraw() and HTMLPage.draw() replace element.style.cssText on every frame, and both start with `display: block`. An inline declaration beats the class rule, so `.leaf[data-kind='end']` is never a flex container. justify-content, align-items, flex-direction and gap all do nothing. The same rule works for `.closing` in the reading view, which page-flip does not touch, so the two ends of the preview differ.
failure_scenario: The visitor reaches «هنا تنتهي الصفحات المتاحة للقراءة.» in the book view. The text, the «بقية الحكاية في الكتاب.» line and the «النسخ ←» link are stacked from the top of the leaf under the 12% padding, with no 0.9em gaps, instead of being centred vertically as in the reading view's closing block.
fix: Lay the leaf out with block-level rules that survive an inline display:block: wrap the three children in one inner div in makeLeaf and make that div the flex column (with height:100%, justify-content:center, gap), or place the content with position:absolute; inset:12%; display:flex on the inner wrapper.

title: One page at a time, the page that peels away on «السابقة» is a blank clone, contradicting 'a turning page is never blank'
content: In portrait, page-flip's getFlippingPage(FORWARD) returns pages[current].newTemporaryCopy() (src/Collection/PageCollection.ts:161, src/Page/HTMLPage.ts:26-46). That is element.cloneNode(true) appended to the block. A cloned <canvas> keeps its width/height attributes but not its bitmap, and the clone has no PageSurface, so nothing ever draws into it. The reader's ink is on that canvas and the text layer is hidden while data-turning is set, so the peeling copy shows only paper and the spine shade. flipNext('bottom') (turn(-1) in portrait: the «السابقة» button, → key, click on the right half) takes this path. Landscape turns and the «التالية» direction use the real leaf elements. docs/book-preview.md line 69 says 'a turning page is never blank', and AUDIT-1 S15.5 was fixed on that basis, but only for the pages underneath.
failure_scenario: Phone (portrait), book on page 2. The visitor taps «السابقة» or the right half of the page. turn(-1) calls flip.flipNext('bottom'). page-flip clones the current leaf (canvas bitmap lost), draws the clone on top and peels it. For the 900ms turn the page's words disappear at once and a blank sheet curls away, revealing the previous page's ink. Every previous-page turn on every phone shows this.
fix: When changeState reports 'flipping' in portrait, copy each original canvas into the duplicate leaf's canvas: find the .stf__item nodes with the same data-page and call clone.querySelector('canvas').getContext('2d').drawImage(original, 0, 0). Or set the clone's canvas to the same bitmap via toDataURL/drawImage before the first frame. Then add an e2e frame check for the portrait previous turn.

title: A write error on the output file skips the catch: the .partial file stays and the process dies on an unhandled rejection
content: writeBackup promises (docstring, lines 116-122) that the partial file is deleted on any failure. That only holds when a failure is thrown inside the awaited chain. A failure of the output stream itself is not. failurePromise(out) is a rejecting promise that nothing observes while entries stream: writeChunk races it only on backpressure of the 46-byte header and again for the tag. writeEntryFile (lines 182-190) waits only for the source file's 'end' and never races `failed`. When `out` errors (disk full, removable drive unplugged), the pipe unpipes the cipher, the rejection is unhandled and Node aborts the process. The catch at line 169 never runs, so `await rm(...partial)` never executes. The only test (backup-format.test.ts:179) covers a vanished source file, not a failing destination.
failure_scenario: `pnpm backup --out E:\` (the docs suggest a USB drive) and E: fills up or is unplugged mid-write. Reproduced with fs.createWriteStream patched to raise ENOSPC after 200 KB: the process exits with code 1 through triggerUncaughtException (a stack trace, no 'Backup failed' message) and `x.enc.partial` stays in the output directory (readdir showed ['src','x.enc.partial']). On a full disk the leftover file keeps the space occupied, and every retry can leave another one.
fix: Make the output stream's error part of the awaited chain: `out.once('error', (e) => { for (const s of [framing, gzip, cipher]) s.destroy(e); })`, and race `failed` (plus outFailed) in writeEntryFile's file-read promise. Alternatively build the write path with stream/promises pipeline(framing, gzip, cipher, sink) and keep the try/catch around it. Add a test with a destination that errors mid-stream.

title: Expected failures (wrong passphrase, damaged file, non-empty destination) crash with a raw Node stack trace
content: readBackup deliberately throws coded BackupFormatError values (NOT_A_BACKUP, WRONG_PASSPHRASE_OR_DAMAGED, CORRUPT) so that callers can print a friendly message, but neither call site (line 321 in --extract mode, line 361 in the rehearsal) nor main() catches them. `await main()` rejects at the top level. A wrong passphrase is the most likely failure of a tool the owner runs rarely and after a disaster.
failure_scenario: `ANASAQ_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE=wrong node scripts/restore-check.mjs x.enc --extract <dir>` printed `file:///C:/.../backup-format.mjs:84 ... BackupFormatError: Decryption failed: wrong passphrase or damaged file. at Gunzip.<anonymous> ... Node.js v24.19.0` (a source excerpt plus stack, no readable summary). In rehearsal mode the same happens after `supabase stop` and `supabase init` have already run and the exit cleanup runs another `supabase stop`. Missing file, non-empty destination directory and a truncated file end the same way.
fix: Wrap the body of main() (or the two readBackup calls) in try/catch. For BackupFormatError, print `error.message` to stderr and set exitCode = 1. Optionally run the decrypt before `supabase stop`/`supabase init` so a wrong passphrase costs no CLI calls.

title: Argument loop treats --help/-h and unknown flags as the backup file; a missing --extract value silently starts a full rehearsal
content: The first argument that is not `--extract` becomes the backup file, so the help branch (`args[i] === '--help' || '-h'`) is only reachable as a second positional and `--help` never prints usage. The check on line 50 (`!backupFile || extractArg === ''`) also lets `--extract` as the last argument through with extractArg undefined, so the script falls back to the full Docker rehearsal instead of refusing. backup.mjs has the same hole at line 41: `--out` as the last argument leaves outArg undefined, so the file is written to ~/ANASAQ-backups rather than the requested directory.
failure_scenario: `pnpm restore-check --help` prompts for the passphrase, then runs `supabase stop --project-id anasaq-restore-check` and `supabase init`, and only then fails with ENOENT for a file named `--help`. `pnpm restore-check backup.enc --extract` (or `--extract $env:UNSET_VAR` expanding to nothing) starts Docker and a multi-minute rehearsal instead of extracting. `pnpm backup --out $env:USB` with an empty variable writes the backup to the home directory while the owner believes it went to the USB drive.
fix: Handle `--help`/`-h` before positional assignment, reject any other argument starting with `-`, and treat a missing value (args[++i] undefined or starting with `-`) as usage(2), in restore-check.mjs and backup.mjs.

title: --extract writes the plaintext dumps with default permissions (directory 0755, files 0644) on POSIX
content: S17.4 and G1.4 keep the plaintext out of the repository, and the code comments treat it as highly sensitive (auth password hashes, TOTP secrets, customer records). readBackup itself creates the destination and every file with Node's defaults: mkdir with mode 0o777 and createWriteStream with 0o666, both reduced only by the umask. The default rehearsal is protected because mkdtempSync makes a 0700 parent, but `--extract <dir>` uses a user-chosen directory created by these calls. The docs list macOS/brew as a supported platform.
failure_scenario: On a shared Mac or Linux machine, `pnpm restore-check backup.enc --extract ~/restore` leaves ~/restore (0755) with data.sql and roles.sql (0644). Another local account reads the auth password hashes, TOTP secrets and customer records until the owner deletes the directory. On Windows the user-profile ACL protects it, so the exposure is only on multi-user POSIX hosts.
fix: Create the destination with `mkdir(destDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` (line 219, also line 382 for sub-directories) and open entry files with `createWriteStream(dest, { mode: 0o600 })` (line 383).

title: AUDIT-1 G4.6 regression: allowlist again runs `node dist/cli.js` and `graft-dev` without a prompt
content: AUDIT-1 G4.6 was recorded as fixed by deleting `Bash(graft-dev:*)` and `Bash(node dist/cli.js:*)`. The committed HEAD version has neither. The uncommitted working-tree version (rewritten by a graft re-init today at 17:25) has both again. `git diff HEAD -- .claude/settings.json` shows them as `+` lines. This repository has no `dist/`, and `.gitignore` does not cover `dist/cli.js`. The entries belong to graft's own development tree, not to this project.
failure_scenario: In acceptEdits mode, where edits are auto-approved, an agent steered by injected content (a web page, a scraped file) writes `dist/cli.js`, then runs `node dist/cli.js`. The allowlist skips the Bash permission prompt, so arbitrary code runs as the owner, with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and the other environment secrets available. The next `git add -A` or `git commit -a` also makes the regression permanent in `main`.
fix: Restore the file from HEAD (`git checkout -- .claude/settings.json`), or delete only lines 86-87 and keep the deliberate settings. Stop re-running `graft init` on this tree, or review its diff before committing.
note: graft session-start hook rewrote the working tree

title: verify-plan currently fails: the frozen AGENTS.md was rewritten by an uncommitted graft re-init
content: `PLANS/evidence/source-manifest.json` freezes AGENTS.md at 5304 bytes with sha256 ee7567f5.... `git show HEAD:AGENTS.md` matches that hash. The working-tree AGENTS.md is 5200 bytes with sha256 0268cf0d..., so this script throws before writing planning-checks.json. I hashed all 162 manifest entries; AGENTS.md is the only mismatch. The cause is the uncommitted `graft init` rewrite of the tool-managed block (`git diff -- AGENTS.md`: 15 lines changed). The plan's own gate is red in the current tree, and commit 4f22b78 said verify-plan passed.
failure_scenario: An acceptance run that executes `verify-plan.ps1` in this tree fails with 'Changed bytes: AGENTS.md'. If someone re-records the manifest to make it pass, the graft-generated text becomes the plan's frozen source. Any later graft upgrade will break the gate again, because the whole file is frozen while a third-party tool owns part of it.
fix: Run `git checkout -- AGENTS.md` (and the other tooling files touched by the re-init) so verify-plan passes. To stop it recurring, keep the graft block out of the hashed bytes, or stop running `graft init` against this repository.

title: AUDIT-1 S18.4 regression: graft MCP server is unpinned again (`npx -y @nanonets/graft`)
content: S18.4 pinned the MCP server, and HEAD has `@nanonets/graft@0.21.1`. The working tree drops the version: `git diff HEAD -- .mcp.json` shows `-"args": ["-y", "@nanonets/graft@0.21.1", "mcp"]` replaced by an unpinned spec. D19 requires pinned tooling. The drift is already visible on this machine. The npx cache holds graft 0.21.1, the global install is 0.16.0, and today's re-init rewrote AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, settings.json and both helper scripts from a different template than HEAD.
failure_scenario: Every session start runs `npx -y @nanonets/graft mcp`, which resolves whatever `latest` is at that moment and executes it. It inherits the owner's environment, including CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (used by `.mcp.json`'s cloudflare-api server). A compromised or breaking upstream release therefore runs unreviewed code with that token in scope, and a new release can rewrite the tracked config files again, as happened today.
fix: Restore `"@nanonets/graft@0.21.1"` in args (`git checkout -- .mcp.json`), and bump the pin deliberately.
note: graft session-start hook rewrote the working tree

title: Exclusion of 1.1 GB of source assets, including the children's films, exists only in the untracked .git/info/exclude
content: Only `/BOOK_ASSETS/ANAS_WHATSAPP_CHAT/` is ignored by the tracked `.gitignore`. `git check-ignore -v BOOK_ASSETS/SORTED_2026-09-21/01-started-here/videos/46-kid-picnic-jam.mp4` reports `.git/info/exclude:8`. That file also excludes `BOOK_ASSETS/v2-design/`, `v3-art/` and `v4-art/`, and it is per-clone and never cloned. Together these are 397M + 17M + 479M + 255M. `git ls-files BOOK_ASSETS` tracks only 64 files. The SORTED folder holds the five child films (46-50) that AUDIT-1 G4.2 keeps out of the site until guardians consent. `prepare-media.mjs` describes these sources as 'git-excluded', which is true only on this one clone.
failure_scenario: The history was rewritten and re-cloned on 09-30 (D42). On any fresh clone or second machine where the owner copies BOOK_ASSETS back in, `git status` lists SORTED_2026-09-21 as untracked. One `git add -A` then commits the unconsented children's videos plus about 1.1 GB of binaries. Removing them again needs another history rewrite, as D42 already required for the WhatsApp export.
fix: Add `/BOOK_ASSETS/SORTED_2026-09-21/`, `/BOOK_ASSETS/v2-design/`, `/BOOK_ASSETS/v3-art/`, `/BOOK_ASSETS/v4-art/` (and `/artifacts/anas-questions/`) to `.gitignore`, next to the WhatsApp rule.

title: Regenerated multi-agent config files are untracked and unignored, undoing commit 4f22b78's cleanup
content: Commit 4f22b78 deleted `.adal`, `.cursor`, `.gemini`, `.grok`, `.kiro`, `.windsurf`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `opencode.json` on the owner's instruction ('one source of truth, remove all noises'). A graft re-init recreated all of them at 17:25 today, and `git status` lists them as untracked. Nothing in `.gitignore` covers them. The ESLint ignores for them were removed in the same commit, so they would also be linted (a lint run on `.cursor/hooks/graft-hooks.cjs` exits 0, so nothing breaks yet).
failure_scenario: The next `git add -A` or `git commit -a` in this tree commits 9 tool-config paths that the owner just had removed. Their copies of the graft hook and MCP config drift from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, which is the reason 4f22b78 gave for deleting them.
fix: Delete the untracked directories and files, or add `/.adal/`, `/.cursor/`, `/.gemini/`, `/.grok/`, `/.kiro/`, `/.windsurf/`, `/GEMINI.md`, `/opencode.json` and `/.github/copilot-instructions.md` to `.gitignore`.
note: graft session-start hook rewrote the working tree

title: Graft's per-prompt hook is back next to codegraph's, against CLAUDE.md and the token-budget rule
content: CLAUDE.md says to use Graft or CodeGraph, 'not redundant queries to both', and I24 forbids token waste. Commit c222225 removed graft's `prompt` UserPromptSubmit hook, leaving only `codegraph prompt-hook`. The working tree adds the graft hook back, so both tools now inject context into every user prompt. `graft-hooks.cjs prompt` runs `graft ask <prompt> . --json -n 3` (dist/claude/hooks.js:473).
failure_scenario: Every prompt pays for two retrieval packs and an extra process spawn of up to the 15 s (in the file's own units) hook budget. The owner has already complained about wasted tokens.
fix: Delete the second UserPromptSubmit entry (lines 46-53), or restore the file from HEAD.
note: graft session-start hook rewrote the working tree

title: Hook timeouts are written in milliseconds, but Claude Code reads them as seconds
content: Every hook here uses values of 8000 to 15000. The official plugins installed under `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json` use 5, 10 and 90, which are seconds. Graft's generator writes ms-sized numbers, so none of the five hooks has a real cap. The values are 10000, 8000, 15000, 8000 and 8000, at lines 22, 33, 52, 63 and 74.
failure_scenario: A hook that hangs (for example `npm root -g` behind a locked Windows npm cache, or graft waiting on a lock) blocks the prompt, the tool call or the Stop for up to 8000-15000 seconds (2-4 hours) instead of the intended 8-15 seconds. The helper swallows import errors, but not a hung child process.
fix: Use seconds: 10, 8, 15, 8, 8. Because graft regenerates the file, re-apply after any re-init.

title: `Bash(npx graft:*)` allows an unrelated registry package when graft is not resolvable
content: The graft CLI is `@nanonets/graft`, and its binary is `graft`, which is already allowed by `Bash(graft:*)`. `npm view graft` returns an unrelated package, graft@0.3.1 'Full-Stack JavaScript Through Microservices'. `npx graft` resolves the spec `graft` from the registry when no local bin named graft is found in the project. The entry existed at HEAD and AUDIT-1 did not cover it.
failure_scenario: On a machine or cloud session where graft is not installed inside the project (a fresh Linux clone), an agent following AGENTS.md's `graft map` types `npx graft map`. The allowlist runs the unrelated npm package without a prompt, with the owner's environment.
fix: Delete `Bash(npx graft:*)`; `Bash(graft:*)` already covers the real binary.

title: The Edge Function entrypoints are never linted or type-checked by lint, typecheck, tests or CI
content: `supabase/functions/**` is ignored by ESLint (this line) and excluded by tsconfig.json line 51. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no Deno step. I grepped `src/`, `tests/` and `scripts/` for imports of `functions/*/index`, and there are none, so nothing pulls the six entrypoints into the tsc program. The shared modules are covered only through their importers. `supabase/functions/staff-admin/index.ts` (126 lines) is the owner step-up and role-change endpoint; five other wrappers are 5 lines each. They compile only when `supabase functions serve` or a deploy runs them, and `test:db`/e2e are not run in CI.
failure_scenario: A wrong property name, a missing import or a type error in `staff-admin/index.ts` passes `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and the whole CI job (all green). It surfaces only as a 500 or a boot failure in a local integration run, or after deploy.
fix: Add a CI step running `deno check supabase/functions/*/index.ts` (setup-deno, using each function's deno.json import map), or a Deno-typed tsc project for that folder.

title: Second copy of base32Decode/totpCode silently accepts invalid characters
content: `base32Decode`, `totpCode`, `createStaff`, `serviceClient`, `anonClient` and `uniqueEmail` exist in both this file and tests/integration/support.ts. The two `base32Decode` copies have diverged. The integration copy throws on an invalid character (support.ts:90-91). This copy does `indexOf(char)` and gets -1, and `(-1).toString(2).padStart(5, '0')` is `'000-1'`, so non-binary characters enter the bit string and `parseInt` yields a wrong byte. The e2e callers pass raw `innerText()` of `[class*="secret"]` with no trim (auth.spec.ts:35, owner-operations.spec.ts:647).
failure_scenario: If the secret element ever renders a trailing newline, a space, or grouped text, the helper computes a wrong 6-digit code with no error. `mfa.verify` then fails with an invalid-code message. The failure looks like an app or auth regression instead of a test-helper fault.
fix: Move the shared helpers into one module (for example tests/support/totp.ts), keep the throwing variant, and trim the secret text before decoding.

title: The privacy gate for the published book preview is made of `assert` statements
content: `verify()` is the only guard that proves the public PDF holds no JavaScript, action, attachment, link, email or metadata and that its text equals the approved source. Every check is an `assert`. Python strips assertions under `-O` or `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1`. The docstring and AUDIT-1 S15.4 treat the output as sanitized and hash-recorded. The current file passes: I grepped the published PDF for /Author, /Info, /Metadata, /URI, /Annots, /JavaScript and emails and found none, and its sha256 equals content/book-source-manifest.json.
quote: assert EMAIL.search(data) is None, "an email address is left in the preview"
failure_scenario: If the script runs with PYTHONOPTIMIZE set (some Python images and CI wrappers set it), `verify()` does nothing. A Word export whose metadata carries the author's email is then written to public/book/khous-preview.pdf and recorded in the manifest as verified.
fix: Replace the asserts in `verify()` with `if ...: sys.exit(...)` or `raise RuntimeError(...)`, which are not stripped.

title: publish_due now drops a failed schedule for good, and nothing in the product shows the failure
content: The S01.2 fix isolates each scheduled row, and on failure it clears publish_at and writes a content.publish_due_failed audit row. The comment at line 244 and docs/operations.md say this is "so the owner can see it". No screen reads audit_events. The UI's only RPC and table readers are staff_directory, job_runs_latest, outbox_attention, content_documents and similar, and there is no audit view. The failure is therefore invisible to the owner, and the schedule is destroyed. Before the fix the row stayed scheduled and retried every minute, so fixing the cause (for example renaming the clashing post) published it automatically. After the fix the owner's intent is lost. The failing case is easy to hit: the post-slug unique index is only enforced on published_documents, so two drafts with the same slug both schedule fine, and the second fails at its due time (src/lib/admin-publish.ts checks the slug clash only at interactive publish).
quote:
exception when others then
      update public.content_versions
      set publish_at = null
failure_scenario: Post A is live with slug "riyadh-notes". The editor drafts post B with the same slug and schedules it for 09:00 (schedule_version does not check the live slug index). At 09:00 publish_due runs content_go_live(B), which hits published_documents_post_slug (23505). The handler nulls B's publish_at and writes content.publish_due_failed. content_documents now shows B unscheduled with no live copy, and no page shows why. The owner learns of it only by noticing the post is missing, or by querying audit_events by hand.
fix: Make the failure visible where the owner already looks. In the handler also insert a finance.job_runs row (job 'content_publish', status 'failed', detail with collection, doc_id and sqlstate). Add 'content_publish' to KNOWN_JOBS in src/components/admin/AdminHome.tsx so job_runs_latest surfaces it. Alternatively keep publish_at and push it back with a retry cap. Correct the comment and the runbook, which say the owner can see the audit row.

title: S07.6 fixed only for the staff-row lookup; a transient Auth failure in getClaims is still reported as 401 UNAUTHENTICATED
content: S07.6's root cause is "a server fault is reported as unauthenticated", so a caller such as StatsView.tsx:53 (which maps UNAUTHENTICATED to the 'forbidden' owners-only message) shows the wrong page. The fix throws for the failed staff query but leaves the sibling path in the same function. In supabase-js getClaims, any AuthError is returned as { data: null, error } rather than thrown. That includes AuthRetryableFetchError from a network failure or a 5xx from Auth, whether raised by the JWKS fetch or by the getUser fallback used for HS-signed tokens. Line 36 folds every such error into return null. Both admin.ts and staff-admin then answer 401 UNAUTHENTICATED for a valid token during an Auth blip.
failure_scenario: The owner opens the stats page while Supabase Auth answers 503. getClaims returns { error: AuthRetryableFetchError }. staffFromRequest returns null. handleAdmin replies 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. StatsView.tsx:53 maps that to 'forbidden', and the owner is shown the owners-only message. TeamView shows 'سجّل الدخول أولًا' and pushes a needless re-login. The actual state is a temporary server fault on a valid session.
fix: Import isAuthRetryableFetchError from @supabase/supabase-js. When error is set and isAuthRetryableFetchError(error) is true, throw new Error('AUTH_UNAVAILABLE') so handleAdmin and staff-admin answer 500 FAILED, and keep return null only for a genuinely invalid or expired token.

title: The 2xx-only filter also drops 304 revalidations, so repeat visits vanish from 'most requested pages'
content: S07.1 filters top paths to edgeResponseStatus in [200, 300) to remove 404 scans and redirects. Cloudflare Pages serves the static HTML with no cache override (public/_headers sets Cache-Control only for /admin, /_next/static and similar). Pages' default for HTML is a must-revalidate policy with an ETag, so a returning visitor's browser sends a conditional request and the edge answers 304. A 304 has edgeResponseStatus 304, which the new filter excludes, so every repeat page view is missing from the count. The ranking then reflects first visits and hard reloads, and it can reorder the owner's list.
failure_scenario: /journal/riyadh-notes is read 40 times by 10 first-time visitors and 30 returning ones. The 30 returning views are 304s and are not counted, so it shows 10. /store, read 15 times by first-time visitors, shows 15 and ranks above it. The owner's list misranks the pages people actually come back to.
fix: Count 200 and 304 only. Replace the two range filters with edgeResponseStatus_in: [200, 304] (or an OR of the two statuses). Redirects (3xx other than 304), 404 and 5xx stay excluded.

title: Saving while a local copy is on offer leaves the offer pending and switches autosave off for the rest of the session
content: The S08.2 fix stops autosave whenever `localOffer` is non-null, but `save()` never clears `localOffer`. `save()` calls `clearStoredDraft()`, so the offered copy is deleted from localStorage while the banner and the in-memory `localOffer` stay. From then on the autosave effect returns at its first line on every change. It does not write, and it does not remove the key. This brings back the S08.3 data loss (text typed and lost on tab close), and the banner still offers to restore a copy that is no longer stored. The same guard also means that edits typed before the banner is answered are never protected.
failure_scenario: 1) A previous crash left a local copy, so the document opens with the banner «يوجد تعديل غير محفوظ محليًا لهذا المستند». 2) Anas ignores the banner, edits a paragraph and clicks «حفظ». 3) save() inserts the version and runs clearStoredDraft(), but localOffer stays set. 4) He keeps writing for ten minutes and closes the tab. The effect returned early on every keystroke, so nothing was written and no copy is offered on the next visit. The ten minutes of text are lost. If he clicks «استعادة النسخة غير المحفوظة» instead, the old text silently replaces the newer saved text in the form.
fix: In save(), after a successful insert, call setLocalOffer(null) and setStaleBase(null). To also protect edits made before the offer is answered, keep the offer in state only and let autosave write under the normal key once it has been shown, instead of skipping while localOffer is set.

title: Image and video id checks still use `in`, the same inherited-key hole S08.10 fixed for room ids
content: S08.10 replaced `docId in roomSchemas` with `Object.hasOwn` because `in` accepts `constructor`, `toString` and `__proto__`. The image and video id schemas in the same module keep the `in` test against plain JSON objects, so those names validate as known manifest ids. The images field is a free-text input with a datalist, so any typed string reaches the schema. Both schemas feed every image/video field: rooms, scenes, posts, product covers and the media form.
quote:
.refine((id) => id in imageManifest || isMediaId(id), { message: 'معرّف صورة غير معروف.' })
const videoIdSchema = z.string().refine((id) => id in videoManifest, { message: 'معرّف فيديو غير معروف.' })
failure_scenario: An image or video field is set to `constructor` or `toString`, for example by paste. schemaFor(...).safeParse succeeds and the document can be saved and published. On the public site, imageSources('constructor') reads manifest['constructor'] (the Object function), finds no derivatives and returns null, so the slot renders no picture with no build error. VideoTile gets a truthy entry with undefined width, poster and file and renders a broken player. The build never flags the bad id, which is what the 'Missing image manifest entry' guard is meant to do.
fix: Use Object.hasOwn(imageManifest, id) and Object.hasOwn(videoManifest, id) in both refinements (the public lookups in src/lib/images.ts and VideoTile.tsx can get the same guard).

title: Validation error labels drop the list index and the nested field, so the failing item cannot be found
content: The X3.21 fix replaces the whole path with the label of `path[0]`. For list and group fields (rooms `movements`, `items`, `photos`; scenes `photos`), every error becomes the list label plus the Zod message. The item number and the inner field, which the old `issue.path.join('.')` output carried, are gone. The errors still disable «نشر» through `savedParsed`, so the owner has to search every item by hand.
failure_scenario: The scenes gallery has 30 photos and photo 17 has an unknown image id. The form lists «المشاهد: معرّف صورة غير معروف.» and Publish stays disabled. Nothing says which of the 30 items or which of its fields is wrong. Before the fix the line began with `scenes.16.…`, which at least gave the index.
fix: Build the label from the whole path: top-level label, then the 1-based index for numeric segments, then the nested field's label (walk `field.fields` for group and list). For example «المشاهد › 17 › الصورة: …».

title: save() and renameFolder() write the stale `selected` after an await, overwriting a different image chosen meanwhile
content: Both handlers close over `selected` and set it again after awaiting the network. Nothing blocks choosing another tile while a save or rename is in flight (only the «حفظ» button is disabled by `saving`). When the request returns, `setSelected({ ...selected, ...patch })` re-selects the old image, and `setValues` merges the old image's name and folder into the form of the image just chosen. The next «حفظ» updates the old image's row (`.eq('id', selected.id)`) with the other image's alt text, caption and rights.
quote:
setSelected({ ...selected, ...patch })
    setValues((previous) => ({ ...previous, folder: parsed.data.folder, name: parsed.data.name }))
failure_scenario: Anas edits image A and clicks «حفظ», then clicks tile B before the request returns. select(B) fills the form with B's values. When A's update completes, selected becomes A again (the heading shows A's name) while the form still holds B's alt, caption and rights, with A's name and folder written over B's. He fixes one word and clicks «حفظ». Image A's row is overwritten with B's alt text, caption and rights, and neither the message nor the heading reveals it. renameFolder() at lines 437-439 has the same pattern.
fix: After the await, apply the result only if the selection is unchanged: use `setSelected((current) => (current?.id === selected.id ? { ...current, ...patch } : current))`, and guard setValues the same way (compare against a ref holding the current selected id). Alternatively disable the tiles while `saving` or a rename is running.

title: A failed quote refresh leaves the old summary live, submit enabled, and no way to retry
content: AUDIT-1 S14.3 replaced the whole-form error with an inline warning, but only the quote === null case got a retry button (lines 421-430). When a quote already exists and a later refresh fails, the summary keeps showing the old quote, the warning at lines 663-667 says "أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات", and nothing on screen can retry: the debounced effect only reruns when [ready, cart, city, coupon] change, and refreshQuote() is called only from the quote-null view and from POLICY_CHANGED. `stale` is also defined as `!quoteFailed && ...`, so it is false exactly when the refresh failed. That defeats S14.8's own guard: the submit button stays enabled and submit() proceeds against a quote priced for a different city or coupon. The old quoteHash no longer matches, so the function answers QUOTE_CHANGED. That refusal consumes one of the five hourly `checkout:email` throttle takes, which run before pricing in checkout_create. The QUOTE_CHANGED handler then calls setQuote() but never clears quoteFailed or updates quoteKey, so the failure alert stays next to a fresh quote. CartView.tsx:161 has the same warning with no retry control.
quote: const stale = quote !== null && !quoteFailed && quoteKey !== currentKey
failure_scenario: Buyer has a physical cart with a good quote, then switches the city select. The quote request fails once (5xx or a network blip). The alert appears, the old shipping row stays, and submit stays enabled. There is no retry control, and applyCoupon() with the same code is a no-op. Pressing «تأكيد الطلب» sends the old quoteHash with the new city, gets 409 QUOTE_CHANGED and burns a create attempt. The only way to retry is «تعديل السلة» or a reload, and both discard the typed email, name, phone and address.
fix: Treat a failed refresh as stale: `stale = quote !== null && quoteKey !== currentKey`, and disable submit while quoteFailed. Render an «أعد المحاولة» button beside the inline warning that calls refreshQuote() (and one in CartView). In the QUOTE_CHANGED branch also call setQuoteFailed(false) and setQuoteKey(currentKey).

title: Coupon field has no maxLength; a >64-char value makes every quote fail and the persisted value dead-ends /checkout
content: The function caps couponCode at 64 (quoteSchema and createSchema in _shared/checkout.ts), and a 422 INVALID makes fetchQuote() throw, which the form treats as a generic quote failure. Neither coupon input (this one, and CartView.tsx:272) has maxLength. applyCoupon() also writes the value to sessionStorage under COUPON_KEY. On the next load of /checkout the saved coupon is restored before the first quote, so the request fails with quote === null. The S14.3 view shown then contains only the message and «أعد المحاولة», which repeats the same failing request. The coupon field is not rendered in that view, so the buyer cannot fix the cause.
failure_scenario: The buyer pastes a whole WhatsApp line containing a code (more than 64 chars) into the cart coupon box and presses «تطبيق». The cart quote fails with a generic alert. If a good quote was already on screen, the «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب» link is still shown. On /checkout the persisted coupon fails every quote, so the buyer sees only «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» and a retry that always fails, with no coupon field to clear.
fix: Add maxLength={64} to both coupon inputs. Optionally drop a saved coupon when the quote fails with quote === null, or render the coupon field in the failure view.

title: Hold and cancel results are still not conveyed: focus lands on a group named only by the order number
content:
AUDIT-1 S14.5 is fixed by focusing the order box after create or cancel. The box is role="group" with aria-labelledby pointing at the order-number paragraph only. The hold text at line 399 is a plain

with no role. The cancel result at lines 390-392 is a role="status" paragraph that is mounted already filled in the same render that mounts the box. This is the pattern the same commit treats as missed by screen readers when it fixes X3.12 (AddToCart) and S13.5 (VideoTile) by keeping the region mounted. With focus on the group, the announcement is its name and role, not the paragraphs inside it.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader buyer confirms the order and hears "رقم الطلب: ABCDEFGH, مجموعة". They never hear that it is a 20-minute hold with no charge. After «إلغاء الطلب» they hear the same label, not «أُلغي الطلب.».
fix: Give the group aria-describedby pointing at the hold/closed paragraph ids (or fold the message into the labelledby text). Alternatively keep one always-mounted role="status" paragraph in the order box and only change its text.

title: ACTIVE_HOLD with no pending order in this tab still says «أكمله أو ألغه أولًا», which the page cannot do
content: S14.9 persisted the idempotency key so an identical retry after a lost reply replays the order. Any change to the request (one address typo, or a price change that moves quoteHash) changes the digest, so a new key is minted. The function's ACTIVE_HOLD guard matches on email hash or checkout session, not on key. When readPendingOrder() is null (the reply was lost), the branch falls through to the generic server message. That message tells the buyer to complete or cancel a hold the page has no token for. This is the exact complaint of S14.9, and it remains for any non-identical retry.
failure_scenario: Create succeeds on the server but the reply is lost. The buyer notices a typo in the address, fixes it and resubmits. This is a new fingerprint and a new key, so the function returns 409 ACTIVE_HOLD. The page shows «لديك طلب قيد الانتظار؛ أكمله أو ألغه أولًا.» with no order box and no cancel. The buyer is locked out until the 20-minute hold expires.
fix: When ACTIVE_HOLD arrives and readPendingOrder() is null, show a specific message: «لديك طلب محجوز من محاولة سابقة؛ أعد إرسال البيانات نفسها كما كانت، أو انتظر 20 دقيقة.» Do not reuse the server text that names actions the page lacks.

title: A capped (partial) add is still confirmed as a full add
content: S06.8 ("confirms an add that addLine refused or capped") is fixed only for the case where nothing changes. addLine clamps the merged quantity to 20, so adding 5 to a line already at 18 adds 2. cartCount(next) then differs from cartCount(cart), the refusal branch is skipped, and the status says «أُضيف إلى السلة. في السلة الآن N.» with N the total across all lines. The buyer is never told that only part of the request was added.
failure_scenario: The cart holds 18 of variant X. The buyer enters 5 and presses «أضف إلى السلة». Only 2 units are added (capped at 20), but the note reads «أُضيف إلى السلة. في السلة الآن 20.», so the buyer believes 5 more were added.
fix: Compare the requested quantity with the delta: `const added = cartCount(next) - cartCount(cart)`. If added < quantity, say that only `added` were added and that the maximum is 20 per product.

title: The intro picture is dropped when the first band line is the last block of the intro
content: The S13.2 fix claims (lines 85-87) that the film and the poster are each "drawn exactly once, whatever band lines the owner sets". posterAt is texts.find((i) => i > firstBand), which is undefined when no text block follows the first band. This happens when the owner marks the intro's last paragraph as a band line, which the admin allows. Then no TextRun gets figure={room.intro.vignette}, and the poster is never rendered at all. The other two cases, no band and a mid-intro band, work.
quote: const posterAt = firstBand === -1 ? texts[texts.length - 1] : texts.find((i) => i > firstBand)
failure_scenario: In the admin, Anas adds the final intro paragraph to bandLines. intro becomes [text, band]. firstBand is 1, texts is [0], and posterAt is undefined. The page shows the film under the band but the vignette picture has disappeared from /built.
fix: Fall back to the last text when none follows the band: `texts.find((i) => i > firstBand) ?? texts[texts.length - 1]`.

title: Admin draft preview of a post still shows the stock «المجلس» crumb after the journal is renamed
content: The G3.1 fix makes the journal name editable (D11) through getJournalName(). PostView defaults journalName to 'المجلس', and the only caller that omits it is the admin's draft preview (RoomPreview.tsx:69). The published page and the preview then disagree, although shapePost was introduced so they cannot differ.
quote: export function PostView({ post, journalName = 'المجلس' }: { post: JournalPost; journalName?: string }) {
failure_scenario: Anas renames the menu item to «المدونة». The live post page shows «→ المدونة» in the crumbs. His draft preview of the next post still shows «→ المجلس», so he cannot check the real header.
fix: Have the admin preview read the /journal nav label from the site settings it already loads and pass it as journalName, or at least pass the same value BookView's preview gets.

title: A second failed retry drops keyboard focus to <body> again
content: The retry fix moves focus from «إعادة المحاولة» to the loading status region. If the open fails again, setFailed(true) unmounts that focused status div and mounts the alert view. The effect only focuses in the loading state (`!failed`), and nothing focuses the new retry button or alert. Focus falls to <body>, the same defect S15.3 fixed for the mode toggle.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user presses Enter on «إعادة المحاولة» and the PDF fails to load again. The focused status node disappears, focus goes to <body>, and the next Tab starts from the top of the page, far above the reader.
fix: When `failed` becomes true and attempt > 0, focus the alert container (tabIndex -1) or the retry button. This is the same ref-and-effect pattern used for the toggle.

title: The text-layer length invariant was deleted from the real-preview test
content: The f38f04d hunk replaced `expect(fixed).not.toMatch(/األ|اآل/)` with the wider regex and deleted `expect(fixed.length).toBe(raw.length)`. That invariant is why fixLigatures can rewrite the text layer in place: it swaps characters inside each pdf.js item, so selection and find offsets still line up with the drawn words. fixLigatures itself was not touched in this commit, so nothing justifies dropping it. The loop over every page of the real PDF was the only test of it. A later change that inserts or removes a character would now pass.
failure_scenario: Someone changes fixLigatures to normalise a hamza by inserting or removing a character. Every text-layer span after it is offset by one, so selection and search land on the wrong letters, and the suite stays green because the equal-length check is gone.
fix: Restore `expect(fixed.length).toBe(raw.length)` inside the loop, next to the new regex assertion.

title: ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE=DESIGN-B is rejected, so the DESIGN-B visual evidence can no longer be written
content: The S21.1 fix routes every spec's screenshots through shotsDir(pkg), which returns the tracked folder only when ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE === pkg. visual.spec.ts:27 calls shotsDir('DESIGN-B'), and its header comment promises the tracked folder for an ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE=DESIGN-B run. The unchanged guard in playwright.config.ts only accepts P\d\d or LETTERS-DIGITS. 'DESIGN-B' matches neither (checked: the regex returns false; 'CLEANUP-1' returns true). The run therefore throws before any test starts. Before the fix, visual.spec.ts wrote to artifacts/acceptance/DESIGN-B/screenshots unconditionally. Now the only way to refresh the accepted design evidence is impossible, and the docs (docs/development.md:299) name DESIGN-B as a supported package.
failure_scenario: An orchestrator runs `ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE=DESIGN-B pnpm test:e2e` to refresh the 50 visual screenshots. Playwright throws 'ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE must look like P06 or CLEANUP-1, got "DESIGN-B"'. Running without the variable sends the shots to test-results/screenshots/DESIGN-B, so artifacts/acceptance/DESIGN-B/screenshots can never be regenerated.
fix: Widen the regex to accept DESIGN-B, for example /^(P\d{2}|[A-Z]+-(\d+|[A-Z]))$/ or /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)?$/. Update the error text to match.

title: The G4.2 fix has no durable guard in check:export, although the acceptance record says it checks for child-film files
content: G4.2 was that the five child films ship in the static export because public/ is copied whole. The fix deletes the posters and manifest keys and edits the fixture, but nothing keeps them out. PLANS/EXECUTION-STATUS.md:296 records 'check:export (51 required files, no secret, no child-film file)'. scripts/check-export.mjs has no such check: it only tests REQUIRED file presence, RTL attributes, secret patterns and the demo guard. The evidence in artifacts/acceptance/AUDIT-1/commands.txt:39 shows a one-off manual scan of out/ for '-kid-'. tests/unit/collections.test.ts:231 says the films are 'not in the content or the public tree at all', but line 232 asserts only the fixture JSON. The mp4s in public/media are git-ignored and produced locally, so a rerun of the old prepare-media, a restored source, or a manual copy would put them back with every gate green.
quote: console.log(`  OK ${REQUIRED.length} required files present; ${scanned} text files scanned, no secrets`)
failure_scenario: Someone copies 46-kid-picnic-jam.mp4 and its poster into public/media and public/images/started, or re-adds the entries to a manifest, then runs `pnpm build && pnpm check:export`. The script prints OK. The child films are published in out/ before guardian consent.
fix: In check-export.mjs fail when any file under out/ has a path matching /(^|[\\/])\d+-kid-/ or the substring '-kid-', and when '-kid-' appears in any out/ text file. Add the same assertion for the public/ tree to the unit test whose comment already claims it.

title: A complete full run still rewrites both manifests without four committed image entries that no generator produces
content: The S18.3 fix only stops the rewrite when some source file is missing. The root cause is that a full run builds imageManifest = {} (line 403) and overwrites the committed manifest, so any committed entry the script does not generate is dropped. public/images/manifest.json holds started-street-4, started-mothers-hands, started-child-door and started-closed-door, with their webp files in public/images/started/. Neither IMAGES nor POSTER_ONLY mentions them (grep finds nothing in the script), and the P01 commit 70be5c9 introduced them. The new consent instruction at lines 156-162 tells the owner to 'rerun this script', which is exactly the full run. tests/e2e/cms.spec.ts:22 uses `started-street-4` as the scene image, and src/admin/fields.ts imageIdSchema only accepts ids that are in this manifest.
failure_scenario: After guardian consent, the owner re-adds the five reels to VIDEOS and runs `node scripts/prepare-media.mjs` with every source present. The guard passes, the manifest is rewritten without the four started-* entries, and cms.spec.ts's scene test fails with 'معرّف صورة غير معروف' for started-street-4. The webp files stay orphaned in public/.
fix: Seed imageManifest from the existing manifest file (as --only and --posters-only do) and overwrite only the generated keys, or add the four entries to IMAGES/POSTER_ONLY with their sources.

title: The S18.4 pin is gone from the working tree, and the per-agent MCP configs 4f22b78 deleted are back unpinned
content: HEAD's .mcp.json pins `@nanonets/graft@0.21.1` (verified on npm), which is the S18.4 / D19 fix. The working-tree .mcp.json runs `npx -y @nanonets/graft mcp` again. `git diff HEAD` shows the args reformatted with no version. The same unpinned command is in the untracked .cursor/mcp.json, .gemini/settings.json, .kiro/settings/mcp.json, .grok/config.toml and opencode.json, which commit 4f22b78 ('no duplicate agent configs') had removed. .claude/settings.json in the working tree also re-adds `Bash(node dist/cli.js:*)` and `Bash(graft-dev:*)` to the allow list. AUDIT-1 G4.6 removed the former as a code-execution risk. A tool rerun (graft init) regenerated all of this.
failure_scenario: The dirty tree is committed with `git add -A` or `git commit -a`. Every future session then downloads and executes whatever `latest` of @nanonets/graft is at that moment (npx -y, no prompt) and the S18.4 and G4.6 fixes are silently reverted. Locally, the six unpinned configs run the latest version now.
fix: Restore the pinned args in .mcp.json (git checkout HEAD -- .mcp.json). Delete the untracked per-agent configs, and add them and `graft init` output to .gitignore or stop rerunning graft init. Revert the .claude/settings.json allow-list additions.
note: graft session-start hook rewrote the working tree

title: totalBytes still counts the five removed child films
content: The G4.2 fix removed five videos from the manifest by hand but left totalBytes unchanged. The 13 remaining entries sum to 41,697,224 bytes, while the field says 58,588,162. The difference, 16,890,938, is exactly the five removed files (1689416+2869213+3201841+4157767+4972701). The field is written by prepare-media.mjs:457 as the sum of the entries, so the committed file no longer matches what the script would produce. docs/design-direction.md:279 likewise still says '55.9 MiB across 18 videos'.
failure_scenario: Anyone or any check that uses totalBytes as the weight budget for public/media reads 55.9 MiB instead of 39.8 MiB. The manifest disagrees with a fresh full run of the script.
fix: Set totalBytes to 41697224 (or regenerate it from the entries) and update the 55.9 MiB / 18 videos sentence in docs/design-direction.md.

title: The fixture change is not applied to an already-seeded database, and its stored doc now fails the build
content: G4.2 removed the five kid video ids from public/media/manifest.json. The admin schema's videoIdSchema (`id in videoManifest`, src/admin/fields.ts) validates every reel, hidden or not. fetchPublishedOrNull runs schema.parse(row.data) before dropHidden. db:import skips any document that is already published unless --force, and no migration strips the ids from stored documents (the audit_fixes migration does not mention them). AUDIT-1 ran `import-content.mjs --force` on its own machine only (commands.txt:17). Any other local or CI database seeded before f38f04d still holds rooms/started with the five hidden reels. The publish gate rejects that document as 'معرّف فيديو غير معروف', and so does the next static build.
failure_scenario: A developer pulls this commit, keeps their earlier `supabase start` database, and runs `pnpm build`. getStartedRoom parses the stored rooms/started document, hits reels[2].id = '46-kid-picnic-jam', and throws a ZodError, so the whole export fails. The plain `pnpm db:import` they run to fix it reports 'skipped 1 already published' and changes nothing.
fix: Add a one-line upgrade note (run `pnpm db:import --force` after pulling) to docs/development.md and HANDOFF. Alternatively, have import-content compare the published data with the fixture and refuse to skip when they differ.

title: A stray Esc keypress silently drops the next passphrase character
content: After an ESC byte, any character that is not '[' or 'O' and is >= ' ' is treated as Alt+key and discarded. A lone Esc keypress (a common reflex in a password prompt) sends a single ESC byte, so the next typed character is thrown away instead of being kept. The prompt echoes nothing, so the owner cannot see it. The tests only cover a lone ESC followed by Enter. Before the S17.5 change only the ESC byte was dropped.
quote: if (escape === 2 || character >= ' ') continue // a sequence starts, or Alt+key
failure_scenario: At `Passphrase (min 12 characters):` the owner taps Esc to 'clear', then types `arabic-owner-1` and Enter. The first character 'a' is dropped, so the backup is encrypted with `rabic-owner-1`. Typing the passphrase correctly during a later restore-check or real restore gives WRONG_PASSPHRASE_OR_DAMAGED, and the backup cannot be opened.
fix: For ESC followed by anything other than '[' or 'O', reset escape to 0 and fall through so the character is handled normally (drop only the ESC, as before). Or reset the swallow state on a timer.

title: Sitewide object-src 'none' also lands on the preview PDF that ClosedBook and the reader error state link to directly
content: The S12.2 fix adds a Content-Security-Policy to `/*`. That rule matches /book/khous-preview.pdf, so the PDF response carries `object-src 'none'`. The site links to that PDF for top-level opening in three places: ClosedBook.tsx:46 (`افتح الصفحات (PDF)`), ClosedBook.tsx:56 (per-part `#page=N` links) and BookPreview.tsx:45 (the reader error fallback `افتح الصفحات ملفاً (PDF)`). Chromium's built-in PDF viewer draws the file through a plugin embed that the response's CSP governs, and Chromium is known to refuse a PDF served with object-src 'none' ('This page has been blocked by Chrome'). The no-JS and error-recovery path to the book would then show a blocked page. I did not reproduce it: _headers is applied only by Cloudflare Pages and headless Chromium has no PDF viewer. PLANS/ARCHITECTURE.md:74 and ISSUES.md:49 call these four directives 'the directives that cannot break a page', but no test opened the PDF in a real browser with the header.
failure_scenario: A visitor in Chrome or Edge with JS disabled, or whose reader failed to load, clicks «افتح الصفحات (PDF)». The browser requests /book/khous-preview.pdf, gets `Content-Security-Policy: object-src 'none'`, and shows a blocked-page error instead of the PDF. The only fallback that does not need pdf.js is dead.
fix: Verify on the Pages preview in Chrome. If confirmed, add a rule below `/*` that removes the header for the PDF only, for example `/book/khous-preview.pdf` with `! Content-Security-Policy`. Otherwise exclude the PDF from the sitewide rule. Add a header assertion for the PDF to the P10 security spec.

title: Owner step-up can be satisfied by a factor enrolled seconds ago in the same aal1 session
content: The step-up is only `aal === 'aal2'` plus any `totp` amr entry from the last 5 minutes (recent-totp.ts). Nothing requires the verified factor to have existed before the current session. MfaEnroll.tsx:47-51 offers enrolment to any signed-in staff session that has no verified factor. The repo's own e2e test documents the consequence at tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts:40-42: "Enrolling just verified a TOTP code, so the session would pass the 5-minute step-up check". staff-admin also lets an owner be created without a factor (`invite` accepts role 'owner' at staff-admin/index.ts:72, `set_role` has no has_totp check, and bootstrap-owner.mjs creates the first owner without one). The second factor therefore protects nothing against the threat it exists for, a stolen or phished aal1 session, for any owner who has not yet enrolled.
quote: return { userId, role, recentTotp: hasRecentTotp(claims ?? {}, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)) }
failure_scenario: An owner exists with no verified TOTP factor: the bootstrap owner before his first visit to /admin/security, or an owner created by `invite` or `set_role`. The attacker holds an aal1 session (a stolen refresh token, or the mailbox that receives the emailed code). They open /admin/security, scan the QR code with their own authenticator and submit a code, which yields a session with aal2 and a fresh totp amr entry. staff-admin now accepts `invite` (new owner), `set_role`, `set_active`, and admin accepts `commerce-settings-save` and `commerce-policies-approve`, the actions D13 reserves for a fresh second factor. Check on the hosted project whether Auth also lets an aal1 session add a second factor when one is already verified. If it does, the same path works for an already-enrolled owner.
fix: In staff-admin, refuse `invite` with role 'owner', and refuse `set_role` to owner unless the target already has a verified TOTP factor (auth.admin.mfa.listFactors or the staff_directory has_totp flag). In staffFromRequest, treat the step-up as satisfied only when the verifying factor's created_at is older than the session start (claims.session_id, read through a service-role SQL function) or older than a fixed delay. Make the first owner enrol TOTP during hosted bootstrap, before the admin is reachable.

title: A publish is validated only in the browser and at build time, and a failed build is reported as success
content: publish_version is granted to `authenticated`, and an owner or editor can insert content_versions rows directly (20260925120000 lines 31-40). The SQL functions store and publish whatever JSON is in the chosen version. The only schema check is the browser's validateVersion (src/lib/admin-publish.ts:60-96, whose header says it is "for the editor's sake") and the build-time Zod parse in src/lib/content.ts:134, which throws. D32 accepts that a failing build keeps the last good deploy. But site_build_trigger records `ok` when the deploy hook answers 2xx (20260927120000_rebuild_delivery_and_media_sweep.sql:50). The hook only queues the build, so a build that then fails is never shown on the owner home (AdminHome KNOWN_JOBS has no build-outcome signal).
failure_scenario: An editor session (or a stolen editor JWT at aal1) POSTs a content_versions row {collection:'site_settings', doc_id:'site', data:{}} and calls rpc/publish_version on it. published_documents now holds {}. Every later Pages build fails in fetchSiteSettings (siteSettingsStoredSchema.parse), so no publish, price change or takedown (for example hiding a photo after a removal request) reaches the site. The owner home keeps showing site_build as `ok` because each deploy-hook call returned 200. Recovery needs someone to notice in the Cloudflare dashboard and re-publish a valid version, and the attacker can repeat it.
fix: Route publishing through the `admin` Edge Function: validate with schemaFor() server-side, then call publish_version as service_role, and revoke it from `authenticated`. Also surface the real build outcome, for example by having a Pages deploy webhook write finance.job_runs('site_build') or by polling the deployment status, so a failed build shows on the owner home.

title: Anonymous sign-in-code spam locks the owner out and burns the shared Resend quota
content: The sign-in page calls Supabase Auth's OTP sender with no CAPTCHA, and nothing in supabase/config.toml enables one ([auth.captcha] is commented out at lines 216-220). The publishable key is shipped in the static JS, and the owner's address is public (site_settings.contact.email on the contact page), so any anonymous caller can make Auth mail a real code to a staff address. `[auth.email] max_frequency = "1s"` (config.toml:236) is the local value, and ISSUES I28 says the hosted project must match the local Auth settings. The outbox reserve (AUDIT-1 S04.1) counts only finance.email_outbox rows: outbox_claim reads sent_at from that table, so mail sent by Auth over the same Resend SMTP account is invisible to it.
failure_scenario: An attacker POSTs {email: <owner address>} to /auth/v1/otp with the publishable key, once per minute (the hosted per-address minimum). Each call mails a valid 6-digit code. Once the project-wide hourly email cap (`[auth.rate_limit] email_sent`) is reached, Auth answers 429 to everyone, so the owner's own request shows RATE_LIMITED_MESSAGE and no code arrives. About 100 such mails also spend Resend's free daily quota (DAILY_QUOTA = 100 in outbox.ts). outbox_claim still sees roughly 80 sends left, so it claims contact notices and Resend answers daily_quota_exceeded. The notices are pushed to the next UTC midnight, where the attacker spends the quota again. D31 makes the owner's mailbox the only inbox, so the contact form goes dark, and admin sign-in is blocked for as long as the attacker keeps sending, for one HTTP request a minute.
fix: Turn on Auth CAPTCHA with the Turnstile provider ([auth.captcha] locally, Authentication > Attack Protection on the hosted project). Reuse useTurnstile in SignIn.tsx and pass options.captchaToken to signInWithOtp. Keep max_frequency at 60 s or more on the hosted project and add both settings to the I28 checklist.

title: Anyone can lock a known email address out of checkout, and ACTIVE_HOLD confirms it has a live order
content: The per-email hold cap and the per-email throttle are keyed on the sha256 of an email the caller merely types (no verification). The `checkout:email` hit is taken before the hold check, and ACTIVE_HOLD is returned rather than raised, so the increment commits. The victim has no access token for the attacker's order, so the victim cannot cancel it. The 20-minute hold plus 5 hits an hour leaves the victim refused for as long as the attacker keeps going. This is separate from the recorded stock-hold residual and from S06.4. It is reachable only once P08 turns checkout on, because CHECKOUT_DISABLED returns before these lines.
quote: or not finance.rate_limit_take('checkout:email', v_email_hash, 5, interval '1 hour')
failure_scenario: Checkout is enabled. An attacker solves one Turnstile and POSTs `create` with victim@example.com and any valid cart. This makes a pending order for 20 minutes. The victim's own `create` gets 409 ACTIVE_HOLD, «لديك طلب قيد الانتظار؛ أكمله أو ألغه أولًا.», with nothing to cancel. The attacker repeats every 20 minutes (3 creates an hour is under the 5-an-hour cap). The victim's refused attempts also raise the same email bucket, so after 5 hits the victim gets 429 for the rest of the hour. The victim is effectively blocked from buying, and the attacker can check whether any address has a live order.
fix: Do not enforce a hold cap or throttle on an unverified email alone. Scope it to (email_hash, ip_hash) or to the checkout session, and count the email throttle only when an order is actually created. If one-hold-per-email is required, verify the address with an emailed code before the first hold.

title: Per-IP throttles key on the full IPv6 address, so one /64 gets unlimited buckets
content: requestIp returns the client address unchanged and clientKeyHash hashes that whole string. A single IPv6 subscriber or VPS controls a whole /64 (2^64 addresses), so every request can present a new address and land in a fresh finance.rate_limits row. The public `quote` action has no Turnstile, so its 300-an-hour per-IP cap (`checkout-quote:ip`) is its only throttle. The 5-an-hour contact cap and the 10-an-hour checkout cap are also per address, though they sit behind Turnstile.
failure_scenario: A script on a /64 sends `quote` requests, each from a random host address. The per-IP limit never trips. Every call runs checkout_price and inserts a new (bucket, key_hash, window_start) row.
