A sustained few hundred requests a second adds tens of millions of rows within the 2-day purge window (rate-limits-purge, 03:17 daily), and it burns Edge Function invocations and database CPU with no per-caller brake.
fix: In requestIp, reduce an IPv6 address to its /64 prefix (first four hextets, after IPv4-mapped normalisation) before hashing, and cap total keys per bucket per window or add Turnstile to `quote` when the caller's bucket is new.

title: The upload-ticket cap is a concurrency cap, so an editor token can fill Storage faster than the sweep can empty it
content: media_create_ticket counts only tickets that are still open and unexpired (5 minutes), so once a ticket expires the slot is free again. Each ticket hands out up to 5 signed upload URLs to the private bucket, and the bucket's 15 MiB limit applies to every part (declared sizes are checked only in media-complete). Nothing rate-limits media-ticket. The daily media_sweep removes at most BATCH x MAX_BATCHES = 100 x 10 = 1000 quarantine objects (media-sweep.ts:11-13).
quote: where t.actor = p_actor and t.completed_at is null and t.expires_at > now()
failure_scenario: A stolen or malicious editor/owner JWT requests 10 tickets, uploads 5 large parts to each and never calls media-complete. After 5 minutes the tickets expire and it repeats. That is about 50 objects and several hundred MiB every 5 minutes, and more than 14,000 objects a day against a sweep that deletes 1000. Storage quota (1 GB free, 100 GB Pro) is exhausted or billed, uploads then fail for the real editors, and the backlog keeps growing.
fix: Add a per-actor rate limit to media_create_ticket (for example count tickets created in the last hour, not only open ones). Raise or remove the sweep batch cap, or loop until no candidates remain. Consider an aggregate quarantine-bytes cap per actor.

title: A personal Gmail address and the Cloudflare account id are committed in acceptance evidence
content: The `wrangler whoami` output was pasted into a tracked artifact. It names the account owner's personal Gmail address together with the Cloudflare account id, and line 141 of the same file adds a Hyperdrive config id. The repository (Ekka-Barber/anas-studio) is private today, and D42 already rewrote history once to remove personal data. The Worker/Hyperdrive stack in this evidence is retired by D32, so the file has no remaining value.
failure_scenario: The repository is made public or shared with a contractor or another tool. Anyone can then pair the account owner's personal email with the Cloudflare account id and use both for targeted phishing or support social engineering against the Cloudflare account that will hold the production site.
fix: Redact the email and ids in this file and in i20-public-read-path.txt (line 230 and 710), and if the repository will ever leave private, include them in the same history rewrite as D42.

title: Quote reports checkoutEnabled true while checkout_create will refuse for seller or policy setup, so the buyer fills the whole form and gets a 503; after AUDIT-1's approval reset the consent line is empty
content: checkout_quote returns checkoutEnabled = finance.commerce_settings.checkout_enabled only. checkout_create additionally refuses with SELLER_NOT_CONFIGURED (seller_legal_name or seller_registration null) and POLICIES_NOT_CONFIGURED (policy_revisions = '{}'), and DATA-AND-SECURITY step 2 says the quote must resolve 'policy setup'. Both client gates read only that one flag: CartView.tsx:336 shows «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب» when quote.checkoutEnabled, and CheckoutForm.tsx:434 renders the whole form when quote.checkoutEnabled. AUDIT-1 X1.1 made this state dynamic: the trigger policies_reset_approval now sets policy_revisions back to '{}' whenever a published policy seq changes (publish_version, or publish_due from a schedule with no owner present), while checkout_enabled stays true. In that state the quote still says checkoutEnabled true with policyRevisions {}; CheckoutForm builds consentPolicies from Object.keys(quote.policyRevisions), so the consent sentence renders as «قرأت  وأوافق عليها» with no links (nothing to consent to) and the buyer can tick it. The refusal only comes at create time, after the buyer has typed contact and address details and solved Turnstile, and the create attempt also spends one of the per-email/per-IP hourly throttle hits. There is no client-side test of policyRevisions being empty (grep of src for policyRevisions/POLICIES_NOT shows only these uses). Currently masked because nothing sets checkout_enabled, but it is the exact state P08's owner switch will produce after any policy edit.
failure_scenario: Store is open (checkout_enabled true, seller named, policies approved at seq 3). Owner schedules or publishes policy 'refund' seq 4; policies_reset_approval sets policy_revisions = '{}'. A buyer opens /cart: quote returns checkoutEnabled true, policyRevisions {} so «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب» is shown. On /checkout the consent checkbox reads «قرأت  وأوافق عليها» with no policy links. The buyer fills email, name, phone, city, address, ticks consent, passes Turnstile and presses «تأكيد الطلب»: checkout_create returns POLICIES_NOT_CONFIGURED and the UI shows «الشراء غير متاح حاليًا، ويفتح قريبًا.» after the form was completed. Same for a store where seller_legal_name was cleared through commerce_settings_save.
fix: In public.checkout_quote (new forward migration with create or replace) return checkoutEnabled = checkout_enabled and seller_legal_name is not null and seller_registration is not null and policy_revisions <> '{}'::jsonb, i.e. the same three gates checkout_create applies in step 2. Optionally also have CheckoutForm treat an empty policyRevisions as closed. Add an integration test that the quote reports false after a policy republish.

title: Cart page never re-reads storage, so an edit made on a stale cart tab overwrites items added in another tab
content: CartProvider reads localStorage once on mount (line 30) and update() writes the whole cart built from that tab's in-memory state (line 36). Unlike CartLink.tsx it has no 'storage' or CART_EVENT listener. AddToCart on a product page in another tab does a read-modify-write of the same key. Any later quantity, dedication or delete edit on the stale /cart tab therefore replaces the stored cart with the stale lines, silently dropping items added elsewhere. The cart's quote is computed from the same stale state, so the missing item is not shown either. The server re-prices whatever lines it receives, so this is not a price error, but the buyer loses cart lines without a message.
failure_scenario: Tab A shows /cart with variant V1. In tab B the buyer opens a product page and presses «أضف إلى السلة» for V2; localStorage now holds [V1, V2]. Back in tab A the buyer presses + on V1: update(setQuantity(cart, V1, 2)) writes [V1 x2] built from tab A's state, so V2 disappears from storage and from the CartLink count, and checkout orders only V1.
fix: In CartProvider subscribe to window 'storage' (other tabs) and re-run readCart() into state, or make update() read the stored cart and apply the mutation to it (mutations are pure functions over CartV1) instead of writing the in-memory copy.

title: Hold view keeps claiming a live 20-minute hold after the hold has expired; the buyer is never told and cannot reorder until pressing cancel
content: PendingOrder (src/lib/cart.ts:346) stores only orderNumber and accessToken, not holdExpiresAt, and the create reply's order.holdExpiresAt is never kept or shown. On mount CheckoutForm restores it with setPending(readPendingOrder()) (line 108) and, whenever pending is non-null and closed is null, always renders the message «حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة...» with only a cancel button; the normal form is replaced. AUDIT-1 S06.7 fixed only the case where a duplicate create reply reports an ended order. A tab that reloads or is revisited after the 20 minutes still shows the live-hold text although availability ignored the hold at expiry and checkout_expire marked the order expired, and the form stays hidden until the buyer presses «إلغاء الطلب» and the round trip returns status expired.
quote: حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة. الدفع يُضاف في المرحلة القادمة، ولن يُخصم أي مبلغ الآن.
failure_scenario: Buyer presses «تأكيد الطلب» at 10:00 (hold to 10:20), leaves the tab open, returns at 13:00 and reloads /checkout: the page shows «رقم الطلب: ABCD2345» and «حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة», implying the stock is still reserved, although the last unit may already have been sold and the order status is expired. They cannot place a new order (the form is replaced) until they find and press «إلغاء الطلب».
fix: Store holdExpiresAt in PendingOrder (writePendingOrder/readPendingOrder) and, when it is in the past, show the closed state «انتهت مدة حجز الطلب.» and clear pending order and idempotency at once; or fetch the status through the existing cancel call/a status call on mount.

title: The built room reads its two stages by position, though the admin lets editors hide, add and reorder them
content: builtRoomFields.movements is a hideable list. FieldInput gives every list «أعلى», «أسفل», «حذف», «إخفاء» and «أضف عنصرًا». The loader applies dropHidden before the view runs. The view takes the first item as the team stage and the second as the branches stage. Roles are never stored: no kind field, and the label is only the heading. A third item is never drawn. This is not the documented 'stage pictures not drawn' exception (D40). It is the text and layout of the room that the hide control is documented to control (rooms.ts header).
failure_scenario: The owner hides «لم أكن وحدي في هذه الحكاية» (index 0) to rework it. After dropHidden, room.movements is [<seven-branches item>]. The branches text renders as the aubergine team band with the team films, and the saffron branches band with its seven triangles disappears. Adding a third stage «محطة جديدة» publishes fine and never appears. Swapping the two with «أسفل» swaps their styling.
fix: Store the role. Add a select field such as `kind` ('team' | 'branches' | 'other') to builtMovementFields and pick with movements.find(m => m.kind === 'team'), rendering 'other' items generically. Otherwise make the list fixed (no hide, add or reorder) and fail publish when it does not have exactly two items. The same positional pattern is at ShelfRoomView.tsx:63 (moon.images), which is not hideable but has no cue about slot order.

title: Items an editor marks hidden stay readable by the public key, including their library images
content: S01.1 hid only posts with visible off. Every other `hidden: true` list item (room movements, reels, brand wall, product gallery, scene photos) is stored inside published_documents.data. That column is anon-readable in full: the policy passes any row that is not a post, and anon has a table-wide select grant. Only the build-time `dropHidden` in src/lib/content.ts removes these items. The publishable key ships in every page, so the build filter is not a boundary. media_published_ids() also walks the whole JSON, so the library rows of hidden scene photos are anon-readable, and their files sit in the public media-public bucket. The G4.2 comment in prepare-media.mjs states the principle that a hidden flag in the content is not enough. It was applied to the five child films only. DESIGN.md:183 still says the child films 'stay hidden until their guardians agree', which treats the flag as the gate. The admin control is just «إخفاء» with no warning.
failure_scenario: Anas hides scene photo X, a library image, while the person in it has not agreed. The published gallery document now holds {image:'<uuid>', category, caption, hidden:true}. Anyone runs GET /rest/v1/published_documents?collection=eq.scenes&select=data with the publishable key from the page source and gets the uuid. GET /rest/v1/media?id=eq.<uuid> returns its derivatives because media_published_ids() counts it. <SUPABASE_URL>/storage/v1/object/public/media-public/m/<uuid>/1800.webp then downloads the 'hidden' photo. A hidden movement's paragraphs in rooms/built leak the same way.
fix: Strip hidden items where the live copy is written. In content_go_live, save published_documents.data with every array element that has hidden = true removed (a small recursive jsonb function). Then anon RLS and media_published_ids() only ever see shown items, and dropHidden becomes a harmless no-op. The admin reads content_versions and content_documents.latest_data, so unhiding still works.

title: Policy approval opens checkout before the site shows the approved text
content: The buyer ticks «قرأت سياسة … وأوافق عليها». The links go to the static pages /policies/<id>, which show whatever revision the last static build baked in. The order records the approved seq numbers. commerce_policies_approve snapshots the seqs currently in published_documents and never checks that a rebuild containing them has been delivered, let alone finished. X1.1 closes checkout when a policy changes. Approving reopens it at once, while the site rebuild (cron every minute, two-minute throttle, then the Pages build) is still running or has failed. Nothing on the page shows which revision it holds, so a buyer cannot tell. I44 (1) covers approving a revision the owner did not read. This is a different gap: the buyer's page lags the approved revision.
quote: select seq into v_store from public.published_documents where collection = 'policies' and doc_id = 'store';
failure_scenario: The owner publishes refund policy seq 5. The approval resets and checkout closes. He approves seq 5 within a minute, since his TOTP is still fresh. Checkout opens with policyRevisions {refund:5}. The rebuild takes about 4 minutes, or fails on an unrelated bad document. Meanwhile /policies/refund still shows seq 4. A buyer reads seq 4 and accepts. The order stores refund:5, a text they never saw.
fix: In commerce_policies_approve, refuse unless finance.job_runs holds a site_build run with status ok whose finished_at is later than the latest published_documents.updated_at of the four policy docs (or unless site_builds.request_id is null and triggered_at > that time). Also print the seq or date on each policy page so the text is tied to the number the order stores.

title: A failed scheduled publish disappears with no visible trace, and the failure is not caught at schedule time
content: S01.2 isolates each due row, which holds. The stated purpose is 'so the owner can see it' (this file, line 244, and docs/operations.md:306). But the only record is an audit_events row, and no screen reads audit_events (grep of src has no consumer). The handler also clears publish_at for every failure, so content_documents.scheduled_at becomes null. The document then reads «تعديلات غير منشورة» or «مسودة لم تُنشر», and the AdminHome scheduled count just drops by one. `when others` catches transient errors as well, such as deadlock or lock timeout, and cancels the schedule permanently. schedule_version never pre-checks the post-slug unique index, so a certain conflict is only found at go-live.
failure_scenario: On Thursday post A is published with slug `eid-notes`. Post B, drafted earlier with the same slug, is scheduled for Friday 09:00 (schedule_version accepts it). At 09:00 publish_due hits 23505, drops B's schedule and writes content.publish_due_failed. Friday's launch post never appears. The list shows «تعديلات غير منشورة», there is no message, and nobody is told unless they query audit_events.
fix: In schedule_version, for collection 'posts' refuse (23505) when another published post already uses the slug, so the editor sees it at schedule time. Show failures in the admin: a `publish_failed_at`/`publish_error` marker in content_documents plus a banner on AdminHome for owner and editor. Limit the catch-all to unique_violation and check_violation, and leave the schedule in place on other errors so the next minute retries.

title: Pasting text that contains a tab produces a node the schema rejects, so publishing is blocked with an unreadable error
content: The editor keeps Lexical's core nodes, including TabNode. In Lexical 0.51 the default text/plain paste importer turns every \t into a `tab` node (`cur.insertNodes([$createTabNode()])` in @lexical/clipboard). Text in <pre> is converted the same way. editorState.toJSON() then holds {type:'tab', text:'\t'}. The allowlist union has no 'tab', and src/lib/richtext.tsx has no case for it. registerAllowlistTransforms is documented as 'so publishing is never blocked by a paste' but handles only h1 and h4-h6 headings and non-https links. CollectionForm prints the failure as `النص: Invalid input`: Zod's English union message, with no position. The tab is invisible.
failure_scenario: An editor pastes a paragraph copied from a notes app, a terminal or a code snippet, indented with a tab, into a post body, a policy or a product description. Save works, since the DB accepts any object. canPublish becomes false. The form shows «النص: Invalid input» and publishPublish stays disabled. The editor cannot find the invisible tab and loses the post's publishing until they retype the text.
fix: Add a node transform for TabNode in registerAllowlistTransforms that replaces it with a text node of spaces (for example four spaces). Also add a 'tab' node to the schema and the renderer if tabs are wanted. Give the union a custom error message in Arabic that names the node type.

title: The failure counter is never reset by a new build request, so after exhaustion a later request gets one try and no retries
content: failures only returns to 0 on a 2xx. Once it reaches 5, the else branch keeps triggered_at, so nothing retries. The next publish arms one attempt. If that attempt fails, failures becomes 6, `failures + 1 < 5` is false, and it is not re-armed. The 'up to five in a row' budget therefore applies to the first failing episode only. Every later request gets exactly one shot. The migration comment and I34 describe 'the next publish tries once more', so this exhaustion is known. The counter not resetting per request is not. There is also no way to rebuild without publishing something (site_build_request is revoked from authenticated).
quote: triggered_at = case when v_row.failures + 1 < 5 then null else triggered_at end
failure_scenario: The Pages deploy hook fails for a few minutes during a Cloudflare incident. failures = 5 and the request is dropped. Later the owner rotates the hook secret in Vault, and still nothing rebuilds. He publishes a post. The one attempt hits a transient 502, failures = 6, no re-arm. The post is live in the database but never built. The home shows «فاشل» until he publishes again.
fix: In site_build_request() set failures = 0 together with requested_at, so each request gets its own five attempts. Optionally retry a dropped request hourly, or add an owner-only rebuild-now action.

title: The publish gate's media check still puts every id in one GET URL
content: S12.5 chunked the build-time lookups (MEDIA_CHUNK = 100, because Cloudflare refuses a URL past 16 KB). The two browser-side lookups were not changed. This one gates publishing, and it fails closed with a generic message. RoomPreview.tsx:117 has the same call and fails the preview.
failure_scenario: A scenes gallery grows to about 420 library photos. Each uuid adds about 39 characters, the URL passes 16 KB and the request fails. validateVersion returns «تعذّر التحقق من صور المكتبة.» and the gallery can never be published again, although the build loader would cope.
fix: Chunk ids in groups of 100 in validateVersion and RoomPreview, as mediaById does in src/lib/content.ts (or export mediaById-style chunking and reuse it).

title: A blank menu label passes publish and blanks the journal's name on every page
content: navItemFields declares label and href as plain `text`, so publish accepts an empty string (`nonBlank` exists since S11.3 but is applied only in the catalog tables). getJournalName falls back with `??`, which does not catch ''. The empty name feeds the journal page's h1 and title, the post pages' back link and the book page's link. The menu itself shows a link with no name. The same holds for home.name, room titles and taglines.
failure_scenario: Anas clears the «المجلس» label in the settings menu list, meaning to retype it, and publishes. The schema passes. After the rebuild /journal has an empty h1 and an empty <title>, and the menu shows a nameless link.
fix: Set `nonBlank: true` on the nav item label and href, home.name and the room title fields. Use `||` in getJournalName so an empty label falls back to «المجلس».

title: Post tags are collected, validated and published but no public page shows them
content: G3.4 removed admin fields that no page reads, from rooms and footer. `tags` was missed. shapePost (journal.ts:56-66) copies no tags, JournalPost has no such field, and no public component references them. The tag taxonomy kind and the tag picker in the post form exist only to feed nothing.
failure_scenario: An editor tags a post «رحى» and publishes. After the rebuild nothing on /journal or /journal/<slug> shows a tag or filters by it, so the editing work does nothing. A taxonomy of kind «وسم» has no effect either.
fix: Either render tags on the post and card, or drop `tags` and the 'tag' option from the post and taxonomy fields until they are used. Stored documents keep validating because Zod strips unknown keys.

title: Saves write the raw form state, so keys of fields that were removed live on and keep library images 'in use'
content: G3.4's fixCorrections asked to check that the editor strips unknown keys on save, because media_published_ids() and media_usage() match any uuid string anywhere in the stored JSON. load() puts latest_data into the form untouched and save() inserts it untouched, so nothing strips them. The fixture was cleaned, but any stored document from before a field removal keeps the old keys in every later version and every republish.
quote: const { error } = await supabase.from('content_versions').insert({ collection, doc_id: docId, seq: nextSeq, data })
failure_scenario: Before G3.4 the owner set the room-level «الصورة الرئيسية» of بدأتُ من هنا to library image L and published. The field is now removed from the form, but `vignette: 'L'` is in the stored data and copied into every new version. L stays anon-readable, media_delete(L) answers 'Media is in use', and the owner cannot clear it because no field is drawn.
fix: Insert `parsed.success ? parsed.data : data` (Zod strips unknown keys). Or run a one-off migration that strips the removed keys from content_versions' latest rows and published_documents.

title: pullLines and bandLines must repeat a paragraph exactly, but nothing checks it and a typo fix silently drops the styling
content: The header says each entry 'must repeat a paragraph exactly'. classify() in src/components/public/story/flow.ts matches with Set.has on the full string. Neither the Zod schema, the publish gate nor the admin form links the two lists, and the admin shows no hint. Editing the paragraph without editing its copy in pullLines turns the large line into ordinary body text. An edited bandLines entry no longer breaks out as a band, and the following text stays in the previous block.
failure_scenario: The owner fixes a typo in the paragraph that is set as the large closing line of بدأتُ من هنا, and publishes. The old spelling still sits in pullLines, so Set.has fails and the line renders small. No error appears anywhere.
fix: Add a superRefine to the room schemas: every pullLines and bandLines entry must equal some paragraph of that room (message «هذا السطر لا يطابق أي فقرة»). Optionally build the two lists as checkboxes on the paragraphs.

title: check:export has no check that guardian-pending films are absent, though the status record says it does
content: PLANS/EXECUTION-STATUS.md:296 reports 'check:export (51 required files, no secret, no child-film file)'. The script has no such check. The zero-match scan of out/ for '-kid-' was a manual step in AUDIT-1's commands.txt. The only automated guard is a unit test that greps the fixture JSON. If a `-kid-` entry is added back to VIDEOS in prepare-media.mjs (the comment says how) before consent, the manifests, public/ files and the export would carry the films and every gate would pass.
quote: * - no file contains a server-side secret. The patterns match secret values,
failure_scenario: During P11 someone restores the five 4x-kid films to prepare-media.mjs to test the reels and runs pnpm build. check:export reports OK because it looks only for secrets, required files and the demo word, and the export ships them.
fix: Add a check in check-export.mjs that fails when any file name or text under out/ contains `-kid-` (or a small denylist read from prepare-media.mjs's comment block), and correct the status text to match what the script really checks.

title: Sign-in and TOTP code inputs do not fold Arabic-Indic digits, so a correct code is rejected
content: The code fields pass the raw typed string to Supabase. The site already folds ٠-٩ and ۰-۹ for phone numbers (saudi-mobile.ts foldDigits) and prices (money-input.ts parseRiyals), so the requirement is known, but the three one-time-code inputs were missed: SignIn.tsx:123 (email OTP), StepUp.tsx:74 and MfaEnroll.tsx:129 (TOTP). `maxLength={6}` counts «١٢٣٤٥٦» as six characters, so it is accepted client-side; GoTrue compares bytes and rejects it.
failure_scenario: The owner's Arabic keyboard layout is active (the number row types ١٢٣٤٥٦ on Arabic layouts). He types the six digits from the email or authenticator. verifyOtp / challengeAndVerify fails and the screen says «الرمز غير صحيح أو انتهت صلاحيته.» although the code was right, and the code may expire while he retries.
fix: Fold both ranges before storing or submitting, e.g. `setCode(toLatinDigits(event.target.value).trim())`, with one shared helper (foldDigits without its separator dropping), applied in SignIn, StepUp and MfaEnroll.

title: Every admin navigation remounts the shell: nav and page vanish, focus resets to body
content: AdminShell is rendered inside each of the 13 admin pages (src/app/(admin)/admin/**/page.tsx) instead of in a shared layout. Next keeps layouts mounted across navigation but remounts pages, so each move between admin screens unmounts the nav, restarts `gate` at `checking`, renders nothing while getSession() and the `current_staff_role` RPC run, and only then draws the nav and <main> again. The link the user just activated is destroyed, so focus falls to <body>. There is no `src/app/(admin)/admin/layout.tsx`; the root `(admin)/layout.tsx` only renders <html><body>.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user on /admin tabs to «المحتوى» and presses Enter. The nav and the page disappear for one network round trip (the RPC), the focused link no longer exists, and focus is on <body>. They must Tab from the top through the skip link and up to 8 nav links on every single navigation. A screen reader announces nothing while the shell is blank. The same RPC is also repeated on every screen change.
fix: Move AdminShell into a shared layout that persists (for example a `(shell)` route group under `(admin)/admin/` holding every page except sign-in and preview), keep `gate` state there, and drop the per-page wrapper. `wide` can become a per-page prop or a pathname check inside the layout.

title: Alt text edited in the admin is ignored for the moonlight cup photos, and library images publish with empty alt
content: `moon.images` is a list of `{ id, alt }` (galleryPhotoFields, src/admin/collections/rooms.ts:38-41, alt required). The renderer uses `moon.images[0]` and `[1]` with their `.alt`, but passes the third and fourth to StoryFigure by id only. StoryFigure takes its alt from the hard-coded media-notes table (`noteFor(id)`, Story.tsx:77), which returns `{ alt: '' }` for any id it does not list. Separately, a media-library image resolves to a `media|…` reference string and its required `alt_ar` is never fetched: `mediaById` selects only `id,derivatives` (src/lib/content.ts:72). So any library image put in a room's `vignette` field, or in place of those two photos, is published as `alt=""` (decorative) although the library made Anas write a description.
failure_scenario: Anas opens «على الرف», rewrites the alt of the factory-mug photo (or swaps in a library image whose alt he typed) and publishes. The public page still says «كوب ضوء القمر الأصفر بزهوره المرسومة في المصنع» for the old photo, or renders the new one with alt="", so screen-reader users get no description. His edit has no effect and nothing tells him.
fix: Pass `alt={moonFactory.alt}` (and the `{moonInside}` equivalent) through StoryFigure, falling back to noteFor(id) only for caption/link. For bare `vignette` ids, add `alt_ar` to the `mediaById` select and carry it in the resolved reference, or add an alt field beside each vignette.

title: All 17 admin screens share one document title
content: The admin root layout sets a constant title and no admin page exports its own metadata (grep for `metadata` under src/app/(admin) finds only this line). Next's route announcer reads document.title after a client navigation, and the tab or history entry shows it too. WCAG 2.4.2 expects the title to say what the page is; the public site does this for every route.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user moves from «الفريق» to «المكتبة» to «الإعدادات»; each navigation is announced as «لوحة أنس», so nothing confirms the move. Browser history and tab lists show the same label for every admin page.
fix: Export `metadata = { title: 'الفريق' }` (and so on) from each admin page.tsx, with `title: { default: 'لوحة أنس', template: '%s · لوحة أنس' }` in the layout. For the query-string editors, set document.title from the loaded document.

title: StepUp dialog is unmounted while open, so focus falls to body after verify or cancel
content: TeamView (287) and CommerceSettingsForm (246) render `{stepUp && <StepUp open … />}` and close it by setting `stepUp` to null. That removes an open modal <dialog> from the DOM without calling dialog.close(), and the browser only restores focus to the opener inside close(). Only Escape (native close) restores it. Checked in headless Chromium: focus inside a modal dialog that is removed ends on <body>; after close() it returns to the opener.
failure_scenario: The owner activates «إيقاف» on a team row, the TOTP dialog opens, he types the code and presses «تحقق» (or «إلغاء»). The dialog disappears and focus is on <body>; he has to Tab from the top of the page to find the row he was working on.
fix: Keep <StepUp> mounted and drive it with `open={stepUp !== null}` so its effect calls dialog.close(), or have `cancel()` and the verified path call `dialogRef.current?.close()` before the parent clears state.

title: Removing a cart line deletes the focused button; focus is lost and the removal is not announced
content: «حذف» removes the whole <li>, including the button that has focus, and «إزالة غير المتاح» (line 242) does the same for several lines. Focus goes to <body>. The always-mounted total status announces a new total only after the ~300 ms requote, and when the last line goes the whole view is replaced by «سلتك فارغة.» (a subtree that was never in a live region), so that case announces nothing.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user removes the first of four lines with Enter. Focus resets to the top of the document and they must Tab back through the header and the earlier lines. Removing the only line gives no spoken result at all.
fix: After a removal, move focus to the next line's first control (or the list/summary heading, tabIndex -1) and put «حُذف المنتج» or «سلتك فارغة.» in the existing always-mounted role=status element.

title: Deleting an image drops focus and announces nothing
content: On success confirmDelete closes the dialog and sets `selected` to null in the same batch. That unmounts the details panel, including the «حذف» button that opened the dialog, so dialog.close() has nothing to return focus to and it lands on <body>. The deleted tile silently leaves the grid; no status text says the image was deleted.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user confirms «تأكيد الحذف». The dialog closes, focus goes to <body>, and nothing is spoken; they cannot tell whether the delete worked and must navigate from the top of the page.
fix: After the delete, focus the library heading or the grid (tabIndex -1) and set a role=status message such as «حُذفت الصورة» (keep the region mounted).

title: Restore/discard buttons and other one-shot actions remove the control that has focus
content: acceptLocalOffer and discardLocalOffer set `localOffer` to null, which unmounts the banner and the button just pressed, so focus falls to <body>. Same class elsewhere: MfaEnroll.tsx:83 swaps the enrolment form for «تطبيق المصادقة مفعّل.» after «تفعيل», and EmailView.tsx:90 reloads the attention list so a successfully replayed row (and its focused «إعادة الإرسال» button) disappears. None of these successes is announced (the MfaEnroll and EmailView results are not in a live region).
failure_scenario: A keyboard user restores the unsaved copy with Enter; focus resets to <body> instead of the form fields the restore just rewrote. After enabling the authenticator the form vanishes and the confirmation is never spoken, so the owner cannot tell that MFA is now on.
fix: Move focus to the first field (or the page h1 with tabIndex -1) after these actions, and announce the result through an always-mounted role=status element.

title: Field errors sit in non-live spans, so pressing Enter in the field that is already focused announces nothing
content: When validation fails, submit() sets the errors and calls focus() on the first invalid field. If that field already has focus, focus() is a no-op and the only change is text in a plain <span> plus new aria-invalid/aria-describedby attributes; none of these is announced by screen readers. The contact form has the same shape (ContactForm.tsx:144, an always-mounted span with no role or aria-live). AUDIT-1 X3.4 judged the pattern correct because focus normally moves, which holds only when the user submits from the button or another field.
failure_scenario: On /checkout a screen-reader user types a malformed email and presses Enter in that same field. The «أدخل بريدًا إلكترونيًا صحيحًا.» text appears but focus does not move and no live region fires, so nothing is spoken and the form seems to do nothing. The same happens for the name field, and on /contact for the name and email fields.
fix: Give the error element role="alert" (or render the first error into the existing always-mounted status region) so it is announced whether or not focus moves.

title: Invalid taxonomy slug error is silent and not tied to its input
content:
createTaxonomy() sets `newSlugError` and returns; the message is rendered in a plain

with no role, and the input has no aria-invalid or aria-describedby. Focus stays on «جديد». This is the same failure AUDIT-1 fixed in PublishBar, TableForm and StepUp (X3.5), but this file was not in that list. The message also asks for Latin letters, which a user typing on an Arabic layout is likely to violate.
failure_scenario: On «التصنيفات» a screen-reader user types «رحلات» in the slug field and presses «جديد». Nothing is announced, nothing moves, and the screen reader gives no hint of why the click did nothing.
fix:
Add role="alert" to the

, give it an id, and set aria-invalid and aria-describedby on #new-taxonomy-slug while the error shows.

title: Save is disabled while invalid; the reasons are a static list that is never announced and inputs are not marked invalid
content: TableForm disables «حفظ» whenever the schema fails and lists the issues in a plain list under the fields (CollectionForm.tsx:263 does the same list but keeps Save enabled). The list appears and changes as the user types, but it is not a live region, and text/slug/number inputs carry no aria-invalid or aria-describedby (only MoneyFieldInput got them in X3.4). A disabled button is skipped by Tab, so nothing points the keyboard user at the reason.
failure_scenario: The owner clears a product title and Tabs on to «حفظ». The button is dimmed and unreachable, and the screen reader never says why. The explanation is a list far from the field that he would have to find by reading the page linearly.
fix: Wrap the summary in role="alert" (or aria-live=polite), or keep Save enabled and, on click, focus the summary; add aria-invalid and aria-describedby to the offending input for text fields as MoneyFieldInput does.

title: Image dimensions «800×600» display reversed in the RTL page
content: `×` is a neutral between two European-number runs, so in the RTL paragraph it resolves to the right-to-left level and the two numbers swap places. Measured in headless Chromium: for «الأصل: 800×600 بكسل» the «800» range sits to the right of «600», so the line reads 600×800 from left to right. The derivative list at line 584 (`{derivative.width}×{derivative.height}`) is the same. AUDIT-1 X3.9 fixed the same reordering class for signs beside Latin digits, but not for dimension pairs.
failure_scenario: The owner opens an 800×600 (landscape) upload and sees «600×800» when he reads the digits left to right, so a landscape image looks portrait and the derivative sizes read as height by width.
fix: Wrap each pair in `{w}×{h}` (line 578 and line 584).

title: Reorder and delete buttons in admin lists have identical names on every item
content: Every item in a `paragraphs` or `list` field renders «أعلى», «أسفل», «حذف» (lines 651-674 and 722-745) inside an unlabeled div, so a screen-reader user hears the same three buttons repeated for each item (a scenes list can hold dozens). The same shape appears in TeamView.tsx:186-214 («حفظ», «إيقاف»/«استعادة» per member row), VersionHistory.tsx:116-123 («استعادة» per version) and EmailView.tsx:201-208 («إعادة الإرسال» per row). AUDIT-1 fixed the equivalent problem on the cart (X3.11) and the team role select (S10.4) but not these controls.
failure_scenario: On the scenes editor a screen-reader user tabbing through 26 photos hears «أعلى, button» 26 times with no photo name or number; pressing «حذف» on the wrong one deletes a different photo.
fix: Add an item-specific aria-label to each button (`حذف ${field.label} ${index + 1}`, `استعادة النسخة ${version.seq}`, `إيقاف ${member.display_name}`), or make each item a role=group with aria-label.

title: Journal category filter changes the list without any announcement
content: The scenes gallery announces how many photos a filter left through an always-mounted role=status element (AUDIT-1 S16.7). The journal filter is the same toggle-button group but re-keys and replaces the <ol> silently, so the result of the toggle is invisible to a screen reader.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user presses «رحلات» in the category filter. The list below changes to two posts, but nothing is spoken, so they cannot tell whether anything happened or how many posts match.
fix:
Add `

{`${category}: ${shown.length}`}

` next to the filter, mirroring SceneGallery.

title: Spelling errors in published contact copy
content: The services intro and one service line contain orthographic errors: «الإستشارة» (hamza on a wasl alif; correct «الاستشارة»), «الاتقان» (correct «الإتقان») and «المتابعه» (final ه for ة; correct «المتابعة»). The text is Anas's own deck copy, so it may need his confirmation, but as shipped these are wrong Arabic on a public page (/contact, «الاستشارات»).
failure_scenario: Visitors to /contact read «الإستشارة» and «المتابعه» in the consulting section; the mistakes are on the page that sells the consulting service.
fix: Correct to «الاستشارة», «الإتقان», «المتابعة» (line 14) and confirm the wording with Anas.

title: Verbatim-content drift check is skipped in CI, so the check never runs there
content: The check that Anas's texts in content/initial-content.json match BOOK_ASSETS/SORTED_2026-09-21/CONTENT.md is wrapped in an existence guard. The source file is git-excluded (.git/info/exclude), so on the CI runner (.github/workflows/ci.yml runs `pnpm test` on a clean checkout) the whole describe collapses to one empty `it.skip`. CI stays green whatever the fixture contains. On this machine the file exists, so the check ran and passed (34 files, 486 tests, exit 0). The gap is therefore CI-only, but the only automated guard for the verbatim requirement is enforced solely on the owner's machine.
quote: it.skip('BOOK_ASSETS/SORTED_2026-09-21/CONTENT.md is absent (expected in CI) — skipping drift check', () => {})
failure_scenario: A commit edits a paragraph in content/initial-content.json (typo fix, punctuation change, encoding slip). It is pushed from a machine without BOOK_ASSETS/SORTED_2026-09-21/. CI runs `pnpm test`, the drift describe is a single skipped test, the job passes, and the altered text is imported and published without any test noticing the deviation from Anas's source.
fix: Keep the local check, but add a source-independent guard that runs in CI: commit a hash manifest (SHA-256 per protected paragraph or field) generated from CONTENT.md and assert the fixture against it. Alternatively make the skip fail when `process.env.CI` is set.

title: Extensionless import in vitest.config.ts triggers Vite's native-loader deprecation warning
content: `pnpm test` prints: 'Your Vite config uses features that are unsupported by configLoader: native ... import ./src/lib/env without a file extension (vitest.config.ts:3:41)'. Vite plans to make the native loader the default in a future major. src/lib/env.ts already uses explicit `.ts` specifiers and tsconfig sets allowImportingTsExtensions: true, so only this one import blocks the switch. The config also carries the `assertLocalTestDatabase()` guard that protects `pnpm test:db` from running against a non-local database.
failure_scenario: A dependency bump moves to the Vite major that defaults to the native config loader. Node then cannot resolve './src/lib/env', vitest.config.ts fails to load, and `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:db` and the CI unit step all exit non-zero before any test runs. Because the config is where the disposable-database guard lives, the failure lands on the safety mechanism.
fix: Change line 3 to `import { assertLocalTestDatabase } from './src/lib/env.ts'`. The tsconfig already allows it and env.ts already imports with `.ts`.

title: Retention fixture has no coupon redemption, so the purge's third child delete is unproven
content: finance.buyer_retention_purge() deletes order_items, inventory_reservations and coupon_redemptions before finance.orders (20260930130000_buyer_retention.sql:28-31). coupon_redemptions.order_id is `unique references finance.orders (id)` with no ON DELETE CASCADE (20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:422), and checkout_expire and checkout_cancel leave that row behind (state 'released') on every coupon order. The fixture at lines 77-90 inserts only an order_items row and an inventory_reservations row. The D42 test therefore proves 2 of the 3 child tables.
quote: // Old enough: an expired hold 91 days ago, with a line and a reservation.
failure_scenario: A buyer uses a coupon and the hold expires. 91 days later the nightly job runs. If the `delete from finance.coupon_redemptions where order_id = any (v_orders)` line is dropped or broken (the function is create or replace), `delete from finance.orders` raises 23503 for that order. The whole purge aborts every night, no order or customer is ever deleted, and pg_cron only logs a failed run. buyer-retention.test.ts stays green because no fixture order has a redemption, so the owner's 90-day retention decision silently stops working.
fix: Insert a finance.coupon_redemptions row for oldOrder (a fixture coupon, state 'released', old expires_at) and assert it is gone after the purge. Also assert a recent order's redemption survives.

title: S01.2 only writes an audit row; no screen lets the owner (or an editor) see a dropped schedule
content: The fix and its test stop at the audit row. docs/operations.md:306-307 says the row is written 'so the owner can see it', but no admin route or component reads audit_events (src has none; AdminHome.tsx shows only a count of documents that still have scheduled_at). Only owners can read audit_events at all, and editors are the ones who schedule. The failed document simply drops out of the «المحتوى المجدول» count. No test asserts anything the owner can observe.
quote: "select summary from public.audit_events where action = 'content.publish_due_failed' and entity_id = $1",
failure_scenario: An editor schedules post B for 09:00 with a slug that live post A already uses, exactly this test's case. At 09:00 publish_due() drops B's schedule and writes the audit row. The scheduled count falls by one and nothing else changes. B never goes live, the editor believes it did, and the owner has no screen to find the audit row.
fix: Show recent content.publish_due_failed rows on AdminHome (owner) or keep the failed version marked in the document list, and cover it with an e2e or integration case. Otherwise correct docs/operations.md.

title: X1.1 resets the approval but the buyer still sees an open checkout that dead-ends; nothing tests or tells anyone
content: The test proves the trigger sets policy_revisions to '{}' and bumps the version. It asserts nothing about what buyers or the owner see afterwards. checkout_quote returns `checkoutEnabled` from checkout_enabled alone (20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:768-769). CartView offers «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب» when quote.checkoutEnabled is true. CheckoutForm shows the unavailable note only on `!quote.checkoutEnabled` (CheckoutForm.tsx:434) and builds the consent line from Object.keys(quote.policyRevisions) (CheckoutForm.tsx:173-177). checkout_create answers POLICIES_NOT_CONFIGURED only at submit (SQL lines 859-861). PublishBar's success text has no hint (PublishBar.tsx:59), and no admin screen reads audit_events, so `commerce.policies_reset` is invisible to the owner. No integration or e2e test covers this state (cart-checkout.spec only toggles checkout_enabled).
failure_scenario: checkout_enabled is true and the policies are approved. The owner edits «سياسة الاسترجاع» and publishes it. The trigger sets policy_revisions = '{}'. A buyer opens /cart and sees «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب». /checkout renders the full form with the consent line «قرأت  وأوافق عليها» and no policy link. The buyer fills in every field, ticks consent, passes Turnstile and presses «تأكيد الطلب». The reply is 503 'الشراء غير متاح حاليًا، ويفتح قريبًا.' Until the owner happens to re-approve, every buyer dead-ends at the last step and nothing tells the owner why.
fix: Make checkout_quote report checkoutEnabled = checkout_enabled and seller fields set and policy_revisions <> '{}' so the cart and checkout show the unavailable note up front. Add an assertion for that after the reset here, and a cart-checkout e2e case that publishes a policy with checkout on. Tell the owner in PublishBar or on the settings page that the publish cleared the approval.

title: X1.1 reset test passes only if policies/store already has a version (hidden demo-catalog dependency)
content: `approve(APPROVED)` stores store: 1. publishAs computes seq as max(seq)+1 for ('policies','store'). The trigger resets only when the approved value differs from the new seq (audit_fixes.sql:145). Policies are seeded only by scripts/seed-demo-catalog.mjs; scripts/import-content.mjs does not touch them. docs/development.md:130-135 documents db:reset then db:import as the test:db setup and never mentions the demo catalog.
failure_scenario: On a database from `pnpm db:reset` and `pnpm db:import` only, content_versions holds no policies/store, so publishAs returns seq 1. The approved '1' equals the new seq and the trigger correctly does nothing. The test's `expect(after.policy_revisions).toEqual({})` and the audit-row assertions then fail. A correct trigger reads as a failure, and the suite depends on demo-seed state that AUDIT-1's battery happened to have.
fix: Approve a revision that cannot collide, for example { store: 999, delivery: 999, refund: 999 }, or publish twice and approve the first seq.

title: The 'at the quota nothing is claimed' half never has a priority-0 row pending, so it cannot fail for the intended reason
content: outbox_claim blocks a row with `(o.priority = 0 or v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - p_reserve) and v_sent_today < p_daily_quota` (audit_fixes.sql:373-374). At the second claim the only pending rows are `mid` (priority 1) and `low` (priority 2). Clause 1 already excludes them at 100 sends, so `claimed` is [] whether or not the hard `v_sent_today < p_daily_quota` clause exists. The priority-0 receipt, the only row that clause governs, was accepted earlier and is no longer pending.
quote: // Fill to exactly the quota: nothing is claimed at all.
failure_scenario: A refactor deletes `and v_sent_today < p_daily_quota`. Receipts (priority 0) are then claimed after 100 sends and Resend answers 429 on each, yet the test stays green.
fix: Insert a pending priority-0 row before filling to 100 and assert it is not claimed.

title: 'operations sees nothing' became vacuous when S01.1 required visible: true
content: The fixture publishes `{ cover: ticket }` with no `visible`. Since audit_fixes.sql:49-51 and 79, a post without data->'visible' = true is excluded from media_published_ids(). The media is therefore not public at all, and an operations (authenticated) read returns [] even if a public-read policy were extended to authenticated. The first RLS test (line 218) correctly uses `visible: true`; this one does not.
failure_scenario: Someone changes media_public_read from `to anon` to `to anon, authenticated` so signed-in users can see published images. Operations then reads every published image, but this test still gets [] because its published post is hidden, so the regression goes unnoticed.
fix: Publish the fixture with visible: true (and assert anon sees the same id) before asserting the operations read is empty.

title: X2.6's save-versus-delete race is only exercised in two sequential orders
content: products_check_cover relies on FOR KEY SHARE conflicting with media_delete's `for update` (audit_fixes.sql:657-686, store_media.sql:61), and its comment says the two 'serialize and one of them is refused'. The test only runs a missing-cover insert/update and a delete followed by an unrelated update. Nothing holds one session open while the other runs. tests/integration/outbox.test.ts:165-193 already shows the deterministic technique (open transaction plus lock_timeout).
quote: describe('X2.6: a product cannot be saved with a library cover that is gone', () => {
failure_scenario: The trigger's `for key share` is changed to a plain select. Every assertion here still passes. A concurrent media_delete (which sees no product using the image yet) and a product save (which sees the not-yet-deleted media row) both commit, leaving a product whose cover_image points at a deleted media row.
fix: Add a two-connection test: session A begins and runs media_delete's lock on the media row; session B's product insert or update with that cover must wait (lock_timeout error) or end 23503 once A commits.

title: staff-admin negative paths: last-owner race, operations role, revoked owner and set_active on the last owner are not asserted
content: P03's proof lists anon, editor, operations, owner and a revoked member against the Edge Function. This file covers only anon (401) and editor (403). The last-owner test is sequential and only uses set_role, yet staff_keep_an_owner serializes with pg_advisory_xact_lock precisely for the concurrent case (20260924130000_staff_and_app_server.sql:52-64). set_active:false on the last owner is never called.
quote: it('refuses to remove the last active owner', async () => {
failure_scenario: The advisory lock line is removed, or set_active is reordered to ban in Auth before the database update. Two fresh-TOTP owners demoting each other at once (Promise.all of two set_role calls) both pass the check and leave zero active owners, which needs SQL to recover. Every current test passes.
fix: Add a Promise.all test where two owners (both stepped up, all other owners paused as in the existing test) demote each other and exactly one call succeeds. Add operations and revoked-owner 403 cases and a last-owner set_active:false case.

title: media_delete (the destructive function, redefined in store_media.sql) has no role-denial test
content: Denial cases exist for media_create_ticket (line 93) and foreign tickets, but media_delete is only ever called with an active editor. It was rewritten in 20260927180000_store_media.sql ('otherwise identical') and its `content_assert_publisher(p_actor)` line is the only SQL-level role check on deletion.
quote: it('media_delete refuses used media (23503) and deletes unused media with its keys', async () => {
failure_scenario: A later create-or-replace of media_delete drops the content_assert_publisher line. The admin function's TypeScript check is then the only guard, and no integration test notices that the service-role function accepts an operations or inactive actor.
fix: Assert media_delete answers 42501 for an operations and for an inactive owner.

title: createStaff never cleans up, so repeated runs make auth.spec fail once staff_directory passes 1,000 rows
content: About 85 createStaff call sites in tests/integration and 30 in tests/e2e create confirmed auth users and staff rows that are never removed. staff_directory() is ordered by created_at (20260925090000:71) and PostgREST caps responses at max_rows = 1000 (supabase/config.toml:18). TeamView renders that list, and auth.spec.ts:65 asserts the freshly invited member appears in it. AUDIT-1's own report records 1,730 leftover staff breaking auth.spec, fixed only by resetting the database. docs/development.md tells nobody to reset before test:db or test:e2e.
failure_scenario: After roughly ten full runs on one stack, the invited member is row 1,001 or later. The owner's team table never shows it and `page.getByText(memberEmail)` fails, so an unrelated re-run goes red.
fix: Register every created user id and delete the auth users in an afterAll or global teardown, or document a mandatory db:reset plus db:import plus db:demo-catalog before each acceptance run.

title: The stated reason for skipping test:db is wrong for almost every integration file, so AUDIT-1's DB fixes never gate a commit
content: The job already runs `supabase start` with Postgres, Auth (gotrue), the Data API and Storage, plus `pnpm db:import`. Nearly all tests/integration files need only those: audit-fixes, buyer-retention, policy-approval, commerce-settings, privacy-requests, checkout, outbox, media-security, static-site, content and publish. forms, email-delivery and stats import their handlers directly and need neither the Edge runtime nor Mailpit. Only staff-admin.test.ts calls FUNCTIONS_URL.
quote: # Not run here, and deliberately so: `pnpm test:db` and `pnpm test:e2e`. They
failure_scenario: A migration edit removes policies_reset_approval, deny_password_tokens or the default-privilege revoke (S01.4, S01.5, X1.1). CI stays green because none of the tests that would catch it run there. The regression merges and is found only at the next manual acceptance run.
fix: Add a CI step `TEST_ENV=local DATABASE_URL=... pnpm test:db` after db:import, excluding staff-admin.test.ts (or start edge-runtime for it), and keep the e2e suite local.

title: No e2e asserts an admin auth denial: wrong or expired code, signed-out visit, or a signed-in non-staff user
content: auth.spec.ts has the happy path and the identical 'sent' message for an unknown email. Nothing asserts «الرمز غير صحيح أو انتهت صلاحيته.» (SignIn.tsx BAD_CODE_MESSAGE). Nothing asserts a signed-out visit to an admin URL redirects to /admin/sign-in, or that a signed-in user with no staff row sees «لا تملك صلاحية الوصول». AUDIT-1 rewrote AdminShell's gate logic (error versus no-role versus ready) and added SignIn's back button, with no test on either.
quote: test('an unknown email gets the identical sent message', async ({ page }) => {
failure_scenario: A change makes AdminShell render its children while gate.status is 'signed-out' or 'no-role'. The admin shell and screens show to anonymous and non-staff visitors (data is still RLS-protected), and every e2e test passes because each one signs in first.
fix: Add three short cases: a wrong six-digit code shows the Arabic error, /admin/content signed out lands on /admin/sign-in, and a user created without a staff row sees «لا تملك صلاحية الوصول».

title: The six Edge Function entrypoints sit outside tsc, eslint, unit tests and CI; staff-admin keeps its logic inline
content: Only the six `index.ts` files are excluded from `pnpm typecheck`; all 21 `_shared/*.ts` files are already type-checked through the imports in src and tests (`tsc -p tsconfig.json --listFilesOnly` lists them, including media-sweep.ts and stats.ts). A scratch `tsc --noEmit` with a `declare const Deno` stub over all 27 files exits 0 with zero errors today, so there is no current type defect. No automated gate covers the entrypoints: CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) starts the stack with `-x edge-runtime` and never runs `test:db` or `test:e2e`, the only things that execute them. The five thin wrappers import a handler by name from `_shared`. `staff-admin/index.ts` is the exception: about 110 lines of owner-only invite/role/revoke logic live in the entrypoint, so no unit test can import it.
failure_scenario: A refactor renames `handleJobs` in `_shared/jobs.ts`, or changes the `fail`/`corsHeaders` signature that `staff-admin/index.ts:11-19` uses. Tests import `_shared` directly, and no `tsc` or `eslint` run sees the entrypoint. `pnpm check` and CI stay green. `supabase functions deploy` does not type-check, so the module fails on first invocation: the `outbox` function stops dispatching email and the daily media sweep, or `staff-admin` returns 500 to the owner.
fix: Commit `supabase/functions/tsconfig.json` (Deno stub `.d.ts`, `types: ["node"]`, include `**/*.ts`) and append `&& tsc -p supabase/functions/tsconfig.json` to the `typecheck` script; it passes today. Move the `staff-admin` handler body into `_shared/staff-admin.ts` as `handleStaffAdmin(request, deps)` with the other five pattern and add a unit test with an injected client.

title: A JSON `null` body crashes staff-admin with a bare 500 and no error envelope
content: `JSON.parse(text)` is assigned to `body: Record<string, unknown>` with no object check. `admin.ts:147-149` rejects non-objects with 400 BAD_JSON, but this function does not. The body `null` passes the size check, then `body.action` at line 69 throws a TypeError outside any try/catch. `Deno.serve` answers a plain-text 500 with no CORS headers and no `{ok:false,error,requestId}` envelope, which breaks the contract `http.ts` declares for every Edge Function.
failure_scenario: An owner with a fresh TOTP (or a script holding their token) POSTs the body `null` to /functions/v1/staff-admin. JSON.parse returns null, line 69 `switch (body.action)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`, and the reply is 500 text/plain. The browser treats it as a network/CORS failure, and TeamView shows «تعذّر الاتصال بالخادم.» instead of BAD_JSON. The same body to `admin` gets a proper 400 envelope.
fix: Reuse the `admin.ts:147-149` guard: after parsing, `if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) throw new Error('shape')` inside the existing try, so it returns 400 BAD_JSON.

title: Invite rollback ignores a failed deleteUser, leaving an orphaned auth user that blocks re-inviting the email
content: When the `staff` insert fails after `createUser`, the code calls `deleteUser` and discards its `{error}` result (auth-js returns it rather than throwing). If the delete also fails, the confirmed auth user stays with no `staff` row. Every retry then hits `error?.code === 'email_exists'` and answers 409 USER_EXISTS «هذا البريد مسجّل مسبقًا.». `staff_directory` lists only `staff` rows, so the owner cannot see or remove the orphan from /admin/team.
failure_scenario: The database or GoTrue has a brief outage during an invite: `admin.from('staff').insert` returns an error, and `deleteUser` fails for the same reason. The owner sees «تعذّرت الدعوة» and retries. Every later attempt for that address returns USER_EXISTS, and only the Supabase dashboard can fix it.
fix: Check the `deleteUser` result and report it in the audit summary. Better, on `email_exists` look the user up by id, and if it has no `staff` row, insert the `staff` row for the existing id instead of answering USER_EXISTS.

title: TeamView re-implements callFunction without the 200-shape validation, so a non-envelope 200 throws
content: `src/lib/supabase/functions.ts:28-31` validates a 200 reply (`'ok' in data`) precisely because a gateway or proxy may answer HTML. TeamView keeps a private copy of the same helper that casts `data as ActionResult` with no check. A non-envelope 200 makes `result.ok` undefined, and lines 91, 102 and 119 then read `result.error.*` on undefined and throw a TypeError inside an async handler. AUDIT-1's hardening of the shared helper did not reach this duplicate.
failure_scenario: A proxy answers staff-admin with HTTP 200 and an HTML or empty body. functions-js returns `data` as a string or null, `result.ok` is undefined, and `runAction` throws at `result.error.code`. `busy` was already cleared, nothing is displayed, and the promise rejects unhandled. The owner cannot tell whether an invite, role change or revoke happened.
fix: Delete the local `callStaffAdmin` and use `callFunction('staff-admin', body)` from `@/lib/supabase/functions`; the result type is the same.

title: The stats cache stores an `unavailable` analytics result for five minutes
content: `stats()` caches whatever `ownerStats()` returns. `fetchAnalytics` turns every transient failure (a 10 s timeout, a Cloudflare 5xx, a dropped request) into `{status:'unavailable', reason}`, and that result is cached like a good one. Until the TTL passes, every owner call on that isolate returns the failure with the old `generatedAt`, although Cloudflare has recovered.
failure_scenario: Cloudflare GraphQL answers 500 once when the owner opens /admin/stats. The page shows analytics unavailable. The owner reloads 30 seconds later, and the cached entry still carries `reason: 'HTTP_ERROR'` with the old timestamp, so the screen stays broken for up to five minutes.
fix: Write the cache only when `value.analytics.status === 'ok'`: `if (value.analytics.status === 'ok') cachedStats = { at: Date.now(), value }`.

title: Supply chain: no deno.lock, and one transitive range floats in every function (iceberg-js ^0.8.1)
content: It matters only a little. The top-level pins are exact, and so is almost everything below them. supabase-js 2.117.1 pins auth, postgrest, realtime, storage and functions-js at 2.117.1; realtime-js pins @supabase/phoenix 0.4.5 and tslib 2.8.1; zod and image-size 2.0.4 have no dependencies; there are no https: or jsr: imports. The one floating range is `iceberg-js: ^0.8.1` inside storage-js, which imports it at module top, so it loads in all six functions at boot. No deno.lock exists. pnpm-lock.yaml pins 0.8.1 for Node and the tests, so the tested version is not guaranteed to be the deployed one.
failure_scenario: A later iceberg-js 0.8.x is published (buggy or compromised). The next `supabase functions deploy` resolves it with no lockfile and runs it at boot inside isolates that hold SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, JOBS_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY and TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER. The unit tests and local e2e never exercised that version.
fix: Add `"iceberg-js": "npm:iceberg-js@0.8.1"` to the six deno.json files and commit a per-function deno.lock if the deploy path honors it; confirm the loaded version from the deploy or `deno info` output.

title: Status claims check:export guards against the five child films; the script has no such check
content: The AUDIT-1 evidence line says check:export verifies 'no child-film file'. scripts/check-export.mjs does not. It checks REQUIRED files (51), lang/dir on public pages, secret patterns, service_role JWTs and the I40 demo guard (scripts/lib/demo-guard.mjs). Nothing in it, or in check-budgets, names or pattern-matches 46-kid-picnic-jam, 47-kid-bisht-honey-jar, 48-kid-supermarket-tomato-pesto, 49-kid-hotel-breakfast or 50-kid-cafe-croissant-jam. The recorded run (artifacts/acceptance/AUDIT-1/commands.txt:37) says only '51 required files present; 320 text files scanned, no secrets; demo guard: loopback build'. The only guards are tests/unit/collections.test.ts:220 (the content fixture) and the five films being absent from public/media today. G4.2, the single high finding of AUDIT-1, is exactly this leak, so the sentence reads as a regression guard that does not exist.
quote: - build, check:export (51 required files, no secret, no child-film file) and check:budgets (largest 147.0 KiB);
failure_scenario: Guardian consent is still pending. Someone uncomments the five entries in scripts/prepare-media.mjs:158-164 (its comment says how to add them back) or copies the mp4 files into public/media, then runs pnpm build && pnpm check:export as the status document says to. The check exits 0, and with the planned Pages build command 'pnpm build && pnpm check:export' (I40) the five films with children ship in every export again.
fix: Add a fail to scripts/check-export.mjs for any file under out/ whose name matches /(^|\/)(46|47|48|49|50)-kid-/ (or a named denylist kept next to prepare-media.mjs), with a unit test. Until then, delete 'no child-film file' from this line.

title: Restore step 5 drops the hosted Auth settings that keep sign-up closed, and its 403 check cannot prove the hook
content: Step 5 is the only runbook step for the hosted-only Auth settings, and it lists a subset of PLANS/ISSUES.md I28. It omits 'Allow new users to sign up' OFF, email provider ON, OTP length 6 with expiry 600 s, and TOTP enrol/verify ON. supabase/config.toml drives only the local stack; its own comment (lines 222-226) says [auth] enable_signup=false is what blocks sign-ups and [auth.email] enable_signup=true is the provider switch. A newly created Supabase project starts with sign-up enabled and a 3600 s OTP expiry, and the Arabic template (supabase/templates/magic_link.html) tells staff the code is 'صالح لعشر دقائق'. The check offered, 're-check with a password grant, which must return 403', proves only the hook. GoTrue runs the Custom Access Token hook after the password is verified, and staff accounts have no password, so on a correct project that grant answers 400 invalid_credentials. The local proof (tests/integration/audit-fixes.test.ts:88-93) first sets a password with auth.admin.updateUserById. The three sign-up refusal checks are only in artifacts/acceptance/P03/commands.txt:68-72, which I28 cites by path. DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:99 says 'the hosted project enables both (I28)', yet nothing hosted was changed (EXECUTION-STATUS.md:307). So no single runbook list covers every hosted-only setting with a check that can pass or fail.
quote: Re-apply the Auth settings (I28): SMTP for Resend, redirect URLs, the
failure_scenario: The hosted project is lost and Anas restores into a new project following steps 1-8. Sign-up stays at the new-project default (enabled) because step 5 never mentions it, and the password-grant check is misread or skipped. The publishable key is in every page's JavaScript, so anyone can POST /auth/v1/otp with {"email":"victim@example.com","create_user":true}. That creates auth users and sends the staff sign-in email through the owner's Resend SMTP. An attacker can spend the 100/day Resend quota, which the outbox reserve (RESERVE = 20) is meant to protect for sign-in codes, and so lock staff out of admin sign-in and delay contact notices until 00:00 UTC. The OTP also stays valid for 1 hour while the email says ten minutes.
fix: Replace step 5 with one checklist titled 'Hosted-only Auth settings', taken from I28: site URL and redirect URLs, Allow new users to sign up OFF, email provider ON, OTP length 6 and expiry 600 s, TOTP enrol and verify ON, Arabic magic-link template, Resend SMTP, Custom Access Token hook public.deny_password_tokens, Secure password change ON. Add its checks: (a) with the publishable key, POST /auth/v1/otp with create_user true for an unknown email gives 422 signup_disabled, with create_user false gives 422 otp_disabled, and POST /auth/v1/signup gives 422 signup_disabled; (b) create a throwaway user, set a password with the admin API, password-grant gives 403, delete the user. Point I28 and DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:99 at that checklist and reword the latter as a requirement, not a fact.

title: check:export is cited as proof of 'no migration credential' but has no pattern for one
content: SECRET_PATTERNS in scripts/check-export.mjs:68-75 are sb_secret_, whsec_, a Resend key shape, a PEM private key, the two local dev secrets, plus a service_role JWT decode. There is no pattern for a Postgres connection string (DATABASE_URL, which .env.example:67 calls a migration credential), a Supabase access token (sbp_...), the DB password, the Cloudflare API or analytics tokens, or a Turnstile secret. The contract sentence claims the script proves the absence of a migration credential.
quote: No secret/service-role key or migration credential in the static site or browser (`pnpm check:export`).
failure_scenario: During P11 someone sets DATABASE_URL (or an sbp_ token) as a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable in the Pages build environment, or pastes it into a client component. pnpm check:export exits 0 and the credential is inlined into out/_next/static JavaScript and deployed, while this document says the check covers it.
fix: Add patterns such as /postgres(ql)?:\/\/[^\s"'@]+:[^\s"'@]+@/ and /sbp_[0-9a-f]{40}/ (and the Turnstile 0x4 secret shape) to SECRET_PATTERNS with a unit test, or reword the sentence to list exactly what the script detects.

title: Restore step 4 does not list the Edge Function secrets, and TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER is not a throwaway value
content: Backups deliberately exclude Edge Function secrets (operations.md:520-523), so step 4 is the only place they come back, yet it names two and says 'the rest'. TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER is load-bearing well beyond what .env.example:27-28 says ('Salts the contact form's hashed caller key'). checkout.ts:136-141 derives each order access token as HMAC(pepper, 'order-access:<idempotencyKey>') and stores sha256(pepper:order:token) as orders.access_token_hash. Nothing tells the operator to reuse the original pepper or keep a copy; a fresh random value is the natural choice. An unset TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER makes contact answer 500 (contact.ts:141-142) and checkout 503 (checkout.ts:217); an unset SITE_URL makes contact answer 403 to every origin.
failure_scenario: After a restore the operator sets JOBS_SECRET and RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET and a newly generated TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER. Every stored access_token_hash (7-day order links, P08 download tokens, DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:75) stops matching, so buyers' cancel calls answer 404 and P08 links die. If the operator forgets TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER or SITE_URL, the contact form fails with 500 or 403 and nothing in the runbook would show it.
fix: In step 4 list every secret by name from .env.example (SITE_URL, JOBS_SECRET, TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER, RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM, RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, ANALYTICS_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID, plus PAYMENTS_MODE when it exists), mark TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER 'reuse the original; it is not in any backup; keep a copy with the passphrase', add a smoke test (a contact POST from the site origin answers 201), and fix the .env.example comment.

title: Neither the restore runbook nor the rehearsal proves that the nine pg_cron jobs exist after a restore
content: Every schedule (email-outbox, site-build-trigger, content-publish-due, media-sweep, checkout-expire, rate-limits-purge, job-runs-purge, contacts-purge, buyer-retention) exists only as a row created by `select cron.schedule(...)` inside a migration. history_data.sql marks all migrations applied, so a restore never re-runs them. scripts/restore-check.mjs passes when the COPY row counts in data.sql equal the restored counts (lines 382-395). It never queries cron.job, and it starts from an empty `supabase init` workdir, not the repo's migrations. The runbook's 'what a file does not hold' list (lines 520-523) names Vault, function secrets, Auth settings and keys, but not the cron schema, and steps 3-5 never say to check or re-create the jobs.
quote: 3. Re-create the Vault secrets: `select vault.create_secret(...)` for
failure_scenario: If data.sql does not carry cron.job (the rehearsal cannot tell), the restored project has every function and no schedule. The outbox never runs, publishes never trigger a rebuild, scheduled posts never go live, checkout holds never expire, and contacts-purge, buyer-retention and rate-limits-purge never run, so the 90-day retention promise silently fails. The owner home only shows 'لم يعمل بعد'.
fix: Add a step that runs `select jobname, schedule from cron.job order by 1` and compares it with the nine names above, re-running the cron.schedule lines from the migrations for any that are missing; add the same comparison to restore-check.mjs's pass criteria, and add cron.job to the 'does not hold' list if the dump indeed omits it.

title: The access/erase lookup misses visitors whose address has an internationalized domain
content: contact.ts:53-77 converts any non-ASCII domain to punycode before validation and storage (its comment names the Saudi '.السعودية' TLD), and the DB check only accepts xn-- labels. The runbook's export and delete queries compare against the address exactly as the requester writes it. Step 37 then says to 'list the ids with the query above' before calling privacy_erase_contacts, so a miss feeds straight into the erase call.
quote: select id, name, email, message, created_at from public.contacts where email = lower(btrim('<address>'));
failure_scenario: A visitor who wrote from x@مثال.السعودية asks for deletion. The operator pastes that address, gets 0 rows, tells the visitor nothing is held and writes nothing to the ledger, while the row stored as x@xn--mgbh0fb.xn--mgberp4a5d4ar (or the like) and its message remain.
fix: Tell the operator to punycode the domain first (for example with node -e "console.log(new URL('http://'+domain).hostname)") or to search with `email like '%@xn--%'` plus the local part, and say so next to the query.

title: Data map omits Cloudflare as a recipient of the visitor's raw IP and misstates what the owner sees of staff
content: The Providers row lists only Resend and Supabase. turnstile.ts:68 sends the visitor's raw IP as remoteip to Cloudflare's siteverify on every contact and checkout submission (skipped only for 'local'), and operations.md:48-53 says only that no raw IP is stored or logged by us. Cloudflare also serves the site and Email Routing forwards help@anas.studio. Line 17 says the owner sees names and roles in the team screen, but staff_directory() (20260925090000_audit_and_staff_directory.sql:44-65) returns each member's email and whether they enrolled TOTP. The map is the input to the E08 privacy text.
quote: | Providers | Resend keeps sent-email data 30 days on the Free plan; Supabase keeps its platform logs per plan |
failure_scenario: Anas drafts the E08 privacy policy from this map and omits Cloudflare (Turnstile receives each submitter's IP; Email Routing and Pages handle mail and requests), so the approved policy understates the processors and the processor review E08 requires is incomplete.
fix: Add a Cloudflare row (Turnstile: IP and browser signals per contact or checkout submission; Pages: request logs; Email Routing: help@anas.studio mail) and change line 17 to 'names, emails, roles and TOTP status'.

title: Runbook quotes admin strings that the screens do not show, and keeps pre-D31 package numbers
content: The runbook tells the owner what the stats screen says when unconfigured. StatsView.tsx:32 and :119 render «غير متاح: الإحصاءات غير مُعدّة بعد. تحتاج إلى ANALYTICS_TOKEN و CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID.», and StatsView.tsx:91 renders «غير مُعدّ بعد. تظهر أرقامه عند افتتاح المتجر.»; neither quoted string exists anywhere in src. Line 341-342 also says commerce stays unconfigured 'until the order and payment tables exist (P07/P08)', but the orders tables exist since P07 (20260927160000) and stats.ts:10 still reports not_configured until P08. Line 94 says availability notices are P07; D31 and HANDOFF.md:39 moved them to P08.
failure_scenario: At E11 the owner or an auditor checks the stats screen against this runbook, searches for the quoted Arabic, and cannot match it, so a correct 'not configured' state is reported as a defect or the wrong secret is chased; the P07/P08 wording sends a P08 builder to look for missing tables that already exist.
fix: Quote the real strings (or describe them without quoting), and change '(P07/P08)' to 'P08' for commerce stats and '(P07)' to '(P08)' for availability notices.

title: SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF is a name nothing reads; the backup script uses SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID
content: scripts/backup.mjs:49 and :192 read SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID, and docs/operations.md:550 documents that name. SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF is referenced nowhere in src, scripts, supabase, tests, CI or docs. AUDIT-1 S23.8 removed one stale name from this file but left this one.
failure_scenario: On the owner's machine he fills SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF as the template suggests and expects `pnpm backup --linked` to use it without `supabase link`. The script ignores it and exits with 'No linked Supabase project' (or backs up a previously linked project).
fix: Rename it to SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID in .env.example (with a comment that only backup.mjs reads it), or delete the line.

title: The 'Current state' table still says AUDIT-1 is not committed and stops at the wrong last commit
content: Line 11 says AUDIT-1 was 'not committed'. Line 10 and the package ledger (line 323) say it was committed as f38f04d and pushed, and git log confirms f38f04d, 9f6f37f, cab4000 and 4f22b78. Row 10 names the D42 docs commit as the last commit, but HEAD is 4f22b78 (REPO-SWEEP). KICKOFF tells each session to read this table first (AUDIT-1 S22.1 was the same class).
quote: AUDIT-1 (built and audited 2026-09-30, not committed): see the package ledger.
failure_scenario: A fresh orchestrator session reads the table, believes the AUDIT-1 work is uncommitted, and stages or re-commits already committed files, or asks the owner to authorize a commit that already happened.
fix: Change the Packages cell to 'AUDIT-1 (committed f38f04d, pushed)' and the Last commit cell to 4f22b78, the REPO-SWEEP commit.

title: C25 says the WhatsApp link is live; no WhatsApp number exists anywhere in the content
content: The /contact page shows the WhatsApp tile only when site_settings.contact.whatsapp is set (src/app/(public)/contact/page.tsx:30 and :48). content/initial-content.json has no whatsapp field (keys: nav, footer, home, social, rooms, scenes), and I41 lists only the social links and the scenes for the hosted bootstrap. C25's proof is 'configured live links', and this ledger is the status record the owner package is checked against.
quote: partial (P06): the WhatsApp and social links are live; the ICS feed and calendar integration (P09) are not started.
