failure_scenario: At P11 or P09 acceptance the ledger is read as 'WhatsApp done' and no input is requested from Anas. After the first hosted build /contact has no WhatsApp channel, because no number was ever entered, and the gap is found by a visitor.
fix: Reword to 'the social links are live; the WhatsApp link appears once Anas enters his number in the settings'; add the WhatsApp number to I45/HANDOFF's list of Anas inputs.

title: Stale-version 409 for settings and policy approval rests on SQLSTATE 40001, which the repo itself says PostgREST does not answer
content: audit_fixes.sql:164-165 switched publish_version and schedule_version to unique_violation because 'PostgREST does not answer a 40001 at all: the call hangs'. commerce_settings_save here, and commerce_policies_approve (20260927170000_policy_approval.sql:39), still raise serialization_failure (40001), and the admin Edge Function reaches them through the same PostgREST path (db.ts serviceRpc). admin.ts:370 and :389 turn 40001 into a 409, and operations.md:361-363 and :458-459 document that 409. The only tests are a mocked rpc (tests/unit/admin-function.test.ts:315 and :383) and direct pg connections (tests/integration/commerce-settings.test.ts:144, policy-approval.test.ts:135) that bypass PostgREST; no e2e test covers it.
failure_scenario: Two owner sessions save seller details or approve policies concurrently. If AUDIT-1's observation is right, the loser's request never gets the documented 409 «تغيّرت الإعدادات من جلسة أخرى. أعد تحميل الصفحة.» and the admin function hangs until its time limit; if the observation is wrong, the comment in audit_fixes.sql misleads the next maintainer. Either way the documented behavior is unproven end to end.
fix: Add one test that calls the real admin function (or PostgREST rpc) with a stale expectedVersion and asserts 409. If it hangs, raise a SQLSTATE PostgREST maps, for example unique_violation as publish_version does, and change admin.ts:370 and :389 to match.

title: number fields have no ceiling, so int4 overflow reaches Postgres and shows only «تعذّر الحفظ.»
content: The shared `number` schema has `min`/`max` options, but no table config sets `max` and there is no default (the `money` case defaults to 10_000_000). Every number field in the catalog is a Postgres `integer` (max 2,147,483,647): `products.sort_order`, `product_variants.stock`, `low_stock_threshold`, `sort_order`, `coupons.usage_limit`, `shipping_rates.sort_order`. TableForm maps only 23505, 23514 and 23503, so SQLSTATE 22003 falls to the generic 'تعذّر الحفظ.' with no field named. This is the class S11.3 fixed for text/money fields; the integer fields were left out. Variants.ts:24 is one of the six sites.
quote: let schema = z.number({ message: 'أدخل رقمًا.' }).int('أدخل عددًا صحيحًا.')
failure_scenario: Owner types 3000000000 in «المخزون» (a typo with extra zeros) or in «حد الاستخدام» of a coupon. The schema accepts it (integer, >= 0), Save stays enabled, PostgREST answers 22003 `value "3000000000" is out of range for type integer`, and the form shows only «تعذّر الحفظ.», which reads like an outage, not a bad value.
fix: In the `number` case use `.max(field.max ?? 2_147_483_647, ...)` (same pattern as the money default of 10_000_000) so the form names the field; optionally set a sane `max` on stock and usage_limit in the configs.

title: Customer phone has no client rule; a typo fails as the generic «تحقق من القيم.» (S11.3 not complete)
content: `customers.phone` is checked by `^9665[0-9]{8}$`. `toRow` normalises with `normalizeSaudiMobile` and, when that returns null, sends `values.phone.trim()` as typed, leaving the refusal to the database (the header comment says so). The form schema for `phone` is a plain nullable string, and TableForm shows only 'تحقق من القيم.' for 23514. S11.3 removed this exact no-field-named outcome for code, sku, slug and city_key, but phone was not covered.
failure_scenario: Owner corrects a customer's phone to `0401234567` (not a mobile) or `05012345` (too short). The form shows no error and Save is enabled. toRow sends the raw text, Postgres raises 23514 on `customers_phone_check`, and the owner sees only «تحقق من القيم.» with no hint which field is wrong.
fix: Add a rule to the phone field: empty, or `normalizeSaudiMobile(value) !== null`, with the message used in CheckoutForm ('أدخل رقم جوال سعوديًا صحيحًا.'). The Field type needs a small `refine` option, or a `pattern` that accepts the spellings `foldDigits` folds.

title: Catalog text fields lack the control-character rule the database enforces
content: products.title, product_variants.title, shipping_rates.name_ar and customers.name each have `!~ '[[:cntrl:]]'` in SQL. The client text rules are only `nonBlank`, `maxLength` and `pattern`; none rejects control characters, and `<input type=text>` keeps a pasted tab (only CR/LF are stripped). commerce-settings.ts already mirrors this SQL rule ('لا يُقبل نص فيه رموز تحكم.') with a field error, so the pattern exists but was not applied to the catalog forms.
quote: return field.nonBlank ? schema.refine((value) => value.trim() !== '', { message: 'لا يمكن أن يكون فارغًا.' }) : schema
failure_scenario: Owner pastes a product title copied from a table or spreadsheet, which contains a tab. The schema passes and Save is enabled. The insert hits `products_title_check`, 23514, and the form shows «تحقق من القيم.» without naming the title.
fix: In the text/textarea/slug case add a refine that rejects /[\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]/ (the same test as commerce-settings.ts) when `nonBlank` is set, or for all catalog text fields, with a field-named message.

title: Checkout name is not checked for control characters that checkout_create refuses, so the buyer gets a fieldless error
content: `checkout_create` rejects a name that contains `[[:cntrl:]]` as INVALID_CONTACT, and the same check guards `customers.name`. The zod `name` only trims and bounds the length, and CheckoutForm only checks that it is not blank. The refusal therefore comes from SQL as 422 INVALID_CONTACT, which the client shows as the top-level 'تحقق من بيانات التواصل.' instead of marking the name field (the S06.6 mapping only handles zod `fieldErrors`). The Turnstile token was already spent when this happens.
failure_scenario: A buyer pastes a name copied from a document with an embedded tab, for example `محمد\tالقرني`. Client and zod accept it; `checkout_create` returns INVALID_CONTACT; the page shows 'تحقق من بيانات التواصل.' under the submit button with no field marked and focus not moved, and the buyer needs a new Turnstile pass to retry.
fix: Add `.refine((v) => !/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]/.test(v), { message: 'الاسم فيه رموز غير مقبولة.' })` to `name` so it comes back as `fieldErrors.name`, which CheckoutForm already maps.

title: A coupon over 64 characters makes every quote fail; after a reload checkout shows only a retry button that can never succeed
content: Neither coupon input has a `maxLength` (CartView.tsx:272 and CheckoutForm.tsx:484), while the function's quote and create schemas cap `couponCode` at 64 (checkout.ts:46, :66). An over-long code gets 422 INVALID for the whole quote. `fetchQuote` throws with that message, and both callers discard it and show 'تعذّر تحديث الأسعار؛ أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات.' The code is stored in sessionStorage (COUPON_KEY) and restored on load. In CheckoutForm, with `quote === null` the only output is the retry screen below, which has no coupon input, so retrying resends the same code (S14.3's retry fix does not help here). The way out is to go to /cart and clear the code there. Same class, smaller: the email input has no `maxLength` against `.max(254)` and the phone input none against `.max(64)`, and the function's default English zod message is mapped verbatim under the field (line 314).
failure_scenario: Buyer pastes a 70-character string into «كود الخصم» on /cart or /checkout and presses «تطبيق». The quote returns 422 and the page says prices could not be refreshed, try again. The buyer reloads /checkout: the stored code is restored, the quote fails again with no quote to render, and the page shows only «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» and «أعد المحاولة». No coupon field is available and retrying never works.
fix: Add `maxLength={32}` to both coupon inputs (the DB code cap). In CheckoutForm, render the coupon field (or a «إزالة الكود» action) in the failed-quote state, or drop a stored coupon when a quote with it fails with 422. Add `maxLength={254}` to email.

title: Journal post slug has no length cap or first-character rule, unlike every other slug
content: Products, taxonomies and `content_versions.doc_id` use `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79}$`. The `slug` field type without a `pattern` falls back to `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, and `postFields` declares no `pattern`. Nothing in SQL bounds `published_documents.data->>'slug'` beyond the unique index, which fails only near 2.7 KB. The slug is used as the static route segment in `journal/[slug]`.
quote: const slugSchema = z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, { message: 'يجب أن يتكوّن من حروف لاتينية صغيرة وأرقام وشرطات.' })
failure_scenario: An editor saves a post whose slug is 300 characters (or `-x`). The schema accepts it, publish succeeds (the index accepts it), and the rebuild has to write `journal/<300 chars>` to the export, a path segment over the 255-byte filesystem limit, so the build fails. The last good deployment stays live and the post never appears, with nothing in the admin saying why. At 3,000 characters the unique index itself raises 54000 and Publish shows only «تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.».
fix: Give posts the same rule: `pattern: { regex: /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79}$/, message: ... }` on the `slug` field in posts.ts (and make that the default slug rule).

title: Schedule: no future-time check, and a 5-digit year throws inside run() and leaves every publish button disabled
content: Two boundary gaps at one site. (1) The datetime-local input has no `min` and there is no client check that the time is in the future, while `schedule_version` raises 22023 for `p_at <= now()` and `admin-publish.ts:32` maps every 22023 to 'قيمة غير صالحة لهذا الإجراء.', which does not say the time must be in the future. (2) `riyadhLocalToIso` throws RangeError for years above 9999 (checked: `20265-10-01T10:00` and `275760-09-13T00:00` both throw), and Chrome and Firefox let the year be typed with up to 6 digits. The call sits inside the `task` arrow evaluated by `run` after `setBusy(true)`, so the exception skips `setBusy(false)`. The same throw happens in the coupon datetime field's onChange (FieldInput.tsx:520), where the typed date is silently dropped.
failure_scenario: An editor types the year as 20265 (one extra digit) and presses «جدولة». `riyadhLocalToIso` throws, `run` rejects unhandled, `busy` stays true, so نشر, أرشفة, جدولة and إلغاء الجدولة all stay disabled with no message until the page is reloaded. Separately, an editor who picks yesterday's time gets «جدولة: قيمة غير صالحة لهذا الإجراء.» and no hint about the cause.
fix: Set `min` on the input to the current Riyadh time, check `new Date(riyadhLocalToIso(v)) > new Date()` and the year range before calling, wrap the task in try/finally (or move `setBusy(false)` into a finally in `run`), and map 22023 from schedule_version to 'يجب أن يكون موعد الجدولة في المستقبل.'.

title: Folder rename checks only the new prefix, but the SQL check applies to every child path
content: `media_rename_folder` sets `folder = p_to || substr(folder, char_length(p_from)+1)` for the folder and all its descendants, and the `media` table requires `char_length(folder) <= 120` on each row. `folderIsInvalid(to)` validates the new name alone. The function is one statement, so one overlong child path fails the whole rename with 23514, and the client shows only 'تعذّرت إعادة تسمية المجلد.'.
failure_scenario: Folder «أ» has a child path of 100 characters (`أ/…`, 102 characters in total). The owner renames «أ» to a 40-character name. `to` passes, but the child becomes 141 characters, so the statement is rejected and nothing moves. The owner sees only «تعذّرت إعادة تسمية المجلد.» and cannot tell that a nested folder is too long.
fix: Before calling the RPC, compute `movedFolder(f, renameFrom, to)` for each loaded folder and refuse with a specific message if any result fails `folderIsInvalid` (the folder list is already loaded, S09.11).

title: Content schemas accept blank nav labels/hrefs, taxonomy labels and post titles, and publish them
content: S11.3 added `nonBlank` to the catalog fields, but the content collections kept plain `z.string()`: nav `label` and `href` (here), taxonomies `label` (taxonomies.ts:15), posts `title` (posts.ts:9). Only scenes captions and social links have a publish rule. `validateVersion` passes whatever the schema passes, and the public loaders parse with the same schema, so nothing stops a blank value from going live.
failure_scenario: An editor adds a nav item and saves it with an empty label and href (the default for a new list item is ''). Publish is enabled and succeeds; SiteHeader renders `<Link href="">` with no text, an unnamed link in the main navigation (WCAG 2.4.4 / 4.1.2). A taxonomy with an empty label renders an empty category chip, and a post with an empty title publishes an empty h1.
fix: Add `nonBlank: true` to nav label and href, taxonomy label and post title (the field option already exists), so publish is blocked with a field-named message.

title: archive_document never received the per-document advisory lock, so a racing schedule or first publish survives the archive
content: AUDIT-1 X2.3 added pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('content:...')) to publish_version, schedule_version and cancel_schedule (audit_fixes.sql:177, 203, 232). archive_document is defined only here and in 20260925120000, and no later migration redefines it, so it takes no lock. Its DELETE and its `update content_versions set publish_at = null ... where publish_at is not null` run under READ COMMITTED with no serialization against schedule_version or publish_version. A row inserted or updated by an uncommitted transaction is invisible to them and they do not wait on it. No test runs archive_document against another session (publish.test.ts:141-175 is sequential).
quote: delete from public.published_documents where collection = p_collection and doc_id = p_doc_id;
failure_scenario:
Scenario 1, the archived post comes back. posts/x is live and its latest seq 4 is unscheduled.
T_s (editor A schedule_version(posts,x,4,'10:00')): takes the advisory lock and runs UPDATE content_versions SET publish_at='10:00' WHERE seq=4, uncommitted.
T_a (editor B archive_document(posts,x)): takes no lock, so it does not wait. DELETE published_documents(x) succeeds. Its UPDATE ... SET publish_at=null WHERE publish_at IS NOT NULL sees seq 4 with publish_at NULL (T_s is uncommitted), matches 0 rows and does not block. It writes the audit row, calls site_build_request and COMMITs.
T_s COMMITs.
Result: no live row, but content_versions(x,4).publish_at='10:00'. At 10:00 publish_due calls content_go_live, which re-inserts published_documents(x), and the archived post is public again with a rebuild requested. The audit trail shows content.archive followed by content.publish_due.
Scenario 2, a first publish survives the archive. posts/y was never live. T_p (publish_version) inserts published_documents(y), uncommitted. T_a (archive_document) DELETEs, sees no row and does not wait. Both commit: y is live although the archive reported success.

title: The S04.4 early-event fix misses a delivery or bounce event committed by a webhook transaction that overlaps the accept
content: outbox_result's accepted branch reads email_delivery_events inside the UPDATE, which uses the statement snapshot taken when that UPDATE starts. email_event_record inserts the event and then runs its own UPDATE ... WHERE o.provider_id = p_provider_message_id (20260926120000:433-441) under a separate snapshot. The fix works only when the event has committed before the accept's UPDATE starts. When the two transactions overlap, neither statement sees the other's change: the webhook UPDATE finds provider_id still NULL and locks nothing, and the accept's subquery does not see the uncommitted event. Both commit and the event is applied to no row. No test runs the two concurrently (outbox.test.ts:355-388 inserts the events first). The window is milliseconds; I did not find a bigger one.
failure_scenario:
Row R is 'sending', lease L.
T_r (outbox_result(R, L, 'accepted', 'msg-1')): holds the row lock and starts UPDATE ... SET provider_id='msg-1', delivery=(SELECT ... FROM email_delivery_events WHERE provider_message_id='msg-1'); snapshot S_r has no event.
T_w (webhook email_event_record for 'email.bounced', msg-1): INSERTs the event, then starts UPDATE outbox WHERE provider_id='msg-1'. Its snapshot still sees provider_id NULL (T_r uncommitted), so 0 rows match and there is no wait. T_w COMMITs; the recipient is suppressed.
T_r finishes: the subquery used S_r, so delivery stays NULL. T_r COMMITs.
Result: R is status 'sent', delivery NULL, although a bounce event is stored. outbox_attention lists only rows with status in exhausted/uncertain/suppressed or delivery in bounced/complained/failed, so the bounce never reaches the owner's attention list.

title: Saving image details reports success when the row was deleted or RLS no longer lets the caller update it
content: The metadata save is a Data API UPDATE ... WHERE id with no .select() and no row-count check. A PATCH that matches zero rows (the row was removed by media_delete, or media_staff_update's current_staff_role() check now fails because the member was deactivated or demoted) answers 204 with no error. The code treats error == null as success, shows 'حُفظ' and patches local state. A deleted image or a revoked editor therefore sees a saved confirmation for a write that never happened, until the reloadToken refetch drops the row. media_delete's row lock serializes correctly with the update; the defect is what the client does with a zero-row outcome. No test covers the race.
failure_scenario: Editor A opens image M's details form. Owner B deletes M through the admin function (media_delete: row locked, usage check passes, row deleted, committed). A edits the alt text and clicks save: UPDATE media SET alt_ar=... WHERE id=M matches 0 rows, PostgREST answers 204 with no error, and the UI shows 'حُفظ' and updates the local copy. Nothing was stored. The same happens when A was deactivated between opening the form and saving, because the RLS policy filters the row.

title: publish_due and publish_version/archive_document take the same two locks in opposite order and deadlock on one document
content: publish_due takes FOR UPDATE on the due content_versions row first (line 261), then content_go_live upserts published_documents (20260925120000:147-150). publish_version takes the advisory lock, then content_go_live upserts published_documents, then clears publish_at on content_versions (20260925120000:151-153), so it locks published_documents first and content_versions second. publish_due does not take the advisory lock, so the per-document serialization AUDIT-1 added for X2.3 does not cover it. The published_documents to content_versions foreign key adds a KEY SHARE on the scheduled row, which conflicts with publish_due's FOR UPDATE. archive_document has the same order (delete published_documents, then update content_versions). publish_due's `exception when others` catches the 40P01, so a victim publish_due row is silently unscheduled. No integration test runs publish_due against a second session: audit-fixes.test.ts and static-site.test.ts call it inside one rolled-back transaction, and publish.test.ts has no concurrent calls. A stale scheduled seq going live over a newer manual publish does not persist: publish_version's clear of publish_at either waits behind publish_due's row lock or makes publish_due skip the row. The interleaving below is the only bad outcome found.
failure_scenario:
posts/x has seq 3 scheduled for 10:00:00 and latest seq 4; it is live at seq 2.
10:00:00.000 T2 (cron publish_due): fetches content_versions(x,3) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so T2 holds V(x,3).
10:00:00.002 T1 (editor publish_version(posts,x,4)): takes the advisory lock, passes the stale check, content_go_live runs INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on published_documents(x), so T1 holds P(x).
10:00:00.003 T1: UPDATE content_versions SET publish_at=null WHERE ... publish_at IS NOT NULL, which waits for V(x,3) held by T2.
10:00:00.003 T2: content_go_live(x,3) upserts published_documents(x), which waits for P(x) held by T1.
Cycle T1 -> T2 -> T1. After deadlock_timeout (1 s) Postgres aborts one with 40P01.
Outcome (a), T1 aborted: the editor's publish of seq 4 fails with the generic 'تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.' while T2 commits seq 3 live, which is older than the seq 4 the editor meant to publish. The editor must retry.
Outcome (b), T2's subtransaction aborted: the handler clears publish_at on seq 3 and writes content.publish_due_failed {seq:3, sqlstate:'40P01'}. The failure audit row blames a slug or content error that never happened.
Swap T1 for archive_document(posts,x) (DELETE published_documents(x), then UPDATE content_versions) and the same cycle forms.

title: Policy approval can record a seq that is already being replaced; the reset trigger misses it because it only bites when the key is already approved
content: commerce_policies_approve locks the settings row and then reads the live seqs with plain SELECTs, taking no lock on published_documents. The X1.1 fix (policies_reset_approval, audit_fixes.sql:119-152) resets the approval from an AFTER ROW trigger on published_documents, and its UPDATE matches only when `policy_revisions ? v_doc`. When policy_revisions is '{}' (after an earlier reset, or before the first approval) a publish in flight has a trigger UPDATE that matches nothing and locks nothing, so the approval and the publish do not serialize. When the key is already approved the trigger locks the settings row and the approve call fails with 40001, so that order is safe; the hole is only the unapproved state, which is the normal state during approval. publish_due widens the window, because it runs the trigger early and commits only after the whole loop. No test runs approval against a concurrent publish (audit-fixes.test.ts:239-290 is sequential and rolled back).
quote: select seq into v_store from public.published_documents where collection = 'policies' and doc_id = 'store';
failure_scenario:
State: commerce_settings.policy_revisions = '{}' (reset by an earlier publish), version N. policies/refund is live at seq 3, and the editor holds seq 4.
T_p (editor publish_version(policies,refund,4)): upserts published_documents(refund)=4. The AFTER ROW trigger runs UPDATE commerce_settings ... WHERE policy_revisions ? 'refund'. No key is present, so 0 rows match, no lock is taken and no reset happens. T_p carries on (audit insert, site_build_request) but has not committed.
T_a (owner commerce_policies_approve): SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the settings row succeeds, the version check passes, and SELECT seq FROM published_documents WHERE doc_id='refund' returns 3 because T_p is uncommitted. It writes policy_revisions {store:s, delivery:d, refund:3}, version N+1, and COMMITs.
T_p COMMITs.
Result: live refund policy is seq 4 but the approved revision is 3, and the trigger already ran so nothing resets it. checkout_quote returns policyRevisions refund:3 and checkout_create accepts it. Orders snapshot refund:3 while the rebuilt site shows the text of seq 4, which is the exact mismatch X1.1 set out to prevent. It persists until the next policy publish.
